sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(n),2) AS avg_pit_stops_per_race FROM (SELECT r.raceId, COUNT(ps.stop) AS n FROM races r LEFT JOIN pitStops ps ON ps.raceId=r.raceId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name NOT IN (SELECT name FROM races WHERE year=2000) GROUP BY r.raceId)
answer: The average is 39.71 pit stops per race, across 7 races from 2017. I treated "not hosted in 2000" as meaning the Grand Prix name did not appear in the 2000 calendar. All 7 races are counted, including any with no recorded pit stops.

sql: SELECT p.ID FROM Patient p WHERE p.Admission='-' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND (l.RBC<=3.5 OR l.RBC>=6.0)) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND l.RNP<>'negative' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>0)
answer: Four outpatient patients qualify: 1180510, 4471732, 4840422 and 4915498. A patient qualifies if any lab row has RBC <= 3.5 or >= 6.0 and any lab row (not necessarily the same one) has a numeric RNP above 0. Rows with RNP 'negative' or null are ignored.

sql: SELECT ROUND((MAX(CASE WHEN r.raceId=853 THEN CAST(r.fastestLapSpeed AS REAL) END) - MAX(CASE WHEN r.raceId=854 THEN CAST(r.fastestLapSpeed AS REAL) END)) * 100.0 / MAX(CASE WHEN r.raceId=854 THEN CAST(r.fastestLapSpeed AS REAL) END), 2) AS pct FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=r.driverId WHERE d.forename='Paul' AND d.surname='di Resta' AND r.raceId IN (853,854)
answer: Paul di Resta's fastest-lap speed in race 853 was 48.15% higher than in race 854, which is the baseline. I read "fastest-lap speed" as results.fastestLapSpeed, cast from text to a number. I didn't validate the query with validate_sql before running it. It relies on the Driver and Race Result terms, which are still draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN Tags LIKE '%<r>%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS percentage FROM posts WHERE OwnerUserId = (SELECT Id FROM users WHERE DisplayName = 'Community')
answer: 0.0 (0.00%). I read "Community" as the user with DisplayName 'Community' (Id -1) and the R tag as the exact `<r>` tag. That user owns 211 posts, and none of them has a tag. Tags is null on all 211 posts, so none carries the R tag.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.Street FROM frpm f JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode WHERE f."Low Grade" IN ('9','10','11','12') AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 30 ORDER BY s.CDSCode
answer:
이 쿼리는 K-12 등록 인원이 5-17세 등록 인원보다 30명 넘게 많고, 같은 frpm 레코드의 Low Grade가 9, 10, 11, 12 중 하나인 학교를 CDS 코드 오름차순으로 보여 줍니다. 결과는 학교 이름과 주소 두 열이고, 첫 행은 Alameda High(2201 Encinal Avenue)입니다. 전체 행 수는 세지 않았습니다.

선택한 해석은 두 가지입니다. 첫째, 주소는 우편 주소(MailStreet)가 아니라 학교가 있는 도로명 주소(Street)로 봤습니다. 둘째, 'Adult'는 학년이 아니므로 9학년 이상에 넣지 않았습니다. K와 P는 9학년보다 앞이라 제외했습니다.

두 등록 인원 중 하나라도 비어 있는 학교는 차이를 계산할 수 없어 결과에서 빠집니다.

sql: SELECT m.molecule_id, CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 'YES' ELSE 'NO' END AS carcinogenic, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type <> '-') AS multiple_bonds FROM atom a JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id WHERE a.atom_id = 'TR041_10'
answer: Atom TR041_10 belongs to molecule TR041. It is carcinogenic (YES) and has 5 multiple bonds. I counted a multiple bond as any bond whose type is not '-', which means double ('=') and triple ('#') bonds, and I counted each bond once from the bond table. The ontology terms Atom, Bond and Molecule are still drafts and haven't been certified.

sql: SELECT e.Symptoms, p.Diagnosis FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=e.ID WHERE (',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(e.Diagnosis,' ',''),'+',',') || ',') LIKE '%,SLE,%' AND e.Symptoms IS NOT NULL AND p.Birthday IS NOT NULL ORDER BY p.Birthday DESC, p.ID ASC, e.`Examination Date` DESC LIMIT 1
answer: 가장 어린 환자의 해당 검사 증상은 "CNS susp"이고, 환자 전체 진단은 "SLE"입니다. 해석 기준: 검사 진단을 쉼표와 '+'로 나눠 'SLE'가 단독 항목으로 있는 경우만 SLE로 보았습니다. 그래서 "SLE susp"(의심)와 "JRA->SLE"는 제외했습니다. 가장 어린 환자는 생년월일이 가장 늦은 환자이며, 같으면 환자 ID가 작은 쪽, 해당 환자의 검사가 여러 건이면 가장 최근 검사를 사용했습니다.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT e.type AS event_type, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS members FROM event AS e INNER JOIN attendance AS a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND e.event_date < '2020-06-01' GROUP BY e.type) SELECT event_type, members FROM t WHERE members = (SELECT MAX(members) FROM t)
answer: Meeting and Registration tie, with 30 distinct members each. I counted each member once per event type, however many events of that type they attended. The date filter covers September 1, 2019 through May 31, 2020, which is all events in the data. The Event term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT d.A2 AS district, CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) AS inhabitants FROM district AS d WHERE d.district_id IN (SELECT a.district_id FROM account AS a WHERE a.date >= '1993-01-01' AND a.date < '1993-02-01') AND CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(d2.A4 AS INTEGER)) FROM district AS d2 WHERE d2.district_id IN (SELECT a2.district_id FROM account AS a2 WHERE a2.date >= '1993-01-01' AND a2.date < '1993-02-01'))
answer:
Hl.m. Praha (Prague) has the largest population among the districts that opened an account in the first month. It has 1,204,953 inhabitants, and no other district ties with it.

I read "first month of operations" as January 1993, because the earliest account date in the data is 1993-01-01. I used the account's branch district (account.district_id), not the client's home district. The Account and District terms are still draft (not certified).

sql: SELECT s.School, s.Street FROM frpm f JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode WHERE s.School IS NOT NULL AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 30 AND f."High Grade" IN ('K','1','2','3','4','5','6','7','8')
answer: The query returns 121 schools. I read "highest grade of enrollment" as frpm."High Grade", the grade span in the same FRPM report as the enrollment counts. 'K', '1' through '8' qualify, and 'P', 'Adult' and grades 9 and above do not. "Named school" means schools.School is not null. The street address is schools.Street. The comparison is K-12 enrollment minus ages 5-17 enrollment greater than 30, and rows where either figure is null drop out. Using schools.GSserved for the highest grade instead gives 120 schools, so the two readings differ by about one school.

sql: SELECT SUM(SEX='F') - SUM(SEX='M') AS diff FROM Patient p WHERE Diagnosis='RA' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.UN<30)
answer: 23. There are 30 women and 7 men, so 30 − 7 = 23. I read "RA patients" as patients whose Diagnosis is exactly 'RA'. Variants such as 'RA susp' are excluded. I read "normal urea nitrogen" as UN < 30, the normal range in the docs. A patient counts once if any of their lab results has UN below 30.

sql: SELECT c.colour, COUNT(*) AS hero_count, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rnk FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON p.id=s.publisher_id JOIN colour c ON c.id=s.eye_colour_id WHERE p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' AND c.colour<>'No Colour' GROUP BY c.colour ORDER BY hero_count DESC, c.colour
answer: Blue is the most common eye colour among Marvel Comics heroes with 126, then Brown (89), Green (40), Red (31), Yellow (13), White (12) and Black (11). The query returns 18 colours in total. I treated the 'No Colour' value as an unknown eye colour and excluded it, the same way verified query 3 does. Colours with equal counts share a rank (RANK), so Gold and Purple are both 10, and they are listed alphabetically.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.height_cm>0 THEN s.height_cm END),1) AS avg_height_cm, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg>0 THEN s.weight_kg END),1) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id=p.id WHERE p.publisher_name='George Lucas'
answer: George Lucas's heroes (the publisher 'George Lucas', 15 heroes) average 187.2 cm in height and 83.0 kg in weight. I treated "created" as "published by George Lucas". I treated a height or weight of 0 or NULL as unknown and left it out, which matches the earlier verified queries for this database.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT c.circuitRef, r.time FROM races r JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId=r.circuitId WHERE r.time IS NOT NULL AND r.time<>''), b AS (SELECT MIN(time) mn, MAX(time) mx FROM t) SELECT e.circuitRef AS earliest, l.circuitRef AS latest, CAST(strftime('%s','2000-01-01 '||b.mx)-strftime('%s','2000-01-01 '||b.mn) AS INTEGER) AS gap_seconds FROM b JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT circuitRef, time FROM t) e ON e.time=b.mn JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT circuitRef, time FROM t) l ON l.time=b.mx
answer: Earliest start: fuji (04:30:00). Latest start: americas (20:00:00). Gap: 55,800 seconds (15.5 hours). I used races.time (local start time) and skipped races with no recorded time, which is every race before 2005. Each extreme belongs to a single circuit, so there are no ties.

sql: SELECT SUM(c.colour='No Colour') - SUM(c.colour='Blue') FROM superhero s JOIN colour c ON c.id=s.eye_colour_id WHERE s.weight_kg IS NULL OR s.weight_kg=0;
answer: 122. I counted weight as not recorded when weight_kg is NULL or 0, which is how the docs define a missing weight. In that group, 'No Colour' eyes outnumber blue eyes by 122.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE SSA IS NOT NULL AND SSA NOT IN ('negative','0') INTERSECT SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE `U-PRO` IS NOT NULL AND `U-PRO` NOT IN ('-','0'))
answer:
15 patients have both an abnormal anti-SSA result and a positive proteinuria finding, each at any point in their Laboratory records.

I treated anti-SSA as abnormal when the result is not NULL, 'negative' or '0'. I treated proteinuria as positive when the result is not NULL, '-' or '0'. That reading counts a trace ('TR') as positive, because you defined positive as anything other than negative or none. If you would rather not count traces, the number is 12.

sql: SELECT SUM(s.totalSetSize) AS total_cards FROM sets AS s WHERE (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t.translation) FROM set_translations AS t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL) < 5
answer: 45,452 cards across the 504 sets with fewer than five distinct translated names. I used totalSetSize as the full set size, and sets with zero translations are included.

sql: WITH top AS (SELECT l.loan_id, a.district_id FROM loan l JOIN account a ON a.account_id=l.account_id WHERE l.duration=24 AND a.frequency='POPLATEK TYDNE' ORDER BY l.amount DESC, l.loan_id LIMIT 10), ds AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.district_id, d.A2, CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) pop, d.A11 FROM district d WHERE d.district_id IN (SELECT district_id FROM top)) SELECT (SELECT A2 FROM ds ORDER BY pop DESC, district_id LIMIT 1) AS most_populous_district, (SELECT pop FROM ds ORDER BY pop DESC, district_id LIMIT 1) AS inhabitants, (SELECT ROUND(AVG(A11),2) FROM ds) AS avg_salary
answer: 가장 인구가 많은 지역은 Karvina(주민 285,387명)이고, 해당 지역들의 평균 급여는 8985.75입니다. 대상은 주간 명세서(POPLATEK TYDNE) 계좌의 24개월 대출 중 승인 금액 상위 10건이며, 동일 금액이 없어 순위 동점 처리는 필요하지 않았습니다. 10건은 서로 다른 8개 지역에서 나왔습니다(19번과 31번 지역이 각각 2건). 평균 급여는 대출 건수가 아니라 이 8개 지역을 한 번씩만 세어 계산했습니다. 지역은 계좌를 관리하는 지점의 지역(account.district_id) 기준입니다.

sql: SELECT AVG(HCT) FROM Laboratory WHERE Date LIKE '1991%' AND "U-PRO" IN ('300', '>=300') AND HCT IS NOT NULL
answer: The average hematocrit is 41.6, across 5 tests from 1991 with proteinuria of at least 300 mg/dL. I counted both the exact '300' results and the lower-bound '>=300' result. The other recorded values in 1991 are below 300: '100', '30', 'TR' (trace) and '-'. No other lower-bound forms such as '>300' appear. Tests with no hematocrit reading are excluded from the average.

sql: WITH q AS (SELECT DISTINCT ds.raceId FROM driverStandings ds JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = ds.driverId WHERE d.nationality = 'Australian' AND ds.position < 20) SELECT r.year AS season, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pitStops p WHERE p.raceId IN (SELECT q.raceId FROM q JOIN races r2 ON r2.raceId = q.raceId WHERE r2.year = r.year)) AS total_pit_stops FROM (SELECT DISTINCT year FROM races WHERE year BETWEEN 2002 AND 2013) r ORDER BY r.year
answer: Pit stop totals were 1069 in 2011, 905 in 2012 and 898 in 2013. The seasons 2002 to 2010 show 0 because the database has no pit stop records before 2011. I read "better than 20th" as a standings position below 20, meaning 19th or higher. I took "after the race" to mean the driver standings recorded for that race. The totals count the pit stops of every driver at each qualifying race, not only the Australians.

sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(i.amount), 0) AS total_dues FROM income AS i WHERE i.source = 'Dues' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attendance AS a JOIN event AS e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event WHERE a.link_to_member = i.link_to_member AND e.event_name = 'Football game')
answer:
Membership dues collected from students who attended the Football game total $1,100.

I read "from the students" as income rows with source 'Dues' whose recording member (income.link_to_member) attended the event named 'Football game'. The database has no separate payer field, so that member is the closest link between a payment and a student. The EXISTS check counts each payment once, even if a member appears in attendance more than once. The Income and Event terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(c), 2) AS avg_languages FROM (SELECT s.code, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t.language) FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(t.translation) <> '') AS c FROM sets s WHERE s.releaseDate >= '2016-01-01' AND s.releaseDate <= '2016-12-31')
answer: 4.74. This is the average over the 23 sets released in 2016. Sets with no translations count as 0. A language counts for a set only when its translation row has a non-NULL, non-empty name, because 231 of the 1,210 translation rows have a NULL name.

sql:
WITH w AS (SELECT a.district_id, SUM(t.amount) AS tot FROM trans t JOIN account a ON a.account_id=t.account_id WHERE t.type='VYDAJ' GROUP BY a.district_id),
o AS (SELECT a.district_id, SUM(od.amount) AS so FROM "order" od JOIN account a ON a.account_id=od.account_id GROUP BY a.district_id),
n AS (SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS accts FROM account GROUP BY district_id),
b AS (SELECT d.A2 AS district_name, d.A3 AS region, CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) AS population, w.tot AS total_withdrawn, ROUND(w.tot*1.0/CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER),2) AS wpi, ROUND(COALESCE(o.so,0)*1.0/n.accts,2) AS avg_so
FROM district d JOIN w ON w.district_id=d.district_id LEFT JOIN o ON o.district_id=d.district_id JOIN n ON n.district_id=d.district_id WHERE CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER)>=100000)
SELECT district_name, region, population, total_withdrawn, wpi AS withdrawals_per_inhabitant, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY wpi DESC) AS rank_by_withdrawals_per_inhabitant, avg_so AS avg_standing_order_debit_per_account FROM b ORDER BY rank_by_withdrawals_per_inhabitant, district_name
answer: 46 districts qualify (population >= 100,000 with withdrawals), all ranked using RANK() (ties share a rank, next skipped; no ties occurred). Withdrawals = debit transactions (type 'VYDAJ'), assigned to the account's branch district over the full history. Rank is based on the per-inhabitant value rounded to 2 decimals. Average standing-order debit = total `order` amounts in the district / all accounts in the district (accounts without orders count as zero). Top: Usti nad Orlici (343.79 per inhabitant, rank 1, avg standing order 5,298.02); bottom: Ceske Budejovice (134.64, rank 46, 3,966.25). Ontology Terms used are still drafts (uncertified).

sql: SELECT p.ID, p.Diagnosis, l.DNA FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE instr(',' || REPLACE(p.Diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',', ',SLE,') > 0 AND l.DNA IS NOT NULL AND CAST(l.DNA AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(l2.DNA AS REAL)) FROM Laboratory l2 JOIN Patient p2 ON p2.ID = l2.ID WHERE instr(',' || REPLACE(p2.Diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',', ',SLE,') > 0 AND l2.DNA IS NOT NULL) GROUP BY p.ID, p.Diagnosis, l.DNA ORDER BY p.ID
answer: Patient 2933261, diagnosis "SLE", highest anti-DNA result "185" (no ties). Reading chosen: SLE means the Diagnosis list includes SLE (combined diagnoses such as "SLE, SJS" count; "SLE susp" does not). DNA is stored as text, so values were compared numerically and returned as written. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
SELECT e.Symptoms, p.Diagnosis
FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=e.ID
WHERE instr(',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(e.Diagnosis,' ',''),CHAR(29),',') || ',', ',SLE,') > 0
  AND e.Symptoms IS NOT NULL AND p.Birthday IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY p.Birthday DESC, p.ID ASC, e."Examination Date" DESC
LIMIT 1;
answer: 가장 어린 환자의 검사 기록 증상은 'CNS lupus'이고, 환자의 전체 진단(Patient.Diagnosis)은 'SLE'입니다. 해석 기준은 두 가지입니다. 첫째, 검사 진단에 SLE가 하나의 항목으로 들어 있으면 SLE로 보았고 'SLE susp'(의심)만 있는 경우는 제외했습니다. 둘째, 가장 어린 환자는 생일이 가장 늦은 환자로 정했고, 생일이 같으면 ID가 작은 환자, 해당 검사가 여러 건이면 가장 최근 검사를 골랐습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.molecule_id) FROM atom a WHERE a.element='n' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM atom n JOIN connected c ON (c.atom_id=n.atom_id OR c.atom_id2=n.atom_id) JOIN bond b ON b.bond_id=c.bond_id WHERE n.molecule_id=a.molecule_id AND n.element='n' AND b.bond_type IN ('=','#'))
answer: 110 molecules contain nitrogen and have no nitrogen atom in a double ('=') or triple ('#') bond. Of the 187 molecules with any nitrogen, 77 are excluded. Nitrogen bonds were found through the connected table in either atom direction. Bond types are '-' for single, '=' for double and '#' for triple.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE duelDeck='b' AND hasFoil=0 AND power GLOB '[0-9]*' AND CAST(power AS INTEGER) < 3
answer: 213 cards in duel deck B are not available in foil and have a power below 3. That is 13 with power 0, 74 with power 1 and 126 with power 2. I left out cards whose power is null (non-creatures) or '*', because the docs treat both as unknown power rather than a number below 3.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) AS power_count FROM hero_power hp JOIN superhero s ON s.id = hp.hero_id JOIN gender g ON g.id = s.gender_id WHERE g.gender = 'Male' AND s.weight_kg > 0 AND s.weight_kg < 70
answer: 102 different superpowers are held by at least one male hero under 70 kg. The docs say a weight_kg of NULL or 0 means the weight is missing, and 172 heroes have 0. I excluded both, so only weights above 0 and below 70 count.

sql:
WITH RECURSIVE ex AS (SELECT expense_id, link_to_member, cost, expense_description AS d FROM expense WHERE expense_date >= '2019-10-01' AND expense_date < '2019-12-01'),
split(expense_id, member, item, rest) AS (SELECT expense_id, link_to_member, '', d || ',' FROM ex UNION ALL SELECT expense_id, member, LOWER(TRIM(SUBSTR(rest, 1, INSTR(rest, ',') - 1))), SUBSTR(rest, INSTR(rest, ',') + 1) FROM split WHERE rest <> ''),
kinds AS (SELECT member, COUNT(DISTINCT item) AS k FROM split WHERE item <> '' GROUP BY member),
spend AS (SELECT link_to_member AS member, SUM(cost) AS s FROM ex GROUP BY link_to_member)
SELECT m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS full_name, kinds.k AS kinds_bought, ROUND(spend.s, 2) AS total_spending
FROM kinds JOIN spend USING (member) JOIN member m ON m.member_id = kinds.member
WHERE kinds.k = (SELECT MAX(k) FROM kinds) ORDER BY full_name
answer:
Sacha Harrison bought the most kinds of items in October and November 2019: 7 kinds, with total spending of $407.90 over those two months. No other member tied.

Readings I chose:
- The period is expense dates from 2019-10-01 through 2019-11-30.
- A purchase description can list several items separated by commas, so I split each description into items. A kind is a distinct item name, compared case-insensitively with spaces trimmed.
- Total spending is the sum of the cost of all that member's expenses in the period.

sql: WITH g AS (SELECT c.watermark AS guild, COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) AS n FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid=c.uuid WHERE c.watermark IN ('azorius','boros','dimir','golgari','gruul','izzet','orzhov','rakdos','selesnya','simic') GROUP BY c.watermark) SELECT guild, n AS number_of_cards FROM g WHERE n=(SELECT MAX(n) FROM g)
answer: Golgari has the most cards printed in another language, with 148 cards. There is no tie. I counted distinct card printings (uuid) that have at least one row in foreign_data, and the watermark values are stored in lowercase.

sql:
WITH last AS (
  SELECT p.Admission AS adm,
    (SELECT l.IGG FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.IGG IS NOT NULL ORDER BY l.Date DESC LIMIT 1) AS igg
  FROM Patient p WHERE p.Admission IN ('+','-')
)
SELECT CASE adm WHEN '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS setting,
  ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN igg > 900 AND igg < 2000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) AS pct_normal_igg
FROM last GROUP BY adm ORDER BY adm ASC;
answer:
입원 환자('admitted to the hospital')의 15.8%, 외래 추적 환자('followed at the outpatient clinic')의 13.6%가 가장 최근 IgG 측정값이 정상이었습니다.

적용한 기준은 다음과 같습니다.
- 입원은 Admission가 '+', 외래는 '-'인 환자입니다. 값이 비어 있는 34명과 형식이 잘못된 '+(' 3명은 어느 쪽에도 넣지 않았습니다.
- 가장 최근 IgG는 IGG가 NULL이 아닌 검사 중 날짜가 가장 늦은 값입니다.
- IgG 검사 기록이 없는 환자는 분모에는 포함하고 분자에서는 제외했습니다.
- 정상 범위는 docs의 900 < IgG < 2000(경계값 제외)입니다. 경계값인 900이나 2000인 검사는 전체 2건이고, 이 값들이 최근 측정값인지는 확인하지 않았습니다. 포함 기준으로 바꾸면 결과가 달라질 수 있습니다.

sql: WITH l AS (SELECT a.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) rn FROM Player_Attributes a) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM l JOIN Player p ON p.player_api_id = l.player_api_id WHERE l.rn = 1 AND p.height > 180 AND l.volleys > 70
answer: 416 players are taller than 180 cm and have a volleys score above 70 on their latest rating record. The latest record is the one with the latest date, and the highest id breaks ties on that date. Height is strictly above 180 cm and volleys strictly above 70. I did not drop empty latest records: their volleys are null, so they never pass the filter.

sql: SELECT (SELECT AVG(ball_control) FROM Player_Attributes WHERE player_api_id = (SELECT player_api_id FROM Player WHERE player_name='Abdou Diallo')) - (SELECT AVG(ball_control) FROM Player_Attributes WHERE player_api_id = (SELECT player_api_id FROM Player WHERE player_name='Aaron Appindangoye')) AS diff
answer: Abdou Diallo's mean ball_control is 0.8 points higher than Aaron Appindangoye's (the raw result is 0.7999999999999). I averaged over all of each player's snapshot rows in Player_Attributes: 10 rows for Diallo and 5 for Appindangoye, with no null ball_control values.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(Admission='+')/COUNT(*),2) AS percentage FROM Patient p WHERE STRFTIME('%Y',Birthday) BETWEEN '1930' AND '1940' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID)
answer: 35.9 (14 inpatients out of 39 patients born 1930–1940 with at least one lab test, i.e. 35.90%). I counted inpatients as Admission = '+', and the denominator includes the 3 patients with a blank Admission value.

sql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN d.dob < '1985-01-01' AND r.laps > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS percentage FROM results r JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId = r.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = r.driverId WHERE ra.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2005
answer: 약 64.88%입니다. 분모는 2000~2005년 전체 레이스 결과(results 행)이고, 분자는 그중 1985-01-01 이전 출생 드라이버가 50바퀴를 넘게 완주한 결과(laps > 50)입니다. 사용한 용어(Driver, Race, Race Result)는 draft 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS neutral_superhero_count FROM superhero s JOIN alignment a ON a.id = s.alignment_id WHERE a.alignment = 'Neutral'
answer: 28 superheroes have the alignment 'Neutral'. I read "neither good nor bad" as the Neutral alignment. The unused 'N/A' alignment has 0 heroes. Another 6 heroes have no alignment recorded (NULL alignment_id). I did not count them, because their alignment is unknown rather than neutral. Counting them would give 34.

sql: SELECT 'Alameda' AS county_name, COUNT(*) AS school_count, ROUND(AVG(ROUND(f."Free Meal Count (K-12)"*100.0/f."Enrollment (K-12)",2)),2) AS avg_free_meal_pct, ROUND(AVG(ROUND(f."FRPM Count (K-12)"*100.0/f."Enrollment (K-12)",2)),2) AS avg_frpm_pct, SUM(CASE WHEN f."Charter School (Y/N)"=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS charter_schools, SUM(CASE WHEN f."Charter School (Y/N)"=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS non_charter_schools, ROUND(AVG(sat.AvgScrRead+sat.AvgScrMath+sat.AvgScrWrite),2) AS avg_sat_score FROM frpm f LEFT JOIN satscores sat ON sat.cds=f.CDSCode AND sat.rtype='S' WHERE f."County Name"=(SELECT "County Name" FROM frpm WHERE CAST(CDSCode AS INTEGER)=1612590125716) AND f."Free Meal Count (K-12)">500 AND f."FRPM Count (K-12)"<700
answer: Fremont High (CDS 1612590125716) is in Alameda County. In Alameda, 13 K-12 schools have more than 500 free meals and fewer than 700 FRPM meals. Their average free-meal percentage is 73.53 and their average FRPM percentage is 80.65 (each school's percentage rounded to 2 decimals before averaging). None of the 13 is a charter school, so all 13 are non-charter, per the frpm charter indicator. The average SAT score (reading + math + writing) is 1189, counting only schools with school-level SAT records. Percentages are computed from meal counts / K-12 enrollment * 100, and the Terms used are drafts, not certified.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT DISTINCT CustomerID FROM transactions_1k WHERE Date='2012-08-25' AND Price=634.8) SELECT ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN substr(Date,1,4)='2013' THEN Consumption END)-SUM(CASE WHEN substr(Date,1,4)='2012' THEN Consumption END))/SUM(CASE WHEN substr(Date,1,4)='2012' THEN Consumption END),4) AS relative_change FROM yearmonth WHERE CustomerID IN (SELECT CustomerID FROM c)
answer: 5.8152. 2012-08-25에 634.8을 결제한 고객은 6718번 한 명이고, 이 고객의 연간 소비량은 2012년에서 2013년 사이 약 581.52% 늘었습니다. 결제액은 transactions_1k의 Price 열 값이 634.8인 거래로 해석했습니다. Amount×Price로 계산하면 17139.6이어서 이 값과 맞지 않습니다.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(A11), 2) AS avg_of_avg_salary, COUNT(*) AS district_count
FROM district
WHERE A3 = 'east Bohemia'
  AND district_id IN (
    SELECT a.district_id
    FROM account a
    JOIN disp d ON d.account_id = a.account_id
    JOIN client c ON c.client_id = d.client_id
    WHERE c.birth_date >= '1980-01-01' AND c.birth_date < '1990-01-01'
  )
answer: East Bohemia 지점 지역 10곳이 1980년대생 고객을 한 명 이상 두고 있고, 이 지역들의 평균 급여의 평균은 8618.20입니다. 계좌가 있는 지점의 지역(account.district_id)을 기준으로 했고, 고객의 거주 지역은 쓰지 않았습니다. 계좌 보유는 소유자(OWNER)와 사용자(DISPONENT)를 모두 포함했습니다. 소유자만으로 제한해도 결과는 같았습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.atom_id2) FROM atom a JOIN connected c ON c.atom_id=a.atom_id WHERE a.element='cl';
answer: 271 distinct atoms are directly bonded to a chlorine ('cl') atom across all molecules. I counted distinct neighbor atoms, not bonds, as in the verified sulfur question. The `connected` table stores each bond in both directions, so I started from the chlorine side only. A neighbor that touches two chlorine atoms is counted once.

sql: SELECT c.nationality, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN r.rank = 1 THEN c.constructorId END) AS constructor_count FROM constructors AS c LEFT JOIN results AS r ON r.constructorId = c.constructorId GROUP BY c.nationality ORDER BY constructor_count DESC, c.nationality
answer:
The query returns 24 nationalities. British has 4 constructors with a fastest lap. Italian and German have 2 each. Swiss, Japanese, Indian, French and Austrian have 1 each. The other 16 nationalities have 0, including American, Australian and Brazilian.

I counted a constructor when one of its result rows has rank = 1, which is the officially recorded fastest lap of that race. I did not compute anything from lap times. The rank field is only filled in for 2004 to 2017 races, so constructors whose fastest laps came earlier are counted as 0. Each constructor is counted once per nationality, however many fastest laps it set.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1 AND side IS NOT NULL AND CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER)) FROM cards)
answer: The query returns the distinct names of promotional cards (isPromo = 1) that have multiple faces on one card (side IS NOT NULL) and use the newest frame style across all cards. That style is 2015, because frameVersion cast to a year gives 2015 as the maximum and 'future' casts to 0. The result is truncated here. The run returned its first 100 rows, so I can't give the full count. Examples include "Decorated Knight // Present Arms", "Dusk // Dawn" and "Bonecrusher Giant // Stomp". I took "multiple faces" to mean a non-null side. The Card term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) AS card_count FROM cards c WHERE c.types LIKE '%Creature%' AND CAST(c.power AS INTEGER) >= 10 AND c.setCode IN (SELECT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE language = 'French' AND translation IS NOT NULL AND translation <> '')
answer: 33. I counted distinct creature cards by name, with numeric power of 10 or more. The card had to have a printing in a set that has a French set-name translation in set_translations. I ignored release date and set type. Of the 48 creature cards with power 10 or more, 33 meet the French condition.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT SUM(p.publisher_name='DC Comics') dc, SUM(p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics') m FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON p.id=s.publisher_id) SELECT CASE WHEN dc>m THEN 'DC Comics' WHEN m>dc THEN 'Marvel Comics' ELSE 'Tie' END AS publisher, ABS(dc-m) AS difference FROM c
answer: Marvel Comics has more superheroes, by 163 (387 for Marvel versus 224 for DC Comics). I read "by how many" as the absolute difference between the two counts, and the query returns two columns: publisher and difference.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1 AND originalReleaseDate LIKE '2019/%' AND layout IN ('split','flip','transform','modal_dfc','meld','adventure','aftermath') ORDER BY name
answer: 31개 카드가 해당합니다. 모두 adventure 레이아웃입니다. 2019년에 처음 출시된 프로모 카드 중 다른 다면 레이아웃(split, transform 등)은 없었습니다. 해석은 세 가지로 잡았습니다. 프로모 카드는 isPromo = 1인 카드로 봤습니다. 처음 출시일은 세트 출시일이 아니라 카드의 originalReleaseDate로 판단했고, 이 값이 'YYYY/M/D' 형식이어서 '2019/%'로 걸렀습니다. 다면 카드는 split, flip, transform, modal_dfc, meld, adventure, aftermath 레이아웃으로 봤습니다. 같은 이름은 DISTINCT로 한 번만 나옵니다.

sql: select ROUND(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN ','||REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(Diagnosis,' ',''),'+',','),'->',',')||',' LIKE '%,SLE,%' THEN ID END)/COUNT(DISTINCT ID),2) from Examination where Thrombosis>0 and ID is not null
answer: 57.14%. Of the 7 distinct patients with a thrombosis finding (Thrombosis 1, 2 or 3) at an examination, 4 had SLE in the examination diagnosis (1567380, 2495750, 2803470 "SLE+Psy", 4395720). I used the Examination.Diagnosis column rather than the Patient file. Any exam row with Thrombosis > 0 counts, and a patient counts once. SLE is matched as a whole term, so "SLE+Psy" counts and "SLE susp" is not a case here. I excluded 5 thrombosis exam rows with no patient ID, because they can't be tied to a patient. Two of those mention SLE, so including them would change the figure.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(e)/COUNT(*),2) AS percentage FROM (SELECT p.ID, MAX(CASE WHEN l.RNP<>'negative' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>64 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) e FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE p.SEX='F' AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.ID)
answer: 5.49%. Of 91 women with at least one RNP result, 5 had a titer above 1:64 (only the 1:256 value qualifies). I counted by patient: a woman is elevated if any of her results was above 1:64. Negative results count as available but not elevated, and women never tested are excluded.

sql:
SELECT COALESCE(SUM(m.college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences'), 0) AS humanities_social_sciences_members,
       COUNT(*) - COALESCE(SUM(m.college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences'), 0) AS other_members
FROM member mb
LEFT JOIN major m ON m.major_id = mb.link_to_major;
answer: 7 members major in a department of the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, and 26 do not, which is all 33 members on the roster. One member has no major link, so I counted that member in the "do not" group, since their major cannot be shown to belong to the college. I used the major table's college column to decide which college a major belongs to.

sql: SELECT a.element FROM atom a JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '-' GROUP BY a.element HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MIN(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM atom a2 JOIN molecule m2 ON m2.molecule_id = a2.molecule_id WHERE m2.label = '-' GROUP BY a2.element))
answer: Non-carcinogenic molecules (label '-') contain three elements that each appear once: ca (calcium), k (potassium) and pb (lead). I counted atom rows per element, and elements that never occur in these molecules are not counted. I did not run the final query itself. I ran a grouped count by element, which gave ca, k and pb at 1 each, then sn at 2, i at 3 and br at 4.

sql:
WITH slots AS (
SELECT id, home_player_1 pid FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_2 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_3 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_4 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_5 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_6 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_7 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_8 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_9 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_10 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_11 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016'
UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_1 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_2 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_3 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_4 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_5 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_6 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_7 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_8 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_9 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_10 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_11 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016'),
apps AS (SELECT pid, COUNT(DISTINCT id) n FROM slots WHERE pid IS NOT NULL GROUP BY pid)
SELECT p.player_name, COALESCE(a.n,0) AS matches_played FROM Player p LEFT JOIN apps a ON a.pid=p.player_api_id WHERE p.player_name LIKE 'Adam%' AND p.weight>170 ORDER BY p.player_name, p.player_api_id
answer:
쿼리는 24명을 반환했습니다. 예를 들어 Adam Masina 30경기, Adam Danch 29경기, Adam Marusic 26경기입니다.

적용한 해석은 세 가지입니다.
- 경기 수: 2015/2016 시즌 경기에서 홈 또는 어웨이 선발 11명 슬롯 중 하나에 이름이 오른 경기를 한 경기로 계산했습니다. 한 경기에 한 번만 셉니다. 교체 출전은 데이터에 없어서 포함하지 못했습니다.
- 출전 기록이 없는 선수: 조건에 맞지만 해당 시즌 선발 기록이 없는 선수(Adam Banas 등 9명)는 0경기로 넣었습니다. 제외하려면 apps 조인을 INNER JOIN으로 바꾸면 됩니다.
- 이름 조건: 'Adam'으로 시작하는 이름을 문자 그대로 적용해서 Adama Coulibaly, Adama Francois, Adama Soumaoro, Adamo Coulibaly도 포함됩니다. 이들을 빼려면 조건을 `LIKE 'Adam %'`로 바꾸면 됩니다.

몸무게는 단위 표기 없이 숫자 그대로 170보다 큰 값으로 비교했습니다.

sql: WITH m AS (SELECT p.ID AS ID, MAX(CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)) AS lvl FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE STRFTIME('%Y',p."First Date")='1991' AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.ID) SELECT ID, lvl AS RNP FROM m WHERE lvl=(SELECT MAX(lvl) FROM m) ORDER BY ID
answer: Three patients tie at the highest anti-RNP level of 256: 912147, 4632548 and 4649885. I counted each patient's highest recorded RNP across all their lab dates. Patients with no recorded level were excluded, and 'negative' was treated as 0. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still drafts in the ontology, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.date || '|' || r.text) AS ruling_count FROM rulings r JOIN cards c ON c.uuid = r.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Fireball'
answer: Fireball has 4 distinct official rulings, counted across all dates. The table holds 136 ruling rows for its 36 printings, but those are the same 4 rulings copied onto each printing. If you want the raw row count instead, it is 136.

sql: SELECT SUM(Admission='+') AS inpatients, SUM(Admission='-') AS outpatients, ROUND(100.0*SUM(Admission='+')/COUNT(*),2) AS inpatient_pct FROM Patient WHERE Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' AND Diagnosis NOT LIKE '%SLE susp%' AND Admission IN ('+','-')
answer:
Among confirmed-SLE patients, 164 were inpatients and 113 were outpatients. Inpatients are 59.21% of the 277 patients in those two settings.

Readings I chose:
- **Confirmed SLE:** the profile Diagnosis contains "SLE" but not "SLE susp". Combinations such as "SLE, SJS" and "SLE, APS" count as confirmed. Entries like "SLE susp" and "RA, SLE susp" are excluded. A few entries are ambiguous, such as "SLE  SJS susp" (the "susp" may apply to SJS only). I counted these as confirmed SLE.
- **Care setting:** inpatient means Admission = '+' and outpatient means Admission = '-'. I excluded the 34 blank Admission values and the 3 malformed '+(' values.

sql: SELECT s.NCESSchool FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode WHERE CAST(s.CDSCode AS INTEGER) IN (1751010130583, 1612910137588, 1611760134270) AND f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" = (SELECT MAX(f2."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)") FROM frpm f2 WHERE CAST(f2.CDSCode AS INTEGER) IN (1751010130583, 1612910137588, 1611760134270))
answer:
The school with the highest ages 5-17 enrollment among the three has NCES school ID 09282. Only one school has the top value, so there is no tie. The query would return every tied school if there were one.

I matched the CDS codes as numbers, because they are stored as text and the codes you gave have no leading zero. I took "enrollment of students aged 5-17" to be frpm."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)". The NCES ID comes from schools.NCESSchool, which is text, so the leading zero is kept.

The two terms the query uses, School and Free or Reduced Price Meal Record, are still drafts and have not been certified.

sql: select round(1.0*count(l.loan_id)/count(distinct a.account_id),2) as avg_loans_per_account from account a join disp d on d.account_id=a.account_id and d.type='OWNER' join client c on c.client_id=d.client_id and c.birth_date<'1950-01-01' left join loan l on l.account_id=a.account_id
answer: 0.11. 계정 소유자(disp.type='OWNER')의 생년월일이 1950-01-01 이전인 계정을 대상으로, 대출이 없는 계정도 포함하고 승인 시점과 관계없이 모든 대출을 세어 계정당 평균을 계산했습니다. DISPONENT(권한 사용자)는 소유자로 보지 않았습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.date || '|' || r.text) AS ruling_count FROM rulings r JOIN cards c ON c.uuid = r.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Fireball'
answer: Fireball has 4 distinct official rulings. The database stores rulings per printing, and Fireball has 36 printings, so counting rows gives 136. Those rows repeat the same 4 rulings (same date and text), so I counted each ruling once. If you meant the raw number of ruling rows across all printings, it is 136.

sql: select 100.0*sum(strftime('%Y',Date)='2010')/count(*) - 100.0*sum(strftime('%Y',Date)='2011')/count(*) as diff from badges where Name='Student'
answer: 2010년 점유율에서 2011년 점유율을 뺀 값은 약 -9.54%p입니다. 전체 Student 배지(2010~2014년 합계)를 분모로 계산했습니다. 2010년 542건의 점유율은 약 3.7%이고 2011년 1,959건의 점유율은 약 13.4%입니다. 2011년이 더 높아서 값이 음수로 나옵니다.

sql:
SELECT p.ID,
 CAST(strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',p.Birthday) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09')<strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)) AS INTEGER) AS age
FROM Patient p
WHERE p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE LDH>600 AND LDH<800 AND CAST(REPLACE("U-PRO",'>=','') AS REAL)>=300)
ORDER BY p.ID;
answer: 3 patients qualify: 3182521 (age 73), 4425292 (age 71), 4632548 (age 99). Both findings are required on the same Laboratory row (same ID and Date). LDH is strictly between 600 and 800. Urine protein counts as 300 or more when U-PRO is 300, '>=300' or '>=1000'. I read a plain number as mg/dL, as you specified, so the grade codes '3' and '4' are not treated as 3+/4+ (3 mg/dL is below 300). Age is completed years as of 2026-10-09, computed from Birthday.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.height_cm),1) AS average_height_cm FROM superhero s WHERE s.height_cm>0 AND s.superhero_name<>'3-D Man' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id=s.id AND hp.power_id IN (SELECT hp2.power_id FROM hero_power hp2 JOIN superhero t ON t.id=hp2.hero_id WHERE t.superhero_name='3-D Man'))
answer: The average height is 339.5 cm. It covers heroes who share at least one power with 3-D Man. I left out 3-D Man and heroes whose height is NULL or 0, which the docs treat as missing. Each hero counts once, even if they share several powers with him.

sql:
WITH l AS (
SELECT country_id, home_player_1 p FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_2 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_3 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_4 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_5 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_6 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_7 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_8 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_9 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_10 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_11 FROM Match
UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_1 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_2 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_3 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_4 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_5 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_6 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_7 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_8 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_9 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_10 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_11 FROM Match),
