sql:
WITH b AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT c.uuid, f.name AS jname, c.type AS ctype
  FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid = c.uuid
  WHERE c.watermark = 'boros' AND f.language = 'Japanese'
), r AS (SELECT uuid, COUNT(*) AS n FROM rulings GROUP BY uuid)
SELECT b.jname AS japanese_name, b.ctype AS card_type, COALESCE(SUM(r.n), 0) AS total_rulings
FROM b LEFT JOIN r ON r.uuid = b.uuid
GROUP BY b.jname, b.ctype
ORDER BY b.jname, b.ctype
answer:
The query returns 96 cards with a boros watermark and a Japanese printing, one row per Japanese name plus English type line, with columns japanese_name, card_type, total_rulings. Cards with no rulings show 0. Card and Card Foreign Data are draft ontology terms, not certified.

Readings I chose:
- "English card type" is cards.type, the full English type line (e.g. "Creature — Human Soldier"), not the foreign-language type line.
- The ruling total counts every rulings row across all of a card's boros printings, as the question says. Identical rulings repeated on several printings are not collapsed. The ontology glossary suggests deduping by (date, text), which would give lower totals for multi-printing cards.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) FROM connected c JOIN atom a1 ON a1.atom_id=c.atom_id JOIN atom a2 ON a2.atom_id=c.atom_id2 JOIN bond b ON b.bond_id=c.bond_id JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id=b.molecule_id WHERE a1.element='c' AND a2.element='c' AND m.label='+' AND b.bond_type='='
answer: 478개입니다. 발암성 화합물(label '+')에서 두 원자가 모두 탄소('c')이고 결합 유형이 이중결합('=')인 결합을 bond_id 기준으로 중복 없이 세었습니다. 기존에 확인된 6번 쿼리와 같은 기준입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient p WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.SM IN ('negative','0')) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID=p.ID) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID=p.ID AND e.Thrombosis<>0) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.`U-PRO` IN ('30','100','300','>=300','>=1000','+1(30)','+2(100)'))
answer: 2 patients. Readings I chose: "no thrombosis" means the patient has at least one examination and none has Thrombosis other than 0. Proteinuria of 30 mg/dl or more means U-PRO is one of 30, 100, 300, >=300, >=1000, +1(30) or +2(100). The values 1 to 4, -15, '-', 'TR' and '%%' were not counted. I read 1 to 4 as below 30 and left '%%' out because its meaning is unclear.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom WHERE molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type='#') AND molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element IN ('p','br'));
answer: 4개입니다. 삼중 결합('#')이 있고 인 또는 브로민(p, br) 원자가 하나 이상 있는 분자에 속한 원자를 모두 센 값입니다. "phosphorus or bromine"은 둘 중 하나만 있어도 되는 것으로 해석했고, 원자 수에는 수소를 포함했습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM satscores AS s WHERE s.rtype = 'S' AND s.cname = 'Contra Costa' AND s.NumTstTakr > (SELECT t.NumTstTakr FROM satscores AS t WHERE CAST(t.cds AS INTEGER) = 7618040730051)
answer: 1 school in Contra Costa County had more SAT test takers than the school with CDS code 7618040730051. I counted only school-level rows (rtype = 'S'), took the county from satscores.cname, and used a strict greater-than, so ties are excluded. The 'SAT Score Record' term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.atom_id2) FROM connected c JOIN atom a ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id WHERE a.element = 'cl'
answer: 271 distinct atoms are bonded to a chlorine atom ('cl') across all molecules. I counted each neighbouring atom once, even when it is bonded to more than one chlorine. The `connected` table stores every bond in both directions, so reading the neighbour from one side is enough. If you wanted bonded pairs instead (chlorine, neighbour), the count is 314. A chlorine atom that is bonded to another chlorine is counted as a neighbour.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON p.id = s.publisher_id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'George Lucas' AND s.weight_kg > 0 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id)
answer: 77.40 kg. This is the average over the 5 George Lucas heroes who have at least one superpower and a recorded weight (135, 79, 79, 77 and 17 kg). Per the docs, a weight of 0 or NULL means "not recorded", so those heroes are excluded.

sql: SELECT cardKingdomFoilId, cardKingdomId FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND cardKingdomFoilId IS NOT NULL AND cardKingdomId IS NOT NULL ORDER BY CAST(cardKingdomFoilId AS INTEGER), CAST(cardKingdomId AS INTEGER) LIMIT 3
answer:
The three creature cards with the lowest Card Kingdom Foil ids are (Foil id, Card Kingdom id): 39001 / 38001, 39002 / 38002 and 39003 / 38003.

I made three choices where the question was ambiguous:
- **Creature cards:** I counted a card as a creature if `types` contains 'Creature', which includes artifact creatures.
- **Sort order:** I read "alphabetical order" as ordering the ids, and sorted them numerically because they are stored as text. Ties go to the Card Kingdom id.
- **Rows:** Each row is one printing in `cards`, since the ids are per printing.

sql: SELECT p.ID, CAST(STRFTIME('%Y','2026-10-09') AS INTEGER) - CAST(STRFTIME('%Y',p.Birthday) AS INTEGER) - (STRFTIME('%m-%d',p.Birthday) > '10-09') AS age FROM Patient p WHERE p.Birthday IS NOT NULL AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.HCT >= 52) >= 2 ORDER BY p.ID
answer: Three patients qualify: 2307640 (age 73), 3182521 (age 73) and 4007151 (age 58). Each lab row with HCT >= 52 counts as one result, and a patient needs at least two. Age is completed years on 2026-10-09. Patients with no Birthday are excluded. The Patient and Laboratory Test Terms are still draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT l.ID FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.SC170 IN ('negative','0') AND l.Date = (SELECT MAX(Date) FROM Laboratory WHERE ID = l.ID AND SC170 IS NOT NULL) AND l.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING MAX(Date) > '1997-01-01') ORDER BY l.ID
answer: 16 patient IDs match (944797, 1110526, 4632421, 4878272, 4915498, 4934716, 5065022, 5119703, 5184284, 5296268, 5300381, 5400270, 5404650, 5405581, 5440535, 5452747). I read the two conditions this way. The most recent lab sample is the patient's latest Laboratory.Date for any row, and it must be later than 1997-01-01. The most recent anti-Scl-70 result is the latest row where SC170 is not NULL. Normal means 'negative' or '0', as the wiki defines it. Patients who never had an SC170 result are excluded.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND leadershipSkills LIKE '%''brawl'': True%' AND name IN (SELECT name FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1)
answer: 101 different creature cards. I counted a card if it has a Brawl-commander printing (leadershipSkills has 'brawl': True) and any printing with isPromo = 1. The commander flag is checked on any printing, not only the promo one. If the promo printing itself had to carry the Brawl flag, the count would be 7, because most promo rows have no leadership data. I used the first reading, since commander eligibility belongs to the card and not to one printing. The 'Card' term this query relies on is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN Score > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS percentage FROM posts WHERE OwnerUserId = (SELECT Id FROM users ORDER BY Reputation DESC LIMIT 1)
answer: 0.66% of the top-reputation user's posts score above 50. The user is Id 919 with reputation 87393, and they have 1204 posts. The reputation ranking has no tie at the top. I counted every post type, not only questions.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) AS card_count FROM cards AS c INNER JOIN legalities AS l ON l.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.manaCost = '{0}' AND l.format = 'commander' AND l.status = 'Legal'
answer: 43 different cards have a printed mana cost of {0} and are legal in Commander. I counted distinct card names, because the cards table has one row per printing. "Printed mana cost of {0}" means manaCost is exactly '{0}'. "Legal in Commander" means the legalities row for format 'commander' has status 'Legal'. The Card and Card Legality terms used are still draft (not certified).

answer: The top-reputation user in York, England is 24 years old (user 24789, reputation 106). I counted locations 'York' and 'York, United Kingdom' as York, England. sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(a.element='cl')/COUNT(*),4) AS chlorine_percentage FROM atom a WHERE a.molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type='-')
answer: 염소(cl) 원자는 단일 결합('-')이 하나 이상 있는 분자의 전체 원자 중 3.4824%입니다. 분모는 이런 분자에 속한 모든 원자 수이고, 분자 단위 평균이 아니라 원자 전체를 기준으로 계산했습니다.

The query returns 96 cards (Japanese name, English type, total rulings). A card is a distinct pair of Japanese name (foreign_data, language 'Japanese') and English type (cards.type), limited to cards with watermark 'boros'. Rulings are counted as all rows across every printing, as the question asks. I did not dedupe repeated ruling text, although the wiki suggests deduping for per-name counts. Cards with no rulings show 0. For example, 'Hide // Seek' (Instant) has 0 and 'そびえ立つ雷拳' (Creature — Giant Soldier) has 1.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patient_count FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND l.WBC > 3.5 AND l.WBC < 9.0 AND (l.FG < 150 OR l.FG > 450) AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 15
answer:
1 female patient has a laboratory record, on any date, with a normal WBC, an abnormal fibrinogen level and an RNP above 15.

I read the terms as follows:
- **Normal WBC:** between 3.5 and 9.0, from the Laboratory column documentation. Counting the endpoints as normal gives the same result.
- **Abnormal fibrinogen:** FG below 150 or above 450, the complement of the documented normal range of 150 to 450.
- **RNP above 15:** `CAST(RNP AS REAL) > 15`. Text values such as 'negative' cast to 0, so they drop out.
- **Same-record condition:** all three conditions must hold in the same laboratory record. The count is of distinct patients.

The Patient and Laboratory Test terms I relied on are still draft in the ontology. The run also warned that the profiled FG range is 23.8 to 106.5, which is below the 150 cutoff. The FG filter follows the documented ranges, but the stored FG values look unusual.

sql: SELECT 100.0*(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y',date)='1997' THEN amount END)-SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y',date)='1996' THEN amount END))/SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y',date)='1996' THEN amount END) AS growth_pct FROM loan WHERE account_id IN (SELECT d.account_id FROM disp d JOIN client c ON c.client_id=d.client_id WHERE d.type='OWNER' AND c.gender='M')

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(julianday(e.d) - julianday(p."First Date"))) AS avg_delay_days FROM Patient p JOIN (SELECT ID, MIN("Examination Date") AS d FROM Examination GROUP BY ID) e ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE p.Admission LIKE '+%' AND p."First Date" IS NOT NULL AND e.d IS NOT NULL

sql: SELECT e.Symptoms FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=e.ID WHERE e.Thrombosis>0 AND e.Symptoms IS NOT NULL AND ','||REPLACE(p.Diagnosis,' ','')||',' LIKE '%,SLE,%' GROUP BY e.Symptoms ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, e.Symptoms LIMIT 1

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN pa.defensive_work_rate='high' THEN p.player_api_id END)/COUNT(DISTINCT p.player_api_id),2) AS pct FROM Player p JOIN Player_Attributes pa ON pa.player_api_id=p.player_api_id WHERE p.birthday>='1991-01-01' AND pa.defensive_work_rate IN ('low','medium','high')

sql: WITH latest AS (SELECT player_api_id, MAX(date) AS d FROM Player_Attributes WHERE defensive_work_rate IN ('low','medium','high') GROUP BY player_api_id), cur AS (SELECT pa.player_api_id FROM Player_Attributes pa JOIN latest l ON pa.player_api_id = l.player_api_id AND pa.date = l.d GROUP BY pa.player_api_id HAVING MIN(pa.defensive_work_rate) = 'medium' AND MAX(pa.defensive_work_rate) = 'medium') SELECT ROUND(AVG(p.height), 2) AS avg_height_cm FROM Player p JOIN cur ON p.player_api_id = cur.player_api_id WHERE CAST(substr(p.birthday,1,4) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 1990 AND 1995

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.height_cm > 0 THEN s.height_cm END), 1) AS avg_height_cm, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END), 1) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'George Lucas'

sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM Patient p WHERE
EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.SM IN ('negative','0'))
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID=p.ID)
AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID=p.ID AND e.Thrombosis<>0)
AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory u WHERE u.ID=p.ID AND (u."U-PRO"='%%' OR CASE WHEN u."U-PRO" LIKE '%(%' THEN CAST(substr(u."U-PRO",instr(u."U-PRO",'(')+1,instr(u."U-PRO",')')-instr(u."U-PRO",'(')-1) AS REAL) WHEN u."U-PRO" LIKE '>=%' THEN CAST(substr(u."U-PRO",3) AS REAL) ELSE CAST(u."U-PRO" AS REAL) END >= 30))
answer: 2 patients. Readings I chose: (1) "no thrombosis" means the patient has at least one examination and none has Thrombosis other than 0. (2) Significant proteinuria is a U-PRO of 30 mg/dL or more: plain numbers of 30 and above, '+1(30)' and '+2(100)' by the value in parentheses, '>=300' and '>=1000', and '%%' (saturated dipstick). '-', '0', 'TR', plain 1 to 4, and the unexplained '-15' do not count.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(h.attribute_value), 1) AS avg_intelligence FROM hero_attribute h JOIN attribute a ON a.id = h.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Intelligence' AND h.attribute_value IS NOT NULL AND h.hero_id IN (SELECT hp.hero_id FROM hero_power hp JOIN superpower p ON p.id = hp.power_id WHERE p.power_name IN ('Super Speed', 'Death Touch'))

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(c),2) FROM (SELECT e.event_id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event=e.event_id) AS c FROM event e WHERE e.event_id IN (SELECT link_to_event FROM budget WHERE category='Advertisement'))

sql: SELECT f."Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)", f."District Code" FROM frpm f JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode WHERE s.AdmFName1 = 'Alusine'

sql: SELECT element, COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) AS molecule_count FROM atom WHERE element IN (SELECT a.element FROM bond b JOIN connected c ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id JOIN atom a ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id WHERE b.bond_type = '#') GROUP BY element ORDER BY molecule_count DESC, element ASC;

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS good_non_dc_count FROM superhero AS s JOIN alignment AS a ON a.id = s.alignment_id LEFT JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id WHERE a.alignment = 'Good' AND p.publisher_name IS NOT 'DC Comics'

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) FROM cards AS c JOIN foreign_data AS f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE f.language = 'Chinese Simplified') / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards), 0), 2) AS percentage

sql: SELECT s.School, f.`Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (Ages 5-17)` FROM schools AS s LEFT JOIN frpm AS f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode WHERE s.County = 'Los Angeles' AND s.GSserved = 'K-9'

sql: SELECT CAST(ROUND(AVG(julianday(e.m) - julianday(p."First Date"))) AS INTEGER) AS avg_delay_days FROM Patient p JOIN (SELECT ID, MIN("Examination Date") AS m FROM Examination GROUP BY ID) e ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE p.Admission LIKE '%+%' AND p."First Date" <> ''

sql: select ra.year, re.time from races ra join results re using(raceId) where ra.name='Chinese Grand Prix' and ra.year between 2000 and 2009 and ra.time is not null and re.positionOrder=2 order by ra.time asc, ra.year desc limit 1

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(mv),1) FROM (SELECT name, MIN(convertedManaCost) mv FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND edhrecRank BETWEEN 1 AND 1000 AND name IN (SELECT c2.name FROM cards c2 JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid=c2.uuid WHERE l.status='Banned') GROUP BY name)

sql:
WITH RECURSIVE n(id,rest,tok) AS (
 SELECT ID, replace(replace(replace(replace(Diagnosis,char(11),','),char(29),','),'  ',','),', ',',')||',', NULL FROM Patient WHERE Diagnosis IS NOT NULL
 UNION ALL
 SELECT id, substr(rest,instr(rest,',')+1), trim(substr(rest,1,instr(rest,',')-1)) FROM n WHERE rest<>''
),
t AS (SELECT id, upper(tok) tok FROM n WHERE tok IS NOT NULL AND tok<>'' AND upper(tok) NOT LIKE '%SUSP%'),
p AS (SELECT id FROM t GROUP BY id
 HAVING count(DISTINCT tok)=2 AND count(DISTINCT CASE WHEN tok IN ('RA','SJS') THEN tok END)=2)
SELECT sum(EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.id AND l.PLT BETWEEN 100 AND 400)) AS with_normal_plt,
       sum(NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.id AND l.PLT BETWEEN 100 AND 400)) AS without_normal_plt
FROM p;
answer:
38 patients have a Patient.Diagnosis of exactly rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and Sjögren's syndrome (SJS), in either order. 5 of them have had at least one laboratory result with a normal platelet level, and 33 have never had one. That count includes patients with no laboratory rows.

I made these choices:
- Normal platelet level is PLT from 100 to 400 inclusive, which is the wiki's confirmed convention. The docs give strict bounds (100 < N < 400).
- Entries marked "susp" are ignored as diagnoses. So "RA, SJS, SLE susp" counts as RA plus SJS, while "RA, SJS susp" counts as RA only and is excluded.
- I split the diagnosis text on commas, on the control-character separators, and on a double space ("SJS  RA"), so those variants are included.
- A laboratory row with a NULL PLT is not a normal result.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(Consumption), 2) AS avg_monthly_consumption FROM yearmonth WHERE CustomerID = 15621 AND Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312' AND Consumption > 0
answer: 고객 15621의 2013년 월평균 연료 소비량은 6.02입니다. 소비량이 0보다 큰 달만 계산했고, 해당하는 달은 6월(3.5), 7월(12.91), 10월(1.65)입니다. 소비량이 0.0으로 기록된 4월, 5월, 9월은 연료를 구매하지 않은 달로 보고 제외했습니다. 0인 달까지 넣으면 평균은 달라집니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT q.driverId) FROM qualifying AS q JOIN races AS r ON r.raceId = q.raceId WHERE r.year = 1995 AND q.q1 IS NOT NULL AND q.q1 <> '' AND CAST(SUBSTR(q.q1, 1, INSTR(q.q1, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60 + CAST(SUBSTR(q.q1, INSTR(q.q1, ':') + 1) AS REAL) > 120

sql: SELECT expense_date, SUM(cost) AS total_cost FROM expense WHERE expense_date = (SELECT MAX(e.expense_date) FROM expense e JOIN member m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member WHERE m.position = 'Vice President') GROUP BY expense_date
answer: The Vice President's most recent expense is dated 2019-11-19. All expenses on record for that date total 128.33 (3 expenses). sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(a.alignment='Neutral')/COUNT(*),2) AS neutral_percentage, SUM(a.alignment='Neutral' AND p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics') AS neutral_marvel_count FROM superhero s LEFT JOIN alignment a ON a.id=s.alignment_id LEFT JOIN publisher p ON p.id=s.publisher_id
answer: 3.73% of all 750 superheroes are Neutral, and 10 of those Neutral superheroes were published by Marvel Comics. I counted every superhero in the denominator, including those with 'N/A' alignment.

sql: SELECT f.`County Name` AS county, COUNT(*) AS qualifying_schools FROM frpm AS f JOIN satscores AS t ON t.cds = f.CDSCode WHERE t.rtype = 'S' AND f.`Academic Year` = '2014-2015' AND t.NumGE1500 >= 1 AND f.`Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)` > 0.1 GROUP BY f.`County Name` ORDER BY qualifying_schools DESC, county ASC
answer:
The query returns 56 counties with at least one qualifying school. Los Angeles is first with 305 schools, then San Diego (86), Orange (62), San Bernardino (60) and Riverside (58). Ties are broken alphabetically by county.

I made these choices where the question was ambiguous:
- **Schools only:** I used school-level SAT records (rtype 'S') and excluded district rows.
- **Free-meal rate:** I used the K-12 free-meal eligibility rate, `Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12)`, as a 0–1 fraction above 0.1. It matches free-meal count divided by K-12 enrollment on every row.
- **SAT threshold:** "At least one taker scoring 1500 or higher" means `NumGE1500 >= 1`.
- **Year:** The frpm table holds only 2014-2015 data. I filtered on that year anyway.
- **County name:** It comes from the frpm table. Where I compared it with the schools table for the top counties, the two matched.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT artist, COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS creature_cards FROM cards WHERE types LIKE '%Creature%' AND artist IS NOT NULL GROUP BY artist) SELECT artist, creature_cards FROM c WHERE creature_cards=(SELECT MAX(creature_cards) FROM c)
answer: Kev Walker has illustrated the most different creature cards, with 275. No other artist ties. I counted a creature card when `types` contains 'Creature' (this includes Artifact Creature). Different cards are counted as distinct card names, so reprints don't add to the count.

sql: SELECT s.superhero_name, s.full_name FROM superhero s JOIN hero_attribute ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id JOIN attribute a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Speed' AND ha.attribute_value = (SELECT MAX(h2.attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute h2 JOIN attribute a2 ON a2.id = h2.attribute_id WHERE a2.attribute_name = 'Speed') AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name <> '-' ORDER BY s.superhero_name
answer: 29 superheroes share the top Speed value and have a known full name (Flash, Superman, Quicksilver, Silver Surfer and others). I took "top Speed" as the maximum attribute_value for the 'Speed' attribute, with ties included. I took "real name not identifiable" as full_name NULL or '-', which follows the ontology's glossary. The result is ordered by superhero name, which you didn't ask for. The Superhero, Attribute and Hero Attribute Score terms are still draft, not certified. I did not call validate_sql before run_sql, and run_sql returned no warnings.

sql: SELECT frameVersion AS frame_year, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE name='Tarmogoyf'), 2) AS pct FROM cards WHERE name='Tarmogoyf' AND frameVersion = (SELECT MAX(CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER)) FROM cards WHERE name='Tarmogoyf' AND frameVersion = CAST(CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER) AS TEXT)) GROUP BY frameVersion
answer: The newest frame version among Tarmogoyf's printings is 2015, and 66.67% of all its printings use it. I ignored the non-numeric 'future' frame value when picking the newest year, as the verified Tarmogoyf query does. The percentage is over every Tarmogoyf row in `cards`, one row per printing. The `Card` term it relies on is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, d.url, d.dob, COUNT(q.qualifyId) AS q3_count FROM drivers d LEFT JOIN qualifying q ON q.driverId = d.driverId AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(q.q3) <> '' WHERE d.nationality = 'German' AND CAST(STRFTIME('%Y', d.dob) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 1971 AND 1985 GROUP BY d.driverId ORDER BY q3_count DESC, d.dob ASC
answer: 7 German drivers born 1971-1985: Nico Rosberg 149 Q3 times, Nick Heidfeld 44, Adrian Sutil 19, Ralf Schumacher 15, Timo Glock 13, Markus Winkelhock 0, André Lotterer 0. Drivers with zero Q3 times are kept via a LEFT JOIN, since the question asks for every driver in the range. German means drivers.nationality = 'German'. The Driver and Qualifying Result terms are still drafts, and validate_sql was not run before run_sql.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg)) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero s WHERE s.skin_colour_id = 14 AND s.alignment_id = 2 AND s.weight_kg > 0 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id AND hp.power_id = 9)
answer: 121 kg. This averages 2 characters, with an unrounded mean of 120.5. I read "green-skinned" as skin colour exactly 'Green' (not 'Green/Blue'), "villain" as alignment 'Bad', and "can fly" as having the 'Flight' power. Weights of 0 or NULL are treated as never measured and left out.

sql:
select e.type,
 (select count(distinct a.link_to_member) from attendance a join event x on x.event_id=a.link_to_event where x.type=e.type and x.event_date like '2019%') as members_attended,
 (select coalesce(sum(b.amount),0) from budget b join event x on x.event_id=b.link_to_event where x.type=e.type and x.event_date like '2019%') as total_budgeted
from event e where e.event_date like '2019%' group by e.type order by e.type
answer:
I ran the query and it returns one row per 2019 event type, in alphabetical order. The columns are type, members_attended and total_budgeted.

| type | members_attended | total_budgeted |
|---|---|---|
| Budget | 5 | 0 |
| Community Service | 13 | 0 |
| Election | 0 | 0 |
| Game | 24 | 0 |
| Guest Speaker | 29 | 785 |
| Meeting | 30 | 1175 |
| Registration | 30 | 300 |
| Social | 24 | 0 |

I made three choices where the question was open:
- **Attendance:** "How many members attended" counts distinct members per type, so someone who went to several events of the same type counts once. Counting attendance rows would give larger numbers.
- **Budget:** The budgeted amount is the sum of `budget.amount` (the planned amount), not `spent`. The query uses subqueries so the attendance and budget sums don't multiply each other.
- **Year and zeros:** 2019 means event dates starting with '2019'. Types with no budget lines or no attendees show 0.

sql: WITH RECURSIVE split(eid, cat, cost, item, rest) AS (SELECT x.expense_id, b.category, x.cost, '', x.expense_description || ',' FROM expense x JOIN budget b ON b.budget_id = x.link_to_budget JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE e.event_name = 'October Meeting' AND x.approved = 'true' UNION ALL SELECT eid, cat, cost, trim(substr(rest, 1, instr(rest, ',') - 1)), substr(rest, instr(rest, ',') + 1) FROM split WHERE rest <> ''), d AS (SELECT DISTINCT eid, cat, cost, item FROM split WHERE item <> '') SELECT item, cat AS category, SUM(cost) AS total_cost FROM d GROUP BY item, cat ORDER BY cat, item
answer:
October Meeting has 5 items bought with approved expenses. Each total is the sum of the approved purchases that included the item:
- Advertisement: Posters, $54.25
- Food: Pizza, $51.81
- Food: Water, $69.33
- Food: chips, $69.33
- Food: cookies, $69.33

Water, chips and cookies were bought together in one $69.33 purchase, so each shows the full purchase cost, not a share of it.

Readings I chose:
- Only expenses with approved = 'true' count. The one expense with no approval mark is excluded.
- Items come from splitting the comma-separated expense description, and an item named twice in one purchase counts that purchase once.
- 'October Meeting' is the exact event name. 'Officers meeting - October' and 'October Speaker' are different events and are excluded.
- Item names are kept as stored, so the capitalization differs ('chips' and 'cookies' are lowercase).

The Expense, Budget and Event terms the query relies on are still draft, not certified.

sql:
WITH cl AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.client_id, d.account_id FROM disp d JOIN card c ON c.disp_id=d.disp_id WHERE d.type='OWNER' AND c.type='classic'),
acc AS (SELECT DISTINCT account_id FROM cl),
cc AS (SELECT a.district_id, COUNT(DISTINCT cl.client_id) n FROM cl JOIN account a ON a.account_id=cl.account_id GROUP BY a.district_id),
p AS (SELECT a.district_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.bank||'|'||t.account) ext, SUM(t.amount) tot FROM trans t JOIN acc ON acc.account_id=t.account_id JOIN account a ON a.account_id=t.account_id WHERE t.type='VYDAJ' AND t.account>0 AND t.bank IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(t.bank)<>'' GROUP BY a.district_id)
SELECT di.A2 AS district_name, COALESCE(cc.n,0) AS client_count, COALESCE(p.ext,0) AS external_accounts, COALESCE(p.tot,0) AS total_amount
FROM district di LEFT JOIN cc ON cc.district_id=di.district_id LEFT JOIN p ON p.district_id=di.district_id
ORDER BY total_amount DESC, district_name;
answer:
I ran the query and it returns one row for each of the 77 districts. Hl.m. Praha is first with 96 clients, 123 external accounts and 14,125,240 paid, followed by Olomouc (11 clients, 16 accounts, 3,235,882) and Kolin (12 clients, 22 accounts, 3,149,128). Districts with no matching clients or payments show zeros. I did not look at the bottom of the list.

Readings I chose:
- **Clients:** a client counts if they hold the OWNER disposition on an account and that same disposition has a card of type 'classic'. Each client is counted once, under the branch district of the account they own (`account.district_id`), not their home district.
- **Outgoing payments:** these are `trans` rows with `type='VYDAJ'` on those owned accounts, over the whole history. I kept only payments with a real external counterparty, meaning `account>0` and a non-blank bank code. Of the 634,571 VYDAJ rows in the database, 208,282 have such a counterparty.
- **External accounts:** the count is of distinct (bank, account) pairs per district. A pair paid from accounts in two different districts counts once in each.
- **Total amount:** the sum of `amount` over those payments, unrounded. Ties are broken alphabetically by district name.

If you wanted the total to include outgoing payments with no counterparty recorded, the amounts would be larger. I excluded them because the question is about money sent to accounts at other banks.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT c.Segment AS segment, ROUND((SUM(CASE WHEN y.Date LIKE '2013%' THEN y.Consumption END) - SUM(CASE WHEN y.Date LIKE '2012%' THEN y.Consumption END)) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN y.Date LIKE '2012%' THEN y.Consumption END), 2) AS increase_pct FROM customers c JOIN yearmonth y ON y.CustomerID = c.CustomerID WHERE c.Currency = 'EUR' AND c.Segment IN ('SME','LAM','KAM') GROUP BY c.Segment) SELECT segment, increase_pct FROM t WHERE increase_pct = (SELECT MAX(increase_pct) FROM t) OR increase_pct = (SELECT MIN(increase_pct) FROM t) ORDER BY increase_pct DESC

The data stops at 201311, so 2013 has 11 months against 12 for 2012, and I did not adjust for that. I skipped validate_sql, and the Terms used are drafts.

sql: SELECT a.element, SUM(EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM connected c WHERE c.atom_id=a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2=a.atom_id)) AS bonded_atoms FROM atom a WHERE a.molecule_id='TR397' GROUP BY a.element ORDER BY a.element

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) / 12.0 AS avg_schools_opened_per_month FROM schools WHERE County = 'San Diego' AND OpenDate >= '1980-01-01' AND OpenDate < '1981-01-01' AND DOCType IN ('Unified School District','Elementary School District','High School District','County Office of Education (COE)')

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(p.SEX='F')/COUNT(*),2) AS female_percentage FROM Patient p WHERE p.Birthday IS NOT NULL AND (CAST(substr('2026-10-09',1,4) AS INT)-CAST(substr(p.Birthday,1,4) AS INT)-(substr('2026-10-09',6,5)<substr(p.Birthday,6,5)))>55 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.PT>=14)

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*COUNT(CASE WHEN a.alignment='Neutral' THEN 1 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS neutral_percentage, COUNT(CASE WHEN a.alignment='Neutral' AND p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' THEN 1 END) AS neutral_marvel_count FROM superhero s LEFT JOIN alignment a ON a.id=s.alignment_id LEFT JOIN publisher p ON p.id=s.publisher_id

sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(mj.college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences'), 0) AS humanities_social_sciences_members, COALESCE(SUM(mj.college IS NOT 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences'), 0) AS other_members FROM member m LEFT JOIN major mj ON mj.major_id = m.link_to_major;

sql:
WITH w AS (SELECT a.district_id, SUM(t.amount) AS tw FROM trans t JOIN account a ON a.account_id=t.account_id WHERE t.type='VYDAJ' GROUP BY a.district_id),
o AS (SELECT a.district_id, SUM(o.amount) AS os FROM "order" o JOIN account a ON a.account_id=o.account_id GROUP BY a.district_id),
n AS (SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS accts FROM account GROUP BY district_id)
SELECT d.A2 AS district_name, d.A3 AS region, CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) AS population, w.tw AS total_withdrawn,
ROUND(w.tw*1.0/CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER),2) AS withdrawals_per_inhabitant,
RANK() OVER (ORDER BY ROUND(w.tw*1.0/CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER),2) DESC) AS withdrawal_rank,
ROUND(COALESCE(o.os,0)*1.0/n.accts,2) AS avg_standing_order_debit_per_account
FROM district d JOIN w ON w.district_id=d.district_id JOIN n ON n.district_id=d.district_id LEFT JOIN o ON o.district_id=d.district_id
WHERE CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER)>=100000 ORDER BY withdrawal_rank, district_name
answer:
The query lists every district with at least 100,000 inhabitants that has withdrawals, ranked from highest withdrawals per inhabitant (Usti nad Orlici first, at 343.79). I ran it and it returned rows; I checked the first 50 and did not count the total.

Choices I made where the question was open:
- **Withdrawals:** I counted transactions of type VYDAJ, which the confirmed queries treat as withdrawn money. Cash withdrawals of type VYBER are not included.
- **District of a transaction:** I used the district of the branch where the account is held, not the client's home district.
- **Population:** `district.A4`, converted from text to a number, with 100,000 or more qualifying.
- **Ranking:** competition ranking on the rounded per-inhabitant value, so ties share a rank and the next rank is skipped.
- **Standing orders:** the sum of all standing-order amounts in the district divided by every account held there, so accounts with no standing orders count as zero.

sql: SELECT m.molecule_id FROM molecule m WHERE m.label='-' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM atom a WHERE a.molecule_id=m.molecule_id AND a.element IN ('na','k','ca','sn','cu','zn','y','pb')) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id=m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type='-') ORDER BY m.molecule_id LIMIT 3
answer: TR011, TR101, TR139. Assumptions: non-carcinogenic means label '-'. Metal atoms are the metallic elements present in the data (na, k, ca, sn, cu, zn, y, pb). 'Has single bonds' means at least one bond of type '-', because requiring all bonds to be single returned no rows. The Atom, Bond and Molecule terms are draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE('u' || p.OwnerUserId, 'n' || p.OwnerDisplayName)) AS user_count FROM votes v JOIN posts p ON p.Id = v.PostId WHERE v.BountyAmount >= 30 AND v.CreationDate >= '2010-01-01' AND v.CreationDate < '2011-01-01'
answer: 32 users. I counted distinct post owners across the 48 bounty votes of 30 or more recorded in 2010. A post owner is identified by OwnerUserId, or by OwnerDisplayName when no owner account is recorded (2 of the 48 votes). Bounty date is the vote's CreationDate.

sql: SELECT a.element, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN c.atom_id IS NOT NULL THEN a.atom_id END) AS n FROM atom a LEFT JOIN (SELECT atom_id FROM connected UNION SELECT atom_id2 FROM connected) c ON c.atom_id=a.atom_id WHERE a.molecule_id='TR397' GROUP BY a.element ORDER BY a.element;
answer: TR397 has 34 bonded c atoms, 24 h, 6 n, 16 o and 4 s. It also contains na atoms, but none of them is in a bond, so na is listed with 0. I counted an atom as bonded if it appears on either side of a row in `connected`. I kept elements that have no bonded atoms because the question asks for each element present among the atoms. If you want only elements with at least one bonded atom, drop the na row.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.alignment='Good' THEN s.id END)/COUNT(DISTINCT s.id),2) FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON p.id=s.publisher_id JOIN alignment a ON a.id=s.alignment_id JOIN hero_power hp ON hp.hero_id=s.id WHERE p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics'
answer: 64.97. Reading chosen: Marvel Comics heroes with at least one row in hero_power, counted once each. Heroes with no recorded alignment (6 in the whole table) are left out of the base, because the query joins on alignment. The share with alignment 'Good' is 64.97%.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p WHERE p.SEX='F' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.SC170 IN ('negative','0')) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID=p.ID AND e.Symptoms IS NOT NULL)
answer: 19 distinct female patients. Reading used: normal anti-Scl-70 means at least one Laboratory.SC170 value of 'negative' or '0'. No symptom means no Examination row with non-null Symptoms, and patients with no examination rows count. The Patient, Laboratory Test and Special Examination Terms used are still draft (not certified).

sql: SELECT r.year, d.forename, d.surname, x.time FROM races r JOIN results x ON x.raceId = r.raceId AND x.position = 1 JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = x.driverId WHERE r.name = 'Canadian Grand Prix' AND r.year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2017 AND r.time <= '17:00:00' ORDER BY r.year
answer: Four editions started at 17:00 local time or earlier: 2007 Lewis Hamilton (1:44:11.292), 2008 Robert Kubica (1:36:24.227), 2010 Lewis Hamilton (1:33:53.456) and 2011 Jenson Button (4:04:39.537). I read 'began' as the scheduled local start time in races.time, with 17:00:00 included. 2007, 2008 and 2011 started at 17:00 and 2010 at 16:00. The 2012 to 2017 races started at 18:00 and are excluded. There was no race in 2009. The winner is the driver with position = 1. The 2011 race was a long rain-delayed one, so its time is much longer than the others.

sql: select 100.0*(e.balance-s.balance)/s.balance as pct_increase from loan l join trans s on s.account_id=l.account_id and s.date='1993-03-22' join trans e on e.account_id=l.account_id and e.date='1998-12-27' where l.date='1993-07-05'
answer: The balance of account 1787 (loan 5314, dated 1993-07-05) rose from 1100 on 1993-03-22 to 5835 on 1998-12-27. That is an increase of about 430.45%. Each date has exactly one transaction on this account, so the "recorded balance" is that transaction's balance. I did not round the result.

sql:
WITH gold AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.account_id FROM card c JOIN disp d ON d.disp_id=c.disp_id WHERE c.type='gold'),
t AS (SELECT account_id,
 SUM(CASE WHEN type='PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) rec,
 SUM(CASE WHEN type<>'PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) wd,
 COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN account>0 AND bank IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(bank)<>'' THEN bank||'|'||account END) cp
 FROM trans GROUP BY account_id),
l AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) n FROM loan GROUP BY account_id)
SELECT g.account_id, di.A2 AS district_name, di.A3 AS region,
 COALESCE(t.rec,0) AS total_received, COALESCE(t.wd,0) AS total_withdrawn,
 COALESCE(l.n,0) AS loans_taken, COALESCE(t.cp,0) AS external_counterparties,
 RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(t.cp,0) DESC) AS rank
FROM gold g JOIN account a ON a.account_id=g.account_id JOIN district di ON di.district_id=a.district_id
LEFT JOIN t ON t.account_id=g.account_id LEFT JOIN l ON l.account_id=g.account_id
ORDER BY rank, g.account_id
answer:
쿼리는 골드카드 계좌 87개를 반환합니다. 결과 행은 헤더를 제외하고 87개이며, 외부 거래 상대 수가 같으면 같은 순위를 주고 다음 순위를 건너뛰는 RANK()로 순위를 매겼습니다. 1위는 계좌 2982(Prachatice, south Bohemia)로 외부 거래 상대가 6곳입니다.

모호한 부분은 다음과 같이 해석했습니다.
- 골드카드 계좌는 소유자(OWNER)와 사용자(DISPONENT)를 구분하지 않고, 골드카드가 연결된 모든 계좌로 봤습니다. 데이터에서 골드카드는 모두 OWNER에게 발급되어 있어 결과는 같습니다.
- 지점의 지역구는 account.district_id 기준이고, 지역은 district.A3입니다.
- 총 수신액은 type이 PRIJEM인 거래의 합입니다. 총 인출액은 PRIJEM이 아닌 모든 거래(VYDAJ와 현금 인출 VYBER)의 합입니다. VYDAJ만 인출로 보면 값이 달라질 수 있습니다.
- 대출 건수는 loan 테이블의 건수이고, 대출이 없으면 0입니다.
- 외부 거래 상대는 은행 코드와 상대 계좌 번호가 모두 있고 상대 계좌 번호가 0보다 큰 (bank, account) 조합의 고유 개수입니다. 송금과 수신을 모두 포함하며, 해당 거래가 없는 계좌는 0으로 포함했습니다.
- 집계 기간은 전체 기록 기간입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.atom_id2) FROM connected c JOIN atom a ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id WHERE a.element = 's' AND m.label = '+'
answer: 81 distinct atoms are directly bonded to a sulfur atom in carcinogenic ('+') molecules. I counted distinct atoms. There are 85 sulfur-neighbor bond pairs, because 4 atoms are bonded to two sulfurs. Counting bonds instead would give 85.

sql: SELECT AVG(s.weight_kg) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero s WHERE s.weight_kg > 0 AND s.race_id IS NOT NULL AND s.race_id NOT IN (SELECT s2.race_id FROM superhero s2 JOIN gender g ON g.id = s2.gender_id WHERE g.gender = 'Female' AND s2.race_id IS NOT NULL)
answer:
The average weight is about 156,709.09 kg. That is implausibly large, so a few very large weight values in the data are probably driving it. I did not check for outliers.

How I read the question:
- A race counts as having no female heroes if no hero of that race has gender 'Female'.
- Heroes with no race are left out.
- Unrecorded weights (weight_kg of 0 or NULL) are excluded from the average.
- I left the result unrounded, since you didn't ask for rounding.
- Including or excluding the unknown-race placeholder '-' gives the same value.

The Gender, Race and Superhero terms I used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT c.name, (m/60000)||':'||printf('%02d',(m%60000)/1000)||'.'||printf('%03d',m%1000) AS fastest_lap FROM (SELECT r.circuitId, MIN(l.milliseconds) m FROM lapTimes l JOIN races r ON r.raceId=l.raceId GROUP BY r.circuitId) x JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId=x.circuitId WHERE c.country='Italy' AND m IS NOT NULL ORDER BY c.name
answer: 이탈리아 서킷 중 랩 기록이 있는 곳은 두 곳입니다. Autodromo Enzo e Dino Ferrari의 최단 랩은 1:20.411, Autodromo Nazionale di Monza는 1:21.046입니다. lapTimes의 milliseconds 최솟값을 서킷별로 구해 m:ss.mmm 형식으로 바꿨고, 서킷 국가는 circuits.country = 'Italy'로 판단했습니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS REAL) / f."Enrollment (K-12)", 6) FROM frpm f JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode WHERE s.SOC = '66' ORDER BY f."FRPM Count (K-12)" DESC LIMIT 5
answer: The five rates, ordered by FRPM Count (K-12) from highest to lowest, are 0.917948, 0.999329, 0.896499, 0.89582 and 0.91418. I read the meal count as FRPM Count (K-12) and the rate as that count divided by Enrollment (K-12). Ownership code 66 is schools.SOC = '66'. The School and Free or Reduced Price Meal Record Terms I used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select count(distinct case when t.k_symbol='SIPO' then t.trans_id end) as household_payments, count(distinct case when t.k_symbol<>'' and t.k_symbol<>'SIPO' then t.trans_id end) as other_purpose_payments from trans t where t.amount>4000 and t.account_id in (select d.account_id from disp d join client c on c.client_id=d.client_id where c.gender='M' and substr(c.birth_date,1,4) in ('1974','1975','1976'))
answer: Household payments: 1556. Other-purpose payments: 486. Assumptions: household means trans.k_symbol = 'SIPO'. Payments with a NULL or empty-string k_symbol count as no purpose recorded and are left out. Each transaction is counted once, even if its account has several qualifying male customers.

sql: select round(avg(s.weight_kg)) from superhero s join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id where p.publisher_name='DC Comics' and s.weight_kg>0 and s.eye_colour_id in (select s2.eye_colour_id from superhero s2 join publisher p2 on p2.id=s2.publisher_id where p2.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' and s2.eye_colour_id is not null)
answer: 102 kg. I treated a weight of NULL or 0 as unknown, as the docs define. I matched on eye colour id, so 'No Colour' counts like any other colour.

sql: SELECT id FROM cards WHERE duelDeck = 'a'
answer: 804 cards have duelDeck = 'a'. I returned the integer `id` column of `cards`, not the uuid. Running the query gave 804 distinct IDs, starting 14440, 14441, 14442.

sql: SELECT Diagnosis FROM Patient WHERE "First Date" BETWEEN '1998-02-15' AND '1998-02-28' AND Admission = '+' ORDER BY Birthday ASC, ID ASC LIMIT 1
answer: BEHCET (patient 5761409, born 1985-09-08, first seen 1998-02-17). I treated "inpatient" as Admission = '+', following the wiki's default. Age at first presentation is First Date minus Birthday, so the earliest birthday is the oldest. Two patients in the window have the malformed mark '+(' (5765821, born 1938, diagnosis 'WG^]SJS'; 5766000, born 1950). If you count those as inpatients, the answer becomes 'WG^]SJS'.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT mj.college AS college, COUNT(DISTINCT mj.major_id) AS n FROM member m JOIN major mj ON mj.major_id = m.link_to_major GROUP BY mj.college) SELECT college, n AS num_majors FROM c WHERE n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM c) ORDER BY college
answer: Two colleges tie for the most majors on the roster, with 6 majors each: College of Agriculture and Applied Sciences (6) and College of Humanities and Social Sciences (6). I counted distinct majors per college (not members) across all members regardless of position. Members without a major link are not counted. The query relies on the Major term, which is still a draft and not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c WHERE c.name = 'Counterspell' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM foreign_data f WHERE f.uuid = c.uuid AND f.language = 'French') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM foreign_data f WHERE f.uuid = c.uuid AND f.language = 'Italian')
answer: 9. Counterspell has 48 printings (rows in cards). I counted each printing that has both a French and an Italian entry in foreign_data. I took "printing" to mean one cards row.

sql: WITH l AS (SELECT ID, Date, RNP, CPK, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ID ORDER BY Date DESC) rn FROM Laboratory WHERE RNP IS NOT NULL) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN l ON l.ID=p.ID AND l.rn=1 WHERE p.SEX='F' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 64 AND l.CPK < 250
answer: 2 female patients. Reading used: each patient's most recent laboratory record that has an RNP value, with CPK taken from that same record. Thresholds are strict (RNP > 64, CPK < 250). The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still drafts.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(cnt), 2) AS avg_pit_stops_per_race FROM (SELECT r.raceId, COUNT(ps.raceId) AS cnt FROM races r LEFT JOIN pitStops ps ON ps.raceId = r.raceId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name NOT IN (SELECT name FROM races WHERE year = 2000) GROUP BY r.raceId)
answer:
The average is 39.71 pit stops per race. It covers 7 of the 2017 races: Chinese, Bahrain, Russian, Azerbaijan, Singapore, Mexican and Abu Dhabi. Their pit stop counts are 82, 31, 20, 63, 82, 0 and 0, which total 278. I used the Race term, which is still a draft in the ontology.

I made two choices where the question was ambiguous:
- **Which races count as "not hosted in 2000":** I matched on race name, so a 2017 race is excluded if a race with the same name was held in 2000. Matching on circuit would give a different set of races.
- **Races with no pit stop data:** The Mexican and Abu Dhabi races have no pit stop rows, so they count as 0 and stay in the average. You asked for the average of all of those races. If you drop them, the average becomes 55.60 over 5 races.

sql: SELECT p.ViewCount, u.DisplayName FROM posts p LEFT JOIN users u ON u.Id = p.LastEditorUserId WHERE p.Title = 'Computer game datasets'
answer: The post 'Computer game datasets' has 1708 views, and its last editor is mbq (user Id 88). I used LastEditorUserId joined to users.DisplayName. The post's own LastEditorDisplayName column is empty.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type='#') SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(m.label='+')/COUNT(*),2) AS carcinogenic_pct, ROUND(100.0*SUM(m.label='-')/COUNT(*),2) AS non_carcinogenic_pct FROM t JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id=t.molecule_id
answer: Of the molecules with at least one triple bond (bond_type '#'), 66.67% are carcinogenic (label '+') and 33.33% are non-carcinogenic (label '-'). I counted each molecule once, even if it has several triple bonds. The query ran and returned these values.

young: 9047, old: 9038. I averaged salary (district.A11) over the distinct branch districts (account.district_id) of accounts held by each cohort's clients. A client holds an account through any disp row, owner or disponent. Young is born 1980-01-01 or later, and old is born before 1920-01-01 (1919 or earlier).

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) AS patient_count FROM Patient P JOIN Laboratory L ON L.ID=P.ID WHERE L.Date BETWEEN '1981-01-01' AND '1986-12-31' AND L.PLT BETWEEN 100 AND 400 AND P.Birthday IS NOT NULL AND CAST((strftime('%Y',L.Date)-strftime('%Y',P.Birthday)) - (strftime('%m-%d',L.Date)<strftime('%m-%d',P.Birthday)) AS INTEGER) < 50 AND L."U-PRO" IN ('1','2','3','4','30','100','300','>=300','>=1000','+1(30)','+2(100)')
answer: 45 patients. Age is completed years on the test date (below 50). The date window, platelet range (100 to 400 inclusive) and proteinuria all come from the same lab record. I counted proteinuria as 30 mg/dl or more: values 30, 100, 300, >=300, >=1000, +1(30), +2(100), and grades 1 to 4 on the older scale. Excluded results: '-', '0', 'TR', '-15', '%%' and nulls. Counting grades 1 and 2 was my choice; restricting to marked proteinuria (grades 3 and 4, 300 or more) would lower the count. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still drafts, not certified. I did not run validate_sql.

sql:
SELECT CASE p.Admission WHEN '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS care_setting,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND l.RNP<>'negative' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>=4) THEN p.ID END) AS with_rnp_ge_4,
COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND l.RNP<>'negative' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>=4) THEN p.ID END) AS without_rnp_ge_4
FROM Patient p WHERE p.SEX='F' AND p.Admission IN ('+','-') AND p.Birthday<='1976-10-09' GROUP BY care_setting ORDER BY care_setting
answer:
Female patients aged 50 or older as of 2026-10-09 (born on or before 1976-10-09):
- Admitted to the hospital: 10 patients with an anti-RNP result of at least 4, 328 without.
- Followed at the outpatient clinic: 11 patients with an anti-RNP result of at least 4, 532 without.

Readings I chose: "no such result" includes patients with no lab rows or only 'negative'/NULL RNP values. RNP is stored as text, so I compared it numerically. Age is computed from Birthday against the given date.

sql:
WITH acc AS (SELECT a.account_id, d.A2 AS dn FROM account a JOIN district d ON d.district_id=a.district_id WHERE d.A3=(SELECT A3 FROM district WHERE A2='Litomerice') AND a.date>='1996-01-01' AND a.date<='1996-12-31'),
bal AS (SELECT acc.account_id, acc.dn, (SELECT t.balance FROM trans t WHERE t.account_id=acc.account_id AND t.date<='1996-12-31' ORDER BY t.date DESC, t.trans_id DESC LIMIT 1) AS b FROM acc),
dist AS (SELECT dn, COUNT(*) AS n, AVG(b) AS av FROM bal GROUP BY dn)
SELECT dn AS district_name, n AS accounts_opened_1996, ROUND(av,2) AS avg_end_1996_balance,
 (SELECT ROUND(AVG(b),2) FROM bal) AS region_avg_end_1996_balance,
 (SELECT dn FROM dist ORDER BY ROUND(av,2) DESC, dn LIMIT 1) AS top_district
FROM dist ORDER BY dn;
answer:
Litomerice belongs to the 'north Bohemia' region. Ten of its districts had accounts opened in 1996. Each row below gives accounts opened in 1996 and the average end-of-1996 balance:
- Ceska Lipa: 18 accounts, 31357.06
- Chomutov: 18, 29084.28
- Decin: 12, 34289.08
- Jablonec n. Nisou: 15, 26449.40
- Liberec: 21, 36765.81
- Litomerice: 9, 27278.67
- Louny: 15, 28686.00
- Most: 12, 31364.25
- Teplice: 15, 35322.07
- Usti nad Labem: 12, 35476.25

The region-wide average across all 147 accounts is 31809.19. Liberec has the highest district average at 36765.81, with no tie.

The query returns the two extra figures as repeated columns on every district row (region_avg_end_1996_balance and top_district), so everything comes back in one result. Every 1996 account had at least one transaction on or before 1996-12-31, so none were dropped. Balances are taken from the last transaction on or before 1996-12-31, using the highest trans_id when several share that date.

sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, c.name FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId JOIN constructors c ON c.constructorId=q.constructorId LEFT JOIN results x ON x.raceId=q.raceId AND x.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND r.year=2017 AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2<>'' ORDER BY q.q2, x.grid LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1
answer: Valtteri Bottas, driving for Mercedes. His Q2 time was 1:35.396, behind Lewis Hamilton's 1:34.660. No tie affected the ranking, so the grid tie-break (results.grid) did not come into play. The Terms I relied on are all draft, not certified. The join to results is not a modeled relationship, but it is on the raceId and driverId keys.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END), 2) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero s JOIN hero_attribute ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id JOIN attribute a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Intelligence' AND ha.attribute_value = (SELECT ha2.attribute_value FROM superhero s2 JOIN hero_attribute ha2 ON ha2.hero_id = s2.id JOIN attribute a2 ON a2.id = ha2.attribute_id WHERE a2.attribute_name = 'Intelligence' AND s2.superhero_name = 'Abomination')
answer: The average weight is 103.6 kg. Abomination's Intelligence is 85, and 140 heroes have that score (Abomination is one of them). I left out heroes whose weight is 0 or missing, because the earlier verified queries treat those as unknown. I included Abomination in the cohort. The query returns 103.6, which is 103.60 at two decimals.

sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(DOCType='Unified School District') AS REAL) / SUM(DOCType='Elementary School District') AS ratio FROM schools WHERE County='Orange' AND StatusType='Merged'
answer: The ratio of merged Unified School District schools to merged Elementary School District schools in Orange County is about 0.5714 (4 to 7, inferred from the ratio rather than printed). I read "merged" as StatusType = 'Merged' and the ratio as Unified divided by Elementary. I ran the query but skipped validate_sql, and the School Term it relies on is still a draft.

sql: WITH q AS (SELECT CustomerID, SUM(Consumption) AS t FROM yearmonth WHERE Date BETWEEN '201304' AND '201306' GROUP BY CustomerID) SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN c.Currency='EUR' THEN q.t END),2) AS eur_avg, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN c.Currency='CZK' THEN q.t END),2) AS czk_avg FROM q JOIN customers c ON c.CustomerID=q.CustomerID
answer: 2013년 2분기(4~6월) 고객당 평균 연료 소비량은 EUR 고객 3,627.03, CZK 고객 44,462.45입니다. 고객별로 4~6월 소비량을 합산한 뒤 계정 통화(customers.Currency)별로 평균을 냈습니다. 이 기간에 yearmonth 행이 하나라도 있는 고객을 '소비량이 기록된 고객'으로 해석했습니다. 소비량이 0보다 큰 고객만 포함하면 EUR 3,637.21, CZK 44,499.29로 조금 달라집니다. 사용한 Customer, Monthly Customer Consumption 용어는 아직 인증되지 않은 draft 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT AVG(s.height_cm) AS avg_height_cm FROM superhero s WHERE s.publisher_id=(SELECT id FROM publisher WHERE publisher_name='Marvel Comics') AND s.height_cm>0 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id=s.id AND hp.power_id NOT IN (SELECT hp2.power_id FROM hero_power hp2 JOIN superhero d ON d.id=hp2.hero_id WHERE d.publisher_id=(SELECT id FROM publisher WHERE publisher_name='DC Comics')))
answer: 약 202.6cm입니다. 해당하는 Marvel Comics 캐릭터는 39명입니다. 키가 NULL이거나 0인 경우는 측정값이 없는 것으로 보고 제외했습니다. DC Comics 캐릭터가 한 명도 가지고 있지 않은 능력을 하나 이상 가진 Marvel 캐릭터만 계산했습니다.

Lewis Hamilton set the fastest Q3 time among British drivers born after 1980: 1:04.424 at the 2017 Austrian Grand Prix. No other result tied it. I read "British" as drivers.nationality = 'British' and "born after 1980" as birth year > 1980. I excluded blank and NULL Q3 values. Clean Q3 strings compare correctly as text.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN g=1 THEN c END),2) AS avg_officer_events, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN g=0 THEN c END),2) AS avg_other_events FROM (SELECT m.member_id, m.position IN ('President','Vice President','Secretary','Treasurer') AS g, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_event) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_member=m.member_id) AS c FROM member m)
answer: Officers attended an average of 14.50 events each, and other students attended an average of 9.24. The 4 officers are the President, Vice President, Secretary and Treasurer. The other 29 members are 26 with position 'Member' and 3 'Inactive', and I counted the Inactive ones as other students because you said everyone else counts. Members with no attendance are included with 0 events, and all events are counted with no date cutoff.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN CAST(STRFTIME('%Y', Birthday) AS INTEGER) >= 1960 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS percentage FROM Patient WHERE LOWER(Diagnosis) LIKE '%psoriatic arthritis%'
answer: 50.0% of psoriatic arthritis patients were born in 1960 or later (1 of the 2 such patients in the registry). I matched the diagnosis case-insensitively because it is stored in two spellings, and I used the birth year from Birthday, counting 1960 itself. The denominator is all psoriatic arthritis patients, with no other filter. The Patient term is still draft (not certified). I did not run validate_sql before run_sql.

sql: SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS driver_name, r.name AS race_name, r.year AS race_year, q.q3 AS q3_time FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId = q.raceId WHERE d.nationality = 'British' AND CAST(STRFTIME('%Y', d.dob) AS INTEGER) > 1980 AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(q.q3) <> '' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying q2 JOIN drivers d2 ON d2.driverId = q2.driverId WHERE d2.nationality = 'British' AND CAST(STRFTIME('%Y', d2.dob) AS INTEGER) > 1980 AND q2.q3 IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(q2.q3) <> '')
answer: Lewis Hamilton set the fastest Q3 time among British drivers born after 1980: 1:04.424 at the 2017 Austrian Grand Prix. Only one row came back, so there was no tie. I read "British" as drivers.nationality = 'British' and "born after 1980" as a birth year greater than 1980. Blank Q3 values are excluded. I did not run validate_sql, and the Driver, Qualifying Result and Race terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql:
SELECT m.department AS department_name,
       COUNT(DISTINCT m.major_id) AS majors_offered,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN mem.member_id IS NOT NULL THEN m.major_id END) AS majors_held,
       ROUND(CAST(COUNT(mem.member_id) AS REAL) / COUNT(DISTINCT m.major_id), 2) AS avg_members_per_major
FROM major m
LEFT JOIN member mem ON mem.link_to_major = m.major_id
WHERE m.department IN (SELECT department FROM major WHERE college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences')
GROUP BY m.department
ORDER BY m.department
answer:
11 departments in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences. I read "the majors it offers" and "the majors held" as counts, and the average as member count divided by majors offered. I ran the query and it returns these rows. No department spans more than one college, so the "any of its majors" rule changes nothing.

Columns: department, majors offered, majors held by at least one member, average members per major.

- Aerospace Studies Program: 1 offered, 0 held, 0.00
- Asian Studies Program: 1, 0, 0.00
- English Department: 2, 0, 0.00
- History Department: 1, 0, 0.00
- Journalism and Communication Department: 1, 0, 0.00
- Languages, Philosophy and Communication Studies Department: 8, 3, 0.38
- Liberal Arts Program: 1, 1, 1.00
- Military Science Program: 1, 0, 0.00
- Political Science Department: 3, 2, 1.00
- Religious Studies Program: 1, 0, 0.00
- Sociology, Social Work and Anthropology Department: 4, 0, 0.00

Membership comes from each member's major in the member records. One member has no major recorded, so that member is not counted anywhere. Departments are listed alphabetically.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT f.language) AS foreign_languages FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Swamp'
answer: Swamp has been printed in 11 foreign languages: German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian, Chinese Simplified, Chinese Traditional and Phyrexian. I counted only cards named exactly 'Swamp', so Snow-Covered Swamp is not included. I counted Phyrexian because it appears as a language in the data. Without it the count is 10. sql: SELECT e.event_name, e.event_date, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(b.amount) FROM budget b WHERE b.link_to_event=e.event_id),0) AS total_budgeted, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event=e.event_id) AS attendees FROM event e ORDER BY e.event_name, e.event_date
answer: 쿼리는 이벤트 42건을 모두 한 줄씩 반환합니다. 예산이나 참석 기록이 없는 이벤트도 빠지지 않고 0으로 표시됩니다. 예산은 이벤트별 budget.amount 합계이고, 참석자 수는 attendance의 서로 다른 회원 수입니다. 예산과 참석 기록을 각각 별도 하위 쿼리로 집계해 두 표를 함께 조인할 때 생기는 중복 계산을 피했습니다. event_date는 원본 형식(예: 2020-03-10T12:00:00) 그대로 출력합니다. 같은 이름의 이벤트(Community Theater, Football game, Laugh Out Loud)는 날짜가 달라 별도 행으로 나옵니다. 실행해서 결과를 확인했습니다.

sql:
WITH RECURSIVE over_events AS (SELECT DISTINCT link_to_event AS event_id FROM budget WHERE link_to_event IS NOT NULL AND amount - spent < 0),
split AS (SELECT x.expense_id, '' AS item, x.expense_description || ',' AS rest FROM expense x JOIN budget b ON b.budget_id = x.link_to_budget WHERE b.link_to_event IN (SELECT event_id FROM over_events)
UNION ALL SELECT expense_id, TRIM(SUBSTR(rest, 1, INSTR(rest, ',') - 1)), SUBSTR(rest, INSTR(rest, ',') + 1) FROM split WHERE rest <> '')
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT LOWER(item)) AS distinct_items FROM split WHERE item <> ''
answer: 7 different kinds of items. I counted an event as over budget if any of its budget lines has amount minus spent below zero. I took every expense booked to those events, in any category, and split each comma-separated description into separate items. I counted distinct items ignoring case. Events in the records run from 2019-09-01 to 2020-05-05, so I applied no date filter and treated the whole span as "the semester".

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE SEX = 'F' AND Admission = '+' AND "First Date" BETWEEN '1998-01-01' AND '1998-12-31'
answer: 13 female patients. I read "admitted to the hospital" as Admission = '+', the wiki's standard reading. If the 3 malformed '+(' rows were also counted as admitted, the count would be 16. Patients with no sex recorded (empty string) or no First Date are excluded.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) FROM cards AS c JOIN foreign_data AS f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.isStorySpotlight = 1 AND f.language = 'French') / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE isStorySpotlight = 1), 0), 2) AS percentage
answer: 83.65% of Story Spotlight card printings have a French translation. I counted a printing as translated if foreign_data has a row with language 'French' for its uuid. The denominator is all cards with isStorySpotlight = 1. I skipped validate_sql and ran the query directly. The Card and Card Foreign Data terms it relies on are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS driver_full_name, ps.duration AS pit_stop_time, r.name AS race_name, c.name AS circuit_name, c.location AS circuit_location FROM pitStops ps JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = ps.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId = ps.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId = r.circuitId WHERE r.date >= '2016-09-01' AND r.date < '2016-10-01' AND ps.milliseconds = (SELECT MIN(ps2.milliseconds) FROM pitStops ps2 JOIN races r2 ON r2.raceId = ps2.raceId WHERE r2.date >= '2016-09-01' AND r2.date < '2016-10-01') ORDER BY driver_full_name
answer: Two pit stops tie for the fastest in September 2016, both at 23.633 seconds in the Italian Grand Prix at Autodromo Nazionale di Monza (location: Monza): Daniel Ricciardo and Lewis Hamilton. I treated "held in September 2016" as the race date falling in that month, and compared pit stops by milliseconds so the tie is exact. The Terms used (Pit Stop, Driver, Race, Circuit) are still draft in the ontology, not certified.

sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, strftime('%H:%M:%f', r.time, '+' || (res.milliseconds/1000.0) || ' seconds') AS finish_local_time, d.url FROM races r JOIN results res ON res.raceId=r.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=res.driverId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Azerbaijan Grand Prix' AND res.positionOrder=1
answer:
Daniel Ricciardo won the 2017 Azerbaijan Grand Prix. He crossed the finish line at 15:03:55.573 local circuit time. His page is http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Ricciardo.

I computed the finish time as the scheduled local start time (races.time, 13:00:00) plus his race time (7,435,573 ms, or 2:03:55.573). The database has no recorded finish clock time. This assumes the race started exactly on schedule, and any red-flag delay or late start would shift the real clock time. The result relies on draft (not yet certified) Terms: Driver, Race and Race Result.

sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId=r.circuitId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE c.name='Marina Bay Street Circuit' AND r.year=2008 AND q.q3<>'' ORDER BY q.q3 LIMIT 1
answer: Felipe Massa, with a Q3 time of 1:44.801 at the 2008 Singapore Grand Prix. I read "fastest" as the smallest non-empty Q3 time. The time strings sort correctly as text because they all share the same m:ss.mmm format.

sql: select count(distinct ra.raceId) from results r join races ra using(raceId) where ra.name='Canadian Grand Prix' and r.statusId=3

sql: SELECT e.event_name, e.event_date, COALESCE(b.total_budget, 0) AS total_budgeted, COALESCE(a.members, 0) AS members_attended FROM event AS e LEFT JOIN (SELECT link_to_event, SUM(amount) AS total_budget FROM budget GROUP BY link_to_event) AS b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT link_to_event, COUNT(DISTINCT link_to_member) AS members FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event) AS a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id ORDER BY e.event_name ASC, e.event_date ASC
answer:
The query returns all 42 events with event name, event date, total budgeted amount and number of members who attended, sorted by name and then date. I ran it and checked the rows.

I made two choices where the question was open:
- **Events with no data:** every event is listed. An event with no budget lines shows 0 for the budget, and an event with no attendance rows shows 0 attendees. Many events fall into this group, for example Baseball game has 0 budget and 0 attendees.
- **How the totals are computed:** budget is the sum of `budget.amount` per event, and attendance is the count of distinct members per event. Each is computed in its own subquery, so the two totals don't multiply each other.

Event dates appear as stored, for example `2020-04-07T12:00:00`. The Budget and Event terms are still drafts in the ontology and haven't been certified.

sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name='Yearly Kickoff' THEN b.amount END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_name='October Meeting' THEN b.amount END) AS ratio FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id=b.link_to_event WHERE b.category='Advertisement'
answer: 비율은 약 2.727입니다. Yearly Kickoff의 Advertisement 예산은 150, October Meeting은 55이고, 150/55로 계산했습니다. 이름이 정확히 일치하는 이벤트만 사용했으며, 'October Speaker'(75)는 제외했습니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN u.Reputation < 1000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_not_high_reputation FROM posts p JOIN users u ON u.Id = p.OwnerUserId WHERE p.CreaionDate >= '2010-01-01' AND p.CreaionDate < '2011-01-01' AND p.Score > 5
answer: 2010년에 작성되고 점수가 5 초과인 게시물 중 30.73%가 평판 1000 미만 사용자의 글입니다. 작성일 컬럼은 이 DB에서 철자가 `CreaionDate`로 되어 있어 그대로 사용했습니다. 해당 게시물은 모두 소유자가 users 테이블에 있어서, 소유자가 없는 글은 계산에서 빠진 것이 없습니다. 평판 1000 이상만 고평판으로 계산했습니다.

sql:
WITH g AS (
 SELECT DISTINCT d.account_id FROM disp d JOIN card c ON c.disp_id=d.disp_id
 JOIN account a ON a.account_id=d.account_id JOIN district di ON di.district_id=a.district_id
 WHERE d.type='OWNER' AND c.type='gold' AND CAST(di.A4 AS INTEGER)>=250000),
p AS (
 SELECT t.bank AS bank, t.account AS account, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(t.amount) AS total
 FROM trans t JOIN g ON g.account_id=t.account_id
 WHERE t.type='VYDAJ' AND t.date>='1998-01-01' AND t.date<'1999-01-01'
   AND t.bank IS NOT NULL AND t.account>0
 GROUP BY t.bank, t.account)
SELECT bank, account, n, total FROM p WHERE total=(SELECT MAX(total) FROM p) ORDER BY bank, account;
answer:
In 1998, the largest recipient pair for gold-card owners' accounts at branches in districts with at least 250,000 inhabitants is bank AB, counter-account 44119823. It received 12 outgoing payments totaling 108,408. No other pair tied for that total, so the query returns one row.

I read "ranking... if two tie for the largest total, list both" as asking for the top total only, with ties included. I did not list every pair. If you want the full ranked list, remove the `WHERE total=(SELECT MAX(total) FROM p)` filter and add `ORDER BY total DESC`.

Other choices I made:
- **Gold card owners:** the account's OWNER disposition has a gold card. Each account is counted once.
- **Large district:** the account's branch district has `CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) >= 250000`.
- **Outgoing payments:** type VYDAJ, dated 1998-01-01 through 1998-12-31.
- **Pairs:** only transfers to another bank are counted, meaning rows with a bank and an account number greater than 0. Payments without a counter-account, such as cash, are excluded.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.account_id) FROM account a JOIN loan l ON l.account_id = a.account_id WHERE a.district_id = 1 AND a.date <= '1995-12-31' AND l.status IN ('C','D')

SELECT COUNT(*) FROM account a JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id WHERE d.A3 = 'north Bohemia' AND a.date <= '1995-12-31' AND a.account_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT account_id FROM trans WHERE bank = 'AB')
answer: 32. Reading used: "based in North Bohemia" means the account's branch district (account.district_id) has region A3 = 'north Bohemia'. "As of the end of 1995" means the account was opened on or before 1995-12-31. The AB transaction can fall at any date, since the question says "at some point in their history". Bank AB is trans.bank = 'AB'. The Account, District and Transaction terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(Consumption), 2) AS avg_monthly_fuel_consumption FROM yearmonth WHERE CustomerID = 15621 AND Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312' AND Consumption > 0
answer: Customer 15621's average fuel consumption in 2013 was 6.02 per month. It is the mean of the monthly Consumption values in `yearmonth`, counting only months with Consumption > 0. The data ends at 201311, so 2013 covers January to November. The query uses the draft (not yet certified) Term "Monthly Customer Consumption". I ran the query but skipped the separate validate_sql step.

sql: SELECT p.Birthday FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.GPT < 60 AND p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE CAST(RNP AS REAL) >= 16) GROUP BY p.ID ORDER BY MAX(l.GPT) DESC, p.ID LIMIT 3
answer:
The three Birthdays, in rank order, are 1949-05-11 (patient 5186147, highest normal GPT 59), 1958-10-23 (patient 2320830, GPT 57) and 1963-12-13 (patient 5184284, GPT 57). Patients 2320830 and 5184284 tie at 57, so the smaller ID comes first.

I read "ever had an anti-ribonuclear protein result of 16 or higher" as RNP, cast to a number, being 16 or more on at least one test. The RNP column holds text, and 'negative' casts to 0, so it never qualifies. For "normal range", I took each patient's highest GPT among only their tests with GPT below 60. I did not require every one of their GPT tests to be normal.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT t.team_long_name FROM Team_Attributes ta JOIN Team t ON t.team_api_id = ta.team_api_id WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', ta.date) = '2012' AND ta.buildUpPlayPassing > (SELECT AVG(buildUpPlayPassing) FROM Team_Attributes WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012')
answer: The query returns the distinct long names of teams with a 2012 snapshot whose buildUpPlayPassing is above the 2012 average across all team snapshots dated in 2012. The result begins Aberdeen, AC Ajaccio, Milan, UD Almería and so on. I only saw the first 100 rows because the display truncated, so I don't know the total count. I skipped the verified-query and validate_sql steps and ran the SQL directly. The Team and Team Attributes Terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.driverId) FROM results r JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId=r.raceId JOIN status s ON s.statusId=r.statusId WHERE ra.year=1962 AND ra.name='British Grand Prix' AND s.status='Withdrew'
answer: 5 drivers withdrew from the 1962 British Grand Prix. I read "withdrew" as results rows with status 'Withdrew', the only withdrawal status in the data. The check query returned 5 rows with that status. The final query counts distinct drivers, and I did not run it separately. The Race and Race Result Status terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.nationality n, CAST(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60+CAST(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1) AS REAL) s FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE r.year=1995 AND r.name='Japanese Grand Prix' AND q.q1 IS NOT NULL AND q.q1<>'') SELECT n AS nationality FROM t WHERE s=(SELECT MAX(s) FROM t)
answer: British. The slowest Q1 time at the 1995 Japanese Grand Prix was 16:42.640, set by one British driver, so there is no tie. That time looks unusual, but it is what the data records. I compared times numerically in seconds, because a plain text sort would rank "16:42.640" as faster than "1:48.289". If that 16:42.640 entry is treated as bad data and excluded, the slowest time would be 1:48.289 and the nationality would be Belgian. I kept the entry because the question asks for the slowest recorded time.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) FROM cards c JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid = c.uuid AND l.format = 'commander' AND l.status = 'Legal' WHERE c.manaCost = '{0}'

sql:
WITH avgbal AS (SELECT account_id, AVG(balance) ab FROM trans GROUP BY account_id),
h AS (SELECT DISTINCT cl.gender, a.district_id FROM card c JOIN disp d ON c.disp_id=d.disp_id JOIN client cl ON cl.client_id=d.client_id JOIN account a ON a.account_id=d.account_id JOIN avgbal b ON b.account_id=a.account_id WHERE c.type='gold' AND b.ab>1000),
dd AS (SELECT h.gender, di.* FROM h JOIN district di ON di.district_id=h.district_id WHERE CAST(di.A4 AS INTEGER)>100000),
st AS (SELECT gender, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(A11),2) s, ROUND(AVG(A10),2) u, MAX(CAST(A4 AS INTEGER)) mx FROM dd GROUP BY gender)
SELECT st.n AS district_count, dd.A2 AS most_populous_district, CAST(dd.A4 AS INTEGER) AS inhabitants, st.s AS avg_salary, st.u AS avg_urban_ratio
FROM st JOIN dd ON dd.gender=st.gender AND CAST(dd.A4 AS INTEGER)=st.mx
ORDER BY CASE st.gender WHEN 'F' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, dd.A2;
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 확인했습니다. 결과는 두 행이며, 첫 행이 여성, 둘째 행이 남성입니다. 요청하신 열만 넣어 성별 열은 없습니다.

- 여성: 지점 district 16개, 인구가 가장 많은 district는 Hl.m. Praha(1,204,953명), 평균 급여 9245.44, 도시 인구 비율 평균 69.16.
- 남성: 지점 district 22개, 인구가 가장 많은 district는 Hl.m. Praha(1,204,953명), 평균 급여 9347.86, 도시 인구 비율 평균 71.03.

두 성별 모두 최다 인구 district가 하나여서 동률 행은 없었습니다.

해석한 기준은 다음과 같습니다.
- 골드카드 보유자의 성별은 카드가 연결된 disp의 고객(client) 기준입니다.
- 계좌 평균 잔액은 해당 계좌 모든 거래의 거래 후 잔액(trans.balance) 평균이며, 1,000 초과만 포함했습니다.
- district는 계좌의 지점 district(account.district_id)이고 인구는 A4(텍스트라 숫자로 변환)가 100,000 초과인 곳만 남겼습니다.
- 성별별로 district를 중복 없이 센 뒤 평균을 냈습니다. 급여는 A11, 도시 인구 비율은 A10(퍼센트 값)입니다.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.County, s.District, s.City, f."Enrollment (K-12)", f."FRPM Count (K-12)", f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)", t.NumTstTakr, t.AvgScrRead, t.AvgScrMath, t.AvgScrWrite, t.NumGE1500 FROM schools s LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE CAST(s.CDSCode AS INTEGER) = 1612590137943

sql: SELECT a.element AS element, SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM connected c JOIN bond b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id WHERE (c.atom_id = a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a.atom_id) AND b.bond_type = '-') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM connected c JOIN bond b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id WHERE (c.atom_id = a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a.atom_id) AND b.bond_type <> '-') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS saturated_atom_count FROM atom a GROUP BY a.element ORDER BY a.element
answer: 18 rows, one per element, sorted alphabetically. An atom counts if it has at least one bond and all its bonds are single. Atoms with no bonds are excluded. Elements with no such atoms are kept with 0 (ca, k, na, y, zn); add HAVING saturated_atom_count > 0 to drop them. Counts: br 46, c 1142, ca 0, cl 314, cu 2, f 10, h 4033, i 3, k 0, n 243, na 0, o 441, p 22, pb 1, s 35, sn 2, y 0, zn 0. The Atom and Bond terms used are still drafts, not certified.
