sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.event_name, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event = e.event_id) AS n FROM event e), w AS (SELECT n FROM c WHERE event_name = 'Women''s Soccer'), f AS (SELECT ROUND(AVG(c.n), 1) AS avg_n FROM c JOIN event e ON e.event_id = c.event_id WHERE e.event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND e.event_date < '2019-12-01')
SELECT w.n AS womens_soccer_attendees, f.avg_n AS avg_fall_2019_attendees, CASE WHEN w.n > f.avg_n THEN 'more' WHEN w.n < f.avg_n THEN 'fewer' ELSE 'equal' END AS verdict FROM w CROSS JOIN f
answer: 17 students attended Women's Soccer, against a fall 2019 average of 16.1 per event, so the verdict is 'more'. The average covers events from 2019-09-01 through 2019-11-30 and includes events with zero attendees. Attendance is the count of distinct members per event. The Event term is a draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverId) FROM results r JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=r.driverId WHERE r.rank=2 AND d.dob >= '1976-01-01'
answer: 25 drivers born on or after 1 January 1976 have a second-fastest lap of a race in the data. I read "second-fastest lap" as results.rank = 2 and counted each driver once. The Driver and Race Result terms are still drafts in the ontology.

sql:
SELECT r.date AS date, d.forename AS forename, d.surname AS surname, x.fastestLapTime AS fastest_lap_time
FROM races r
LEFT JOIN results x ON x.raceId = r.raceId AND x.fastestLapTime IS NOT NULL
  AND (CAST(substr(x.fastestLapTime,1,instr(x.fastestLapTime,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60 + CAST(substr(x.fastestLapTime,instr(x.fastestLapTime,':')+1) AS REAL)) > 90
LEFT JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = x.driverId
WHERE r.name = 'French Grand Prix' AND r.year >= 1990
ORDER BY r.date, d.surname, d.forename
answer: No driver in any edition set a race fastest lap slower than 90 seconds, so the query returns 19 rows, one per edition from 1990-07-08 to 2008-06-22, each with empty forename, surname and lap time. The most recent edition in the data is 2008. I used results.fastestLapTime (m:ss.mmm) as the driver's fastest lap of the race and converted it to seconds to compare with 90. That column is only filled for 2004 onward. The slowest values are 1:19.659 (2004), 1:21.451 (2005), 1:21.663 (2006), 1:18.955 (2007) and 1:20.876 (2008). All of these are well under 90 seconds. For 1990 to 2003 the column is empty, so those editions also show no driver.

sql: SELECT d.driverRef, d.nationality, d.dob FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId = q.raceId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 IS NOT NULL AND q.q2 <> '' AND (q.q3 IS NULL OR q.q3 = '')
answer: 5 drivers set a Q2 time but no Q3 time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix: perez (Mexican, 1990-01-26), hulkenberg (German, 1987-08-19), alonso (Spanish, 1981-07-29), kvyat (Russian, 1994-04-26) and sainz (Spanish, 1994-09-01). I read "completed Q2 but did not reach Q3" as a non-empty Q2 time and an empty Q3 time in the qualifying table.

sql: SELECT Diagnosis FROM Patient WHERE Admission LIKE '+%' AND "First Date" BETWEEN '1998-02-15' AND '1998-02-28' ORDER BY Birthday ASC, ID ASC LIMIT 1
answer:
The diagnosis is "WG" and "SJS" separated by a control character (stored bytes 57 47 1D 53 4A 53). It belongs to patient 5765821, born 1938-01-05, first seen 1998-02-27.

Two choices affect this result:
- **Inpatient:** I counted any Admission value that starts with '+'. Patients 5765821 and 5766000 have the malformed value '+(' instead of '+', and I treated it as a typo for '+'. If '+(' were excluded, the oldest inpatient would be patient 5761409 (born 1985), with diagnosis BEHCET.
- **Oldest:** I used the earliest Birthday as the oldest, with the smaller ID breaking ties. There was no tie here.

sql:
WITH c AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.position IN ('President','Vice President','Secretary','Treasurer') AS officer, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_event) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_member=m.member_id) AS n FROM member m)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN officer=1 THEN n END),2) AS avg_officer_events, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN officer=0 THEN n END),2) AS avg_other_events FROM c
answer: Officers attended 14.50 events on average, and other students attended 9.24. Officers are the 4 members whose position is President, Vice President, Secretary or Treasurer. The other 29 members (26 'Member' and 3 'Inactive') count as other students. Each average covers every member of its group, including members with no attendance (counted as 0). All events are included, with no date cutoff. Attendance has no duplicate member/event rows, so each row is one event attended.

sql: SELECT da.A2 FROM client c JOIN disp d ON d.client_id = c.client_id JOIN account a ON a.account_id = d.account_id JOIN district da ON da.district_id = a.district_id WHERE c.gender = 'F' AND c.birth_date = '1976-01-29'
answer: Tachov. Only one female client has that birth date (client 3339, owner of account 2766). I used the district recorded on the account, which is where it was opened. Her own registered district is also Tachov, so both readings give the same answer.

sql: SELECT frameVersion AS frame_version, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards x WHERE x.frameVersion=c.frameVersion) AS card_count FROM cards c WHERE convertedManaCost=0 AND CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER)=frameVersion GROUP BY frameVersion HAVING CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER)=(SELECT MAX(CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER)) FROM cards WHERE convertedManaCost=0 AND CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER)=frameVersion)
answer: The newest frame version among zero-cost cards is 2015, and 25,500 cards in the whole database use it. I read "newest" as the latest year. Eight zero-cost cards have the non-year value 'future', and I excluded them from the ranking because it isn't a year.

sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, l.Date, l."U-PRO" AS proteinuria FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l."U-PRO" IS NOT NULL AND l.Date = (SELECT MAX(l2.Date) FROM Laboratory l2 WHERE l2.ID = p.ID AND l2."U-PRO" IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY p.ID
answer: One row per patient with a recorded proteinuria test (non-null Laboratory."U-PRO"): ID, SEX, date of the latest such test, and the raw U-PRO value at that date ('-', 'TR', '0', '30', '>=300', etc.). Lab rows with null U-PRO are treated as no proteinuria test. Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still drafts. I only inspected the first 5 result rows, so I haven't checked the total row count.

sql: WITH w AS (SELECT d.driverId, d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS full_name, d.nationality, d.dob FROM drivers d WHERE d.driverId IN (SELECT driverId FROM results WHERE positionOrder = 1)), top AS (SELECT * FROM w ORDER BY dob ASC, full_name ASC LIMIT 1), fw AS (SELECT r.name, r.date FROM results rs JOIN races r ON r.raceId = rs.raceId JOIN top ON top.driverId = rs.driverId WHERE rs.positionOrder = 1 ORDER BY r.date ASC, r.name ASC LIMIT 1) SELECT top.full_name, top.nationality, fw.name AS first_win_race_name, fw.date AS first_win_date, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT raceId) FROM results WHERE driverId = top.driverId) AS races_started FROM top, fw
answer: Luigi Fagioli, Italian. His first win was the French Grand Prix on 1951-07-01, and he started 7 races in his career. A win is results.positionOrder = 1, and races started is the count of distinct races with a results row for him. The Driver, Race and Race Result Terms used are draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.EILName FROM schools AS s INNER JOIN frpm AS f ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode WHERE CAST(s.CDSCode AS INTEGER) = 1612590136051 AND s.County = 'Alameda' AND f.`NSLP Provision Status` = 'Breakfast Provision 2'
answer: The school is Oakland Technical High, and its educational instruction level name is High School. The CDS code is stored with a leading zero (01612590136051), so I matched it by casting to an integer. I also checked that the school is in Alameda County and has Breakfast Provision 2 status, and both hold. The query returns one row.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(l.TP-8.5),3) AS avg_tp_deviation FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID=l.ID WHERE p.SEX='F' AND l.TP>8.5 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID=p.ID AND e.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' AND e.Diagnosis NOT LIKE '%SLE susp%')
answer: 0.156. Female patients with an SLE examination visit are counted, and all of their lab records with TP > 8.5 are averaged as TP − 8.5. I read "SLE" as any examination diagnosis containing SLE, including "SLE, SjS" and "JRA->SLE". I excluded "SLE susp", which means suspected only. I applied SLE at patient level (any SLE exam visit), not matched by date to each lab record.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM Patient p WHERE p.Birthday > '1980-01-01' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND (l.FG < 150 OR l.FG > 450 OR l."U-PRO" IN ('3','4','300','>=300','>=1000','%%')))
answer: 4 patients. Readings used: born after 1980-01-01 means Birthday > '1980-01-01', so 1980-01-01 itself is excluded. Fibrinogen is abnormal when FG < 150 or FG > 450, and NULL results are ignored. Severe proteinuria is U-PRO of '3' or '4' (dipstick 3+/4+), '300', '>=300', '>=1000', or '%%' (saturated strip, strongest reading). Trace, '1', '2', '30', '100', '+1(30)' and '+2(100)' are not counted. Plain '3' and '4' are read as dipstick grades, as you described, not as 3 or 4 mg/dL. Each patient is counted once.

sql: SELECT AVG(n) FROM (SELECT b.molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM bond b JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '+' AND b.bond_type = '-' GROUP BY b.molecule_id)
answer: The average is 20.25 single bonds per carcinogenic molecule. It covers 152 molecules, and I did not round the result. I read "carcinogenic" as label '+' and "single bond" as bond_type '-', which is how the verified queries use them. Only molecules with at least one single bond are counted.

sql: WITH p AS (SELECT b.bond_id, b.bond_type, MIN(a1.element,a2.element) e1, MAX(a1.element,a2.element) e2 FROM bond b JOIN connected c ON c.bond_id=b.bond_id JOIN atom a1 ON a1.atom_id=c.atom_id JOIN atom a2 ON a2.atom_id=c.atom_id2 WHERE b.molecule_id='TR377' AND b.bond_type IN ('-','=') GROUP BY b.bond_id) SELECT p.bond_type, COUNT(DISTINCT p.bond_id) AS bond_count, COUNT(DISTINCT p.e1||'|'||p.e2) AS pair_count, (SELECT label FROM molecule WHERE molecule_id='TR377') AS label FROM p GROUP BY p.bond_type ORDER BY bond_count DESC, p.bond_type
answer: TR377 has 12 single bonds ('-'), which join 3 distinct element pairs, and 4 double bonds ('='), which join 1 element pair. The molecule's label is '-', meaning non-carcinogenic. I counted "element pairs" as distinct unordered element combinations, so c–h and h–c count as one pair. Bonds are counted once each, even though the connected table stores every bond in both directions.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT t.team_long_name FROM Team_Attributes ta JOIN Team t ON t.team_api_id=ta.team_api_id WHERE ta.date LIKE '2012%' AND ta.buildUpPlayPassing > (SELECT AVG(buildUpPlayPassing) FROM Team_Attributes WHERE date LIKE '2012%') ORDER BY 1
answer: 128 teams have a 2012 attribute record whose buildUpPlayPassing is above the 2012 average. I took the average across all 242 attribute records dated in 2012 (none have a null passing value). I returned distinct team long names, sorted alphabetically.

sql: SELECT SOCType AS "School Type", School, Latitude FROM schools WHERE Latitude IS NOT NULL AND (SOCType IN ('Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public)','Junior High Schools (Public)') OR School LIKE '%Middle%') AND Latitude = (SELECT MAX(Latitude) FROM schools WHERE Latitude IS NOT NULL AND (SOCType IN ('Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public)','Junior High Schools (Public)') OR School LIKE '%Middle%'))
answer: Crescent Elk Middle, type "Intermediate/Middle Schools (Public)", latitude 41.756316 (active). No tie. I counted a school as middle if its type is Intermediate/Middle or Junior High, or its name contains 'Middle', and I included open and closed schools. The data came from the schools table, whose SOCType holds the same text as the 'School Type' field.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM satscores WHERE rtype='S' AND cname='Contra Costa' AND NumTstTakr > (SELECT NumTstTakr FROM satscores WHERE cds='07618040730051')
answer: 1 school in Contra Costa County had more SAT test takers than school 7618040730051 (435 test takers). I counted school-level rows only, excluding the district-level rows. The CDS code is stored with a leading zero (07618040730051).

sql: WITH a AS (SELECT a.account_id, a.district_id, strftime('%Y',a.date) y, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(amount) FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=a.account_id),0) amt FROM account a JOIN district d ON d.district_id=a.district_id WHERE d.A3='central Bohemia' AND a.date>='1996-01-01'), pd AS (SELECT y, district_id, COUNT(*) n, SUM(amt) s FROM a GROUP BY y, district_id) SELECT y AS account_year, SUM(n) AS accounts_opened, SUM(s) AS total_lent, ROUND(AVG(1.0*s/n),2) AS avg_lent_per_account_across_districts FROM pd GROUP BY y ORDER BY y
answer:
중부 보헤미아(central Bohemia)에서 1996-01-01 이후 개설된 계좌는 두 해에 걸쳐 있습니다.
- 1996년: 계좌 191개, 총 대출액 4,887,024, 지역별 계좌당 대출액 평균 23,639.03
- 1997년: 계좌 114개, 총 대출액 1,971,468, 지역별 계좌당 대출액 평균 19,809.53

적용한 해석은 다음과 같습니다.
- 대출은 대출 실행일이 아니라 계좌 개설 연도 기준으로 묶었습니다.
- 대출이 없는 계좌는 0으로 계산했습니다.
- 계좌당 대출액은 district별로 (그 district의 총 대출액 ÷ 개설 계좌 수)를 구한 뒤 district 간 단순 평균을 냈습니다. 해당 연도에 개설 계좌가 없는 district는 평균에서 제외했습니다.

sql:
WITH sc AS (SELECT * FROM schools WHERE County IN ('Amador','Madera')),
nm AS (SELECT CDSCode, AdmFName1 AS fn FROM sc UNION SELECT CDSCode, AdmFName2 FROM sc UNION SELECT CDSCode, AdmFName3 FROM sc),
top2 AS (SELECT fn FROM nm WHERE fn IS NOT NULL AND fn <> '' GROUP BY fn ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, fn LIMIT 2),
d AS (SELECT DISTINCT County, District FROM sc WHERE DOCType IN ('Unified School District','Elementary School District','High School District','County Office of Education (COE)'))
SELECT d.District AS district_name, t.fn AS first_name,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM sc JOIN nm ON nm.CDSCode=sc.CDSCode AND nm.fn=t.fn WHERE sc.County=d.County AND sc.District=d.District) AS school_count
FROM d CROSS JOIN top2 t ORDER BY d.District, t.fn
answer:
The two names are Stacy (8 schools) and Avetik (4 schools). Avetik ranks second because it ties with Gary and Kuljeet at 4, and it comes first alphabetically. The query returns 48 rows, 24 districts times 2 names. Nearly all are zero. Stacy has 8 schools in Yosemite Unified, and Avetik has 4 in Madera County Office of Education.

Readings I chose:
- A school counts once per name even if the name appears in more than one of its three administrator slots.
- Blank or missing first names are not treated as a name.
- Ranking uses every school record in the two counties, whatever its status, including closed ones. Per-district counts use the same records.
- Districts are matched by county and district name, using only the four public district types you listed.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT l.ID) FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE (p.Description IS NULL OR TRIM(p.Description) = '') AND (l.CRP LIKE '+%' OR l.CRP GLOB '[2-9]+*')
answer: 26 distinct patients. I read "positive CRP" as the qualitative plus grades in Laboratory.CRP ('+', '2+' through '6+', and '6+<'). I did not count numeric values of 1.0 or higher, or values such as '>6', as positive. "No recorded patient description" means Patient.Description is NULL. No rows have an empty string, so the TRIM check changes nothing.

sql: select d.driverRef, d.nationality, d.dob from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) join races r using(raceId) where r.year=2017 and r.name='Italian Grand Prix' and nullif(q.q2,'') is not null and nullif(q.q3,'') is null
answer: 5 drivers set a Q2 time but no Q3 time at the 2017 Italian GP: perez (Mexican, 1990-01-26), hulkenberg (German, 1987-08-19), alonso (Spanish, 1981-07-29), kvyat (Russian, 1994-04-26), sainz (Spanish, 1994-09-01). I read "completed Q2" as a non-empty q2 value, and "did not reach Q3" as an empty or NULL q3. The q2 and q3 columns hold '' as well as NULL for sessions a driver didn't take part in, so the query treats both as missing.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1 AND side IS NOT NULL AND frameVersion = (SELECT frameVersion FROM cards WHERE frameVersion GLOB '[0-9]*' ORDER BY CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER) DESC LIMIT 1)
answer:
The query returns 127 distinct card names. I read the conditions this way:
- Promotional printing: `isPromo = 1`.
- Multiple faces on the same card: `side IS NOT NULL`. The docs say an empty `side` means the card has no multiple faces.
- Most recent frame version: the latest year across all cards, which is 2015. The value 'future' is not a year, so I excluded it. If you count 'future' as the newest frame style, the answer would change.
- Names with a delimiter, such as split cards, are listed as stored, and each name appears once.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom WHERE molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type='#') AND molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element IN ('p','br'))
answer: 4 atoms in total. I counted every atom (all elements) in molecules that have at least one '#' (triple) bond and at least one 'p' or 'br' atom.

sql: SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.CRE >= 1.5) THEN p.ID END) AS abnormal_patients, COUNT(*) AS total_patients, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.CRE >= 1.5) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct FROM Patient p WHERE p.SEX IN ('M','F') GROUP BY p.SEX ORDER BY p.SEX DESC
answer: Men: 7 of 202 patients (3.5%) have at least one creatinine result of 1.5 or higher. Women: 7 of 1,023 patients (0.7%). Totals count every patient of that sex on the Patient table, including patients with no lab results. I left out 13 patients whose sex is blank, since you asked for M and F only. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still drafts in the ontology and have not been certified.

sql: SELECT d.code FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId = q.raceId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3 <> '' ORDER BY d.code;
answer: 10 drivers set a Q3 time at the 2017 Italian GP. Their codes in alphabetical order are BOT, HAM, MAS, OCO, RAI, RIC, STR, VAN, VER, VET. I counted a driver as having set a time when q3 is neither NULL nor an empty string. All 10 have a driver code.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) FROM connected c JOIN atom a ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id JOIN atom b ON b.atom_id = c.atom_id2 WHERE (a.element = 'h' OR b.element = 'h') AND a.molecule_id = (SELECT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element = 'y')
answer: 2 bonds in the yttrium-containing molecule have a hydrogen atom at one end. I counted each bond once by using distinct bond ids, because `connected` stores each bond in both directions. The check query I ran filtered on `bond.molecule_id` instead of `atom.molecule_id` and also returned 2. The yttrium atom is the only `y` atom in the database, so it identifies a single molecule.

sql: SELECT s.code, s.releaseDate FROM sets s WHERE strftime('%Y', s.releaseDate) = '2020' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.language = 'Spanish' AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(t.translation) <> '') ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.code
answer:
34 sets released in 2020 have no Spanish name, for example J20 and PF20 (2020-01-01), THB (2020-01-24) and CC1 (2020-12-04). The query returns the set code and release date for each one.

I counted a set as having no Spanish name if it has no 'Spanish' row in set_translations, or if that row's translation is null or blank. The 'Card Set' and 'Set Translation' terms I used are still drafts in the ontology, not certified.

sql: SELECT b.bond_type, IIF(m.label = '+', 'YES', 'NO') AS carcinogenic FROM bond b JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id WHERE b.molecule_id = 'TR010' GROUP BY b.bond_type, m.label ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, b.bond_type LIMIT 1
answer: TR010에서 가장 많은 결합 유형은 단일 결합 '-'(16개, 이중 결합 '='는 1개)이고, 이 분자는 발암성이 아닙니다(NO). 결과: ('-', 'NO'). 동률이면 결합 기호 순으로 첫 번째를 고르도록 했습니다. 사용한 Term인 Bond와 Molecule은 draft 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN a.alignment = 'Good' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS good_percentage FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON p.id = s.publisher_id LEFT JOIN alignment a ON a.id = s.alignment_id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name <> '-'
answer: 68.27% of Marvel Comics superheroes with a known full name (full_name not NULL and not '-') are good. The denominator is all such heroes, including those with unknown alignment. The Superhero, Publisher and Alignment terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: select s.superhero_name from superhero s join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id join hero_power hp on hp.hero_id=s.id join superpower sp on sp.id=hp.power_id where p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics' and sp.power_name='Super Strength'
answer: 201 Marvel Comics superheroes have 'Super Strength'. The query returns their superhero_name values, one row per hero with no duplicates. I read "superheroes" as the superhero_name column.

sql:
WITH base AS (
SELECT s.CDSCode, s.School, s.County, s.City, s.MailStreet, s.MailCity, s.MailState, s.MailZip, s.Website,
 f.`Enrollment (K-12)` AS enr, f.`FRPM Count (K-12)` AS frpm, 1.0*f.`FRPM Count (K-12)`/f.`Enrollment (K-12)` AS share,
 (sat.AvgScrRead+sat.AvgScrMath+sat.AvgScrWrite) AS avg_sat,
 CASE WHEN sat.NumTstTakr>0 THEN 100.0*sat.NumGE1500/sat.NumTstTakr END AS pct1500,
 s.OpenDate, CASE WHEN s.ClosedDate IS NOT NULL AND s.ClosedDate<>'' THEN 'closed' ELSE 'open' END AS status
FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode
LEFT JOIN satscores sat ON sat.cds=s.CDSCode AND sat.rtype='S'
WHERE s.Charter=0 AND s.EdOpsCode='TRAD' AND s.School IS NOT NULL AND f.`Enrollment (K-12)`>100 AND f.`FRPM Count (K-12)` IS NOT NULL),
parts AS (
SELECT 1 AS ord,'largest FRPM-eligible count' AS part,* FROM base WHERE frpm=(SELECT MAX(frpm) FROM base)
UNION ALL SELECT 2,'smallest FRPM share',* FROM base WHERE share=(SELECT MIN(share) FROM base)
UNION ALL SELECT 3,'the CDS code from my notes',* FROM base WHERE CAST(CDSCode AS INTEGER)=4615150435602)
SELECT part, School AS school_name, County AS county, City AS city, MailStreet AS mailing_street, MailCity AS mailing_city, MailState AS mailing_state, MailZip AS mailing_zip, Website AS website, enr AS k12_enrollment, frpm AS frpm_eligible_count, share AS frpm_share, avg_sat AS avg_total_sat, pct1500 AS pct_sat_takers_1500_plus, OpenDate AS opening_date, status
FROM parts ORDER BY ord, CDSCode
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 확인했습니다. 결과는 3행이고 각 행에 해당하는 항목 이름을 붙였습니다. 앞에 붙인 항목 이름 열(part)은 행이 어느 항목에 해당하는지 표시하려고 추가했습니다.

- 가장 많은 FRPM 대상 학생(4,419명): Paramount High (Los Angeles 카운티, Paramount). K-12 등록 4,814명, FRPM 비율 91.8%, 평균 SAT 총점 1272, 1500점 이상 응시자 14.8%, 개교일 1953-07-01, 상태 open.
- 가장 낮은 FRPM 비율(0.22%, 2명): Orinda Intermediate (Contra Costa 카운티, Orinda). K-12 등록 907명, 개교일 1980-07-01, 상태 open. 이 학교는 SAT 기록이 없어 SAT 두 열이 비어 있고, 웹사이트도 비어 있습니다.
- 메모의 CDS 코드 4615150435602: Oroville High (Butte 카운티, Oroville). K-12 등록 982명, FRPM 692명(70.5%), 평균 SAT 총점 1395, 1500점 이상 응시자 32.7%, 개교일 1980-07-01, 상태 open. 웹사이트는 http://ohs.ouhsd.org입니다.

세 항목에서 동점인 학교는 없었고, 한 학교가 두 항목에 겹치지도 않았습니다.

적용한 해석은 다음과 같습니다.
- "정규 비차터 학교"는 Charter=0이고 교육 형태(EdOpsCode)가 'TRAD'(Traditional)인 학교로 보았습니다. 대안학교, 지역 커뮤니티 학교, 특수학교 등은 제외했습니다.
- K-12 등록 학생이 100명을 넘는 학교만 대상으로 했습니다.
- FRPM 비율은 `FRPM Count (K-12)`를 `Enrollment (K-12)`로 나눈 값(0~1 척도)입니다.
- 평균 총점은 읽기, 수학, 쓰기 평균의 합입니다. 1500점 이상 비율은 응시자 대비 백분율입니다.
- 상태는 ClosedDate가 기록되어 있으면 'closed', 아니면 'open'으로 표시했습니다.
- CDS 코드는 저장된 값에 앞자리 0이 붙어 있어(04615150435602) 숫자로 변환해 비교했습니다.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT CustomerID, SUM(Consumption) s FROM yearmonth WHERE Date BETWEEN '201201' AND '201212' GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING SUM(Consumption)>0) SELECT CAST(ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN c.Currency='CZK' THEN t.s END) - AVG(CASE WHEN c.Currency='EUR' THEN t.s END)) AS INTEGER) AS diff FROM t JOIN customers c USING(CustomerID)
answer: CZK 평균 − EUR 평균 = 14,314 (반올림). 해석: 고객별 2012년 연간 소비량 합계를 구한 뒤 통화별로 고객 평균을 냈고, 2012년 소비량이 0보다 큰 고객만 포함했습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS female_sjs_patients FROM Patient p JOIN Examination e ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND instr(',' || replace(replace(e.Diagnosis, ' ', ''), char(29), ',') || ',', ',SjS,') > 0
answer: 20 female patients. I counted distinct patients whose Examination.Diagnosis, across all dates, contains SjS as its own item. That includes combinations such as "SLE, SjS". It excludes "SjS susp", because the item there is "SjSsusp", not "SjS". Patients with only suspected SjS are not counted.

sql:
WITH f AS (
 SELECT s.code FROM sets s WHERE s.code IN (SELECT setCode FROM cards WHERE name='Abyssal Horror')
 ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.code LIMIT 1),
l AS (SELECT code FROM sets ORDER BY releaseDate DESC, code LIMIT 1)
SELECT s.name, ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN c.manaCost IS NOT NULL AND c.manaCost<>'' AND c.convertedManaCost<=3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS pct
FROM sets s JOIN cards c ON c.setCode=s.code
WHERE s.code IN (SELECT code FROM f UNION SELECT code FROM l) GROUP BY s.code, s.name ORDER BY s.releaseDate;
answer: Urza's Saga (first printing of Abyssal Horror): 58.15%. Time Spiral Remastered (code TSR, latest release 2021-03-19): 80.00%. I used all cards in each set as the denominator (cards with no printed mana cost count as not qualifying), and a card qualifies only if its manaCost is non-empty and convertedManaCost <= 3. Rows are ordered by release date.

sql: WITH s AS (SELECT cs.constructorId, r.year, cs.points, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cs.constructorId, r.year ORDER BY r.round DESC) rn FROM constructorStandings cs JOIN races r ON r.raceId=cs.raceId), t AS (SELECT c.constructorId, c.name, c.url, COALESCE(SUM(s.points),0) pts FROM constructors c LEFT JOIN s ON s.constructorId=c.constructorId AND s.rn=1 WHERE c.nationality='Italian' GROUP BY c.constructorId), k AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY pts DESC) rk FROM t) SELECT name, pts AS career_points, url FROM k WHERE rk<=3 ORDER BY rk, name
answer:
The top three Italian constructors by career points are Ferrari with 6991.5 points (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari), Benetton with 861.5 (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_Formula) and Toro Rosso with 381.0 (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Toro_Rosso). There are no ties, so exactly three rows come back.

I read "points the constructor finished each season with" as the constructor standings points after its last race of each calendar year, summed over all years. I did not add up the per-race results. Italian means `constructors.nationality = 'Italian'`. Constructors with no standings rows count as 0 and are ranked with the rest. The "introduction website" is the `url` column.

sql: WITH RECURSIVE s(id,item,rest) AS (SELECT e.expense_id,'',e.expense_description||',' FROM expense e JOIN member m ON m.member_id=e.link_to_member WHERE m.first_name='Sacha' AND m.last_name='Harrison' UNION ALL SELECT id,trim(substr(rest,1,instr(rest,',')-1)),substr(rest,instr(rest,',')+1) FROM s WHERE rest<>'') SELECT item AS item_name, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS times_bought FROM s WHERE item<>'' GROUP BY item ORDER BY item
answer: Sacha Harrison has 12 expense records, and all of them are approved. Many descriptions list several items separated by commas, such as "Water, chips, cookies", so I split them and counted each item once per expense record. Results: Posters 4, Water 3, chips 3, cookies 3, Travel Mug 2, and 1 each for Alumni Glass, Bakery - Donuts, muffins, Pizza and Post Cards. One caveat: "Bakery - Donuts, muffins" splits into "Bakery - Donuts" and "muffins", because the "Bakery -" prefix is part of the first item's text. If you want those listed as "Donuts" and "muffins", the list needs a small manual adjustment.

sql: SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_single_bonds FROM (SELECT b.molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM bond b JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '+' AND b.bond_type = '-' GROUP BY b.molecule_id)
answer: Carcinogenic molecules (label '+') that have at least one single bond (bond_type '-') average 20.25 single bonds per molecule. Molecules with no single bonds are left out, because the inner query only groups molecules that have a '-' bond. This used the draft Terms Molecule and Bond, which are not certified yet. I did not run validate_sql before run_sql.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(UpVotes),2) AS avg_upvotes, ROUND(AVG(Age),2) AS avg_age FROM users WHERE Id IN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE CreaionDate>='2012-01-01' AND CreaionDate<'2013-01-01' GROUP BY OwnerUserId HAVING COUNT(*)>10)
answer: 2012년에 게시물을 10개 넘게 만든 사용자는 268명이고, 이들의 평균 UpVotes는 505.63, 평균 나이는 36.14입니다. 게시물은 질문과 답변을 모두 포함해 OwnerUserId 기준으로 셌습니다. 나이를 입력하지 않은 사용자(NULL)는 평균 나이 계산에서 빠집니다.

sql:
WITH a AS (SELECT atom_id, element FROM atom JOIN molecule USING(molecule_id) WHERE label='+'),
b AS (SELECT element, COUNT(*) n FROM a WHERE atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id FROM connected UNION SELECT atom_id2 FROM connected) GROUP BY element),
t AS (SELECT COUNT(*) tot FROM a)
SELECT element, ROUND(100.0*(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM a WHERE a.element=b.element)/tot,2) AS pct FROM b,t WHERE n=(SELECT MAX(n) FROM b)
answer: The most common element among bonded atoms in '+' molecules is hydrogen ('h'). It accounts for 42.50% of all atoms in '+' molecules. I counted an atom as bonded if it appears as either end of a row in `connected`. The percentage uses all atoms of '+' molecules, bonded or not. No other element tied with hydrogen.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.driverId) AS drivers_out_qualified FROM qualifying l JOIN races r ON r.raceId=l.raceId JOIN qualifying o ON o.raceId=l.raceId AND o.driverId<>l.driverId WHERE r.year=2010 AND l.driverId=810 AND l.position IS NOT NULL AND o.position IS NOT NULL AND l.position<o.position
answer: Lucas di Grassi out-qualified 9 distinct drivers in 2010. I counted each driver once, even if di Grassi beat them in several races. A driver counts if their qualifying position in the same race was worse (a higher number) than di Grassi's, using the `qualifying.position` column.

sql: select distinct name from cards where setCode='DKA' and ','||keywords||',' like '%,Flash,%' and convertedManaCost=(select max(convertedManaCost) from cards where setCode='DKA' and ','||keywords||',' like '%,Flash,%') order by name
answer: 세 장입니다. Briarpack Alpha, Hollowhenge Spirit, Nephalia Seakite가 모두 변환 마나 비용 4로 같습니다. 'Dark Ascension'은 세트 코드 DKA로 보았고 프로모 세트(PDKA)는 뺐습니다. Flash 키워드는 정확히 일치하는 경우만 셌습니다. 'Flashback'은 다른 키워드라서 제외했습니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg),2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero s WHERE s.superhero_name<>'3-D Man' AND s.weight_kg>0 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id=s.id AND hp.power_id IN (SELECT power_id FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id=(SELECT id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name='3-D Man')))
answer: 282411.79 kg. I treated weight_kg of 0 or NULL as "not recorded", following docs/superhero.csv, and left those heroes out. 3-D Man is excluded. A hero counts once however many powers they share with him. The average is pulled up by Godzilla (90,000,000 kg) and King Kong (9,000,000 kg). I kept them because they are recorded values.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.colors = 'B' AND (',' || c.types || ',') LIKE '%,Artifact,%' AND f.flavorText IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(f.flavorText) <> ''
answer: 11 distinct mono-black Artifact cards (colors = 'B'; types includes Artifact, so Artifact Creature etc. count) have at least one foreign-language row with non-empty flavor text. Cards are counted by distinct name, not by printing. Based on draft (uncertified) terms Card and Card Foreign Data.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT DISTINCT c.circuitRef, r.time AS t FROM races r JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId=r.circuitId WHERE r.time IS NOT NULL AND r.time <> ''), b AS (SELECT MIN(t) AS mn, MAX(t) AS mx FROM t) SELECT e.circuitRef AS earliest_circuit_ref, l.circuitRef AS latest_circuit_ref, CAST(strftime('%s','2000-01-01 '||b.mx)-strftime('%s','2000-01-01 '||b.mn) AS INTEGER) AS gap_seconds FROM b JOIN t e ON e.t=b.mn JOIN t l ON l.t=b.mx ORDER BY 1,2
answer: Earliest start: fuji. Latest start: americas. Gap: 55,800 seconds (15h30m). I compared the local start times in races.time across all seasons and excluded races with no start time recorded (722 rows are NULL). If several circuits tied for the earliest or latest time, the query would return one row per combination. Only one circuit had each here. The Circuit and Race terms are still draft in the ontology.

sql: with top as (select A2 name, A16 crimes from district where A3='central Bohemia' order by cast(A4 as int) desc, A2 limit 3), o as (select avg(A16) a from district) select name as district_name, crimes as crimes_1996, round((select avg(crimes) from top),2) as top3_avg, round(o.a,2) as overall_avg, round((select avg(crimes) from top)-o.a,2) as difference from top, o order by crimes desc
answer: The three most populous central Bohemia districts are Kladno (5,892 crimes in 1996), Mlada Boleslav (4,987) and Pribram (3,868). Their average is 4,915.67. The average over all 77 districts is 5,030.83, so the difference (three-district minus overall) is -115.16. I read "crimes committed in 1996" as district.A16 and cast the text column A4 to an integer to rank by population. The query returns one row per district, with the averages and difference repeated on each row.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM member m WHERE m.link_to_major = j.major_id)) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_majors_without_members FROM major j
answer: 76.99. 전체 113개 전공 중 동아리 회원이 한 명도 없는 전공의 비율입니다. 전공 이름은 중복이 없어 major_id 기준으로 계산했고, 전공이 비어 있거나 major 표에 없는 회원이 1명 있지만 이 비율에는 영향이 없습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM Patient p WHERE p.Birthday > '1960-01-01' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND l.RNP <> 'negative' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 10)
answer: 594 patients born after 1 Jan 1960 never had an RNP result strictly above 10. This includes patients with no lab results. 'negative' and NULL results are not counted as raised, and a result of exactly 10 would not count either. Patients with a missing birthday are excluded. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still draft.

sql: SELECT m.molecule_id FROM molecule m WHERE m.label='-' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM atom a WHERE a.molecule_id=m.molecule_id AND a.element IN ('na','k','ca','sn','pb','cu','zn','y')) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM bond b WHERE b.molecule_id=m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type='-') ORDER BY m.molecule_id LIMIT 3
answer: TR011, TR101, TR139. 해석: 비발암성은 label '-', 단일결합은 bond_type '-'인 결합이 하나 이상 있는 경우로 봤습니다. 금속 원자는 na, k, ca, sn, pb, cu, zn, y로 정했습니다. 문서에 금속 목록이 없어서 데이터에 나오는 원소 중 금속을 직접 골랐습니다.

sql: SELECT s.block, SUM(EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode=s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation<>'')) AS translated_sets, SUM(s.baseSetSize) AS total_base_set_size FROM sets s WHERE s.block IN ('Masques','Mirage') GROUP BY s.block ORDER BY s.block
answer: Masques: 2 sets have a translated name, and the base sets total 640 cards. Mirage: 1 set has a translated name, and the base sets total 684 cards. Readings I chose: every set in the block counts, including the promo sets (PMMQ, PNEM, PPCY for Masques). A set counts as translated if it has at least one non-empty translation, and each set is counted once however many languages it has. The base-size total sums baseSetSize across all sets in the block, including sets with no translation. Masques has 7 sets and Mirage has 4. In Masques, MMQ and PCY have translations. In Mirage, only WTH does.

sql: select d.forename, count(distinct d.driverId) n from results r join races ra on ra.raceId=r.raceId join drivers d on d.driverId=r.driverId where ra.name='Italian Grand Prix' and r.positionOrder=2 group by d.forename having n>=2 order by n desc, d.forename;
answer: Two forenames recur among Italian Grand Prix runners-up: Mike (3 different drivers) and Juan (2 different drivers). I counted distinct drivers, not editions. By edition the counts would be Mike 4 and Juan 3, because some drivers finished second more than once. "Runner-up" means positionOrder = 2 in races named 'Italian Grand Prix'.

sql:
WITH ab AS (SELECT account_id, AVG(balance) AS avgbal FROM trans GROUP BY account_id),
h AS (SELECT DISTINCT cl.gender, a.district_id FROM card c JOIN disp d ON d.disp_id=c.disp_id JOIN client cl ON cl.client_id=d.client_id JOIN account a ON a.account_id=d.account_id JOIN ab ON ab.account_id=a.account_id WHERE c.type='gold' AND ab.avgbal>1000),
s AS (SELECT h.gender, di.district_id, di.A2 AS name, CAST(di.A4 AS INTEGER) AS inh, di.A11 AS sal, di.A10 AS urb FROM h JOIN district di ON di.district_id=h.district_id WHERE CAST(di.A4 AS INTEGER)>100000),
g AS (SELECT gender, COUNT(*) AS n, ROUND(AVG(sal),2) AS avg_salary, ROUND(AVG(urb),2) AS avg_urban, MAX(inh) AS mx FROM s GROUP BY gender)
SELECT g.gender, g.n AS district_count, s.name AS most_populous_district, s.inh AS inhabitants, g.avg_salary, g.avg_urban AS avg_urban_ratio
FROM g JOIN s ON s.gender=g.gender AND s.inh=g.mx
ORDER BY CASE g.gender WHEN 'F' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, s.name
answer:
Women (F): 16 districts, the largest is Hl.m. Praha with 1,204,953 inhabitants, average salary 9,245.44, average urban ratio 69.16. Men (M): 22 districts, the largest is also Hl.m. Praha (1,204,953), average salary 9,347.86, average urban ratio 71.03. There were no ties for the largest district.

Readings I chose:
- A gold-card holder is the client on the disposition the card is attached to. Gender comes from that client, and the account is that disposition's account.
- An account's average balance is the mean of `trans.balance` over all its transactions, and it must be strictly greater than 1,000.
- Each district is counted once per gender, even if several qualifying accounts sit there. The 100,000 inhabitants cut-off is strictly greater than.
- The average salary and urban ratio are plain averages over the distinct districts, not weighted by accounts or inhabitants.

sql: SELECT Segment, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM (SELECT c.Segment, y.CustomerID FROM customers c INNER JOIN yearmonth y ON c.CustomerID = y.CustomerID WHERE y.Date BETWEEN '201201' AND '201212' GROUP BY y.CustomerID, c.Segment HAVING SUM(y.Consumption) < 30000 AND MAX(y.Consumption) > 0) GROUP BY Segment ORDER BY Segment
answer: Customers with 2012 total consumption below 30,000 (strictly), per segment: KAM 1,123; LAM 2,031; SME 21,862. Interpretation: "used their cards in 2012" = Consumption > 0 in at least one month of 2012; the total is the sum of monthly Consumption for 201201–201212. The Customer and Monthly Customer Consumption Terms are still draft (not certified).

sql:
WITH c AS (
 SELECT s.School, s.Charter, s.GSserved, 1.0*f.`Free Meal Count (K-12)`/f.`Enrollment (K-12)` AS r,
  t.AvgScrRead+t.AvgScrMath+t.AvgScrWrite AS tot
 FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds=s.CDSCode AND t.rtype='S'
 WHERE s.County='Alameda' AND s.School IS NOT NULL AND (s.GSserved='12' OR s.GSserved LIKE '%-12')
  AND f.`Enrollment (K-12)`>0 AND f.`Free Meal Count (K-12)` IS NOT NULL)
SELECT School AS school_name, ROUND(r,4) AS free_meal_rate,
 CASE Charter WHEN 1 THEN 'Yes' WHEN 0 THEN 'No' ELSE 'Unknown' END AS is_charter,
 GSserved AS grades_served,
 CASE WHEN tot IS NULL THEN 'No SAT Data'
  WHEN tot > (SELECT AVG(AvgScrRead+AvgScrMath+AvgScrWrite) FROM satscores WHERE rtype='S')*1.05 THEN 'Above Average'
  WHEN tot < (SELECT AVG(AvgScrRead+AvgScrMath+AvgScrWrite) FROM satscores WHERE rtype='S')*0.95 THEN 'Below Average'
  ELSE 'Average' END AS sat_performance_level
FROM c WHERE r=(SELECT MAX(r) FROM c)
answer:
California School for the Blind | 0.9833 | No | K-12 | No SAT Data. It is the only school at the top, so there is no tie. Next highest are California School for the Deaf-Fremont at 0.9829 and Civicorps Corpsmember Academy at 0.9000.

Readings I chose:
- "Serves up through 12th grade" means the directory's GSserved is '12' or ends in '-12'. I did not also require EILCode = 'HS', so K-12 schools count.
- Free meal rate is Free Meal Count (K-12) divided by Enrollment (K-12) from frpm. I excluded schools with zero enrollment.
- The docs define no cutoffs for "SAT performance level", so I defined it myself. It compares a school's total SAT (reading + math + writing) with the statewide mean of school-level totals (1426.3). Within 5% of the mean counts as Average, above that as Above Average, below that as Below Average, and no SAT row as No SAT Data. This school has no SAT row, so the result is No SAT Data under any cutoff.

The most populous district is district 70, with 285,387 inhabitants. The average salary across the districts the ten loans come from is 8,985.75.

Readings I chose:
- Loans are 24-month loans on accounts with frequency 'POPLATEK TYDNE' (weekly issuance).
- The branch district is account.district_id.
- The ten largest loans are ordered by amount descending, then loan_id ascending. Because the loan_id tie-break gives every loan a unique rank, this is just the first ten rows.
- Each district is counted once in the salary average, even if several of the ten loans come from it.
- Inhabitants are district.A4, which is stored as text, so I cast it to an integer. Salary is district.A11.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.element='i' THEN a.atom_id END) AS iodine, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.element='s' THEN a.atom_id END) AS sulfur FROM connected c JOIN bond b ON b.bond_id=c.bond_id JOIN atom a ON a.atom_id=c.atom_id WHERE b.bond_type='-';
answer: 3개의 요오드(i) 원자와 77개의 황(s) 원자가 단일 결합('-')에 한 번 이상 참여합니다. connected 테이블에는 결합마다 양방향 행이 저장되어 있어서 atom_id 쪽만 봐도 모든 원자가 포함됩니다.

sql: WITH fl AS (SELECT c.client_id, c.birth_date, l.loan_id, l.account_id, l.amount, l.duration, l.payments, l.status, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY l.amount DESC) AS rnk FROM loan l JOIN disp dp ON dp.account_id = l.account_id AND dp.type = 'OWNER' JOIN client c ON c.client_id = dp.client_id WHERE c.gender = 'F'), top AS (SELECT * FROM fl WHERE rnk <= 3), tx AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS n_tx, SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS deposits FROM trans WHERE account_id IN (SELECT account_id FROM top) GROUP BY account_id), reg_loans AS (SELECT d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS n FROM loan l JOIN account a ON a.account_id = l.account_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id GROUP BY d.A3), reg_sal AS (SELECT A3 AS region, ROUND(AVG(A11), 2) AS avg_sal FROM district GROUP BY A3) SELECT t.client_id, ROUND(t.amount, 2) AS loan_amount, t.duration AS duration_months, ROUND(t.payments * t.duration, 2) AS total_payments, ROUND(t.payments * t.duration - t.amount, 2) AS interest_paid, t.status AS loan_status, d.A2 AS district, d.A3 AS region, tx.n_tx AS transaction_count, ROUND(COALESCE(tx.deposits, 0), 2) AS total_deposits, CASE WHEN tx.deposits > 2 * t.amount THEN 'High Income' WHEN tx.deposits > t.amount THEN 'Medium Income' ELSE 'Low Income' END AS income_category, rl.n AS loans_in_region, rs.avg_sal AS region_avg_salary, CAST(strftime('%Y','2026-10-09') AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', t.birth_date) AS INTEGER) - (CASE WHEN strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09') < strftime('%m-%d', t.birth_date) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS age FROM top t JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id LEFT JOIN tx ON tx.account_id = t.account_id JOIN reg_loans rl ON rl.region = d.A3 JOIN reg_sal rs ON rs.region = d.A3 ORDER BY t.amount DESC, t.client_id
answer:
The three largest loans held by female clients (no ties at the cutoff, so exactly three rows):

| client | amount | months | total payments | interest | status | district / region | transactions | deposits | income category | loans in region | region avg salary | age |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10997 | 566,640 | 60 | 566,640 | 0 | C | Hl.m. Praha / Prague | 200 | 447,173 | Low Income | 84 | 12,541.00 | 54 |
| 2823 | 541,200 | 60 | 541,200 | 0 | D | Karvina / north Moravia | 329 | 515,538 | Low Income | 117 | 9,049.18 | 79 |
| 8506 | 495,180 | 60 | 495,180 | 0 | C | Jesenik / north Moravia | 76 | 770,790 | Medium Income | 117 | 9,049.18 | 46 |

Interest paid is 0 for all three because the monthly payment times the duration equals the approved amount exactly in the data.

Readings I chose where the question was open:
- **Loan holder:** the client with the OWNER disposition on the loan's account, since only owners take loans. Female DISPONENT co-holders are not counted.
- **Branch district:** the district of the account's branch (account.district_id), not the client's home district.
- **Total deposits:** the sum of credit (PRIJEM) transaction amounts over the account's whole history.
- **Transaction count:** all transactions on the account.
- **Loans in region:** every loan whose account sits at a branch in that region, for all clients.
- **Region average salary:** the average of A11 over all districts in the region.

The ontology Terms used (Account, Client, Disposition, District, Loan, Transaction) are all still draft, not certified. validate_sql was not run. run_sql warned that the loan-to-disp and loan-to-trans joins are not registered relationships. Both follow the shared account_id key.

sql:
WITH sle AS (SELECT ID, Diagnosis FROM Patient WHERE (',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(Diagnosis, ''), CHAR(13), ','), CHAR(10), ','), CHAR(29), ','), CHAR(11), ','), '  ', ','), ' ', '') || ',') LIKE '%,SLE,%' OR (',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(COALESCE(Diagnosis, ''), CHAR(13), ','), CHAR(10), ','), CHAR(29), ','), CHAR(11), ','), '  ', ','), ' ', '') || ',') LIKE '%,SLE(%')
SELECT s.ID, s.Diagnosis, l.DNA FROM sle s JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = s.ID WHERE l.DNA IS NOT NULL AND CAST(l.DNA AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(l2.DNA AS REAL)) FROM sle s2 JOIN Laboratory l2 ON l2.ID = s2.ID WHERE l2.DNA IS NOT NULL)
answer:
환자 2933261의 진단은 'SLE'이고, 최고 anti-DNA 검사 결과는 185입니다. 동률인 환자는 없습니다.

해석한 기준은 두 가지입니다. 첫째, 진단 목록에 'SLE'가 독립 항목으로 들어 있으면 SLE 환자로 봤습니다. 'SLE susp'처럼 의심으로만 적힌 경우는 제외했고, 'SLE, SJS'처럼 다른 질환이 함께 적힌 경우는 포함했습니다. 둘째, DNA 열이 텍스트라서 숫자로 바꿔 최댓값을 비교했고, 출력은 검사에 적힌 원래 값을 그대로 썼습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.atom_id2) AS atom_count FROM atom AS a JOIN connected AS c ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id WHERE a.element = 'cl'
answer: 271 atoms are directly bonded to a chlorine atom (element 'cl'). I counted distinct neighbor atoms, so an atom bonded to two chlorines counts once. The `connected` table stores each bond in both directions, so joining on `atom_id` finds every neighbor. This follows the verified sulfur query in docs/verified_queries.md. The result relies on the Atom term, which is still draft.

sql: WITH f AS (SELECT l.raceId, l.driverId, MIN(l.milliseconds) AS ms FROM lapTimes l WHERE l.milliseconds > 0 GROUP BY l.raceId, l.driverId HAVING MIN(l.milliseconds) > 90000) SELECT r.date, d.forename, d.surname, CASE WHEN f.ms IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE (f.ms/60000) || ':' || printf('%02d.%03d', (f.ms%60000)/1000, f.ms%1000) END AS fastest_lap_time FROM races r LEFT JOIN f ON f.raceId = r.raceId LEFT JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = f.driverId WHERE r.name = 'French Grand Prix' AND r.year >= 1990 ORDER BY r.date, d.surname, f.ms, d.forename
answer:
The query returns 20 rows for the 19 French Grand Prix editions from 1990 to 2008. 2008 is the most recent edition in the data. Only the 2007 edition (2007-07-01) has drivers over 90 seconds: Anthony Davidson at 1:44.767 and Jarno Trulli at 2:19.632. The other 18 editions appear with their date and empty driver and lap time columns.

Choices I made where the question was open:
- **"Slower than 90 seconds"** means a fastest lap above 90.000 s, so exactly 90.000 s is excluded.
- **Lap times** come from the per-lap table (`lapTimes`), taking each driver's minimum lap in the race. The official `results.fastestLapTime` column is empty for every edition before 2004, and for 2004 to 2008 it has no value above 90 s. Using it would have shown no driver in any edition. The lap-by-lap data starts in 1996, so 1990 to 1995 show no drivers because no laps are recorded for them, not because everyone was fast.
- **Format:** I converted milliseconds to m:ss.mmm.
- **Ordering:** by date, then surname, then lap time, then forename.

The Terms I relied on (Race, Driver, Lap Time) are still in draft status, not certified.

sql: SELECT s.type AS expansion_type, COUNT(DISTINCT t.setCode) AS japanese_name_sets FROM sets s LEFT JOIN set_translations t ON t.setCode = s.code AND t.language = 'Japanese' AND TRIM(COALESCE(t.translation, '')) <> '' GROUP BY s.type ORDER BY s.type
answer:
쿼리를 실행해 확인했습니다. 세트 유형 20개가 모두 나오고, 일본어 이름이 있는 세트가 없는 유형은 0으로 표시됩니다. 일본어 이름이 있다고 본 기준은 set_translations에 language가 'Japanese'이고 translation이 비어 있지 않은 행이 있는 경우입니다. 한 세트에 일본어 행이 여러 개여도 1개로 계산합니다.

결과는 다음과 같습니다.
- archenemy 1, box 3, commander 7, core 7, draft_innovation 2, duel_deck 16
- expansion 41, from_the_vault 8, masters 5, planechase 2, premium_deck 1
- 0인 유형: funny, masterpiece, memorabilia, promo, spellbook, starter, token, treasure_chest, vanguard

정렬은 유형 이름의 알파벳순입니다.

sql: WITH pa AS (SELECT a.atom_id, a.element FROM atom a JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id=a.molecule_id WHERE m.label='+'), tot AS (SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM pa), bonded AS (SELECT element, COUNT(*) c FROM pa WHERE atom_id IN (SELECT atom_id FROM connected UNION SELECT atom_id2 FROM connected) GROUP BY element), el AS (SELECT element FROM bonded WHERE c=(SELECT MAX(c) FROM bonded)) SELECT el.element, ROUND(100.0*(SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pa WHERE pa.element=el.element)/tot.n,2) AS pct FROM el CROSS JOIN tot
answer: Hydrogen ('h') is the most common element among bonded atoms in '+' molecules, with no ties. It accounts for 42.50% of all atoms in those molecules. Atoms were counted as bonded if they appear at either end of a connected row, and the percentage denominator is every atom in the '+' molecules.

sql:
WITH a AS (
  SELECT substr(ac.date,1,4) AS yr, ac.district_id, COUNT(*) AS n,
         SUM(COALESCE(l.amount,0)) AS lent
  FROM account ac
  JOIN district d ON d.district_id = ac.district_id
  LEFT JOIN loan l ON l.account_id = ac.account_id
  WHERE d.A3 = 'central Bohemia' AND ac.date >= '1996-01-01'
  GROUP BY yr, ac.district_id)
SELECT yr AS year, SUM(n) AS accounts_opened, SUM(lent) AS total_lent,
       ROUND(AVG(lent * 1.0 / n), 2) AS avg_lent_per_account_across_districts
FROM a GROUP BY yr ORDER BY yr;
answer:
Results (central Bohemia, accounts opened from 1996-01-01; the data ends in 1997 for this region):
- 1996: 191 accounts, 4,887,024 lent, 23,639.03 average across districts of lent per account
- 1997: 114 accounts, 1,971,468 lent, 19,809.53 average across districts of lent per account

Assumptions: "region" is district.A3 = 'central Bohemia', matched through the account's own (branch) district. Accounts without a loan count as 0 lent. For each year, I took lent-per-account within each district (district loan total divided by the accounts opened there that year), then averaged those across the districts that had accounts opened that year. Districts with no accounts that year are left out, since their ratio is undefined. Loans are attributed to the account's opening year, not the loan's own date.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1 AND side IS NOT NULL AND originalReleaseDate LIKE '2019/%'
answer: 31 distinct card names (e.g. "Decorated Knight // Present Arms", "Fae of Wishes // Granted"). I read "promotional" as isPromo = 1 and "multiple faces" as side IS NOT NULL (split, transform, adventure, modal_dfc, etc.). I filtered on the card's own originalReleaseDate (stored as text like 2019/1/25), not the set's release date. DISTINCT collapses repeated promo printings. Names appear in the combined "A // B" form stored in the name column.

sql: WITH l AS (SELECT preferred_foot f, attacking_work_rate w, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) rn FROM Player_Attributes WHERE date < '2015-01-02') SELECT COUNT(*) AS player_count FROM l WHERE rn=1 AND f='left' AND w IN ('low','medium')
answer: 1,795 players. I took each player's most recent rating record dated on or before 1 January 2015 and counted those whose preferred foot was left and whose attacking work rate was 'low' or 'medium'. The column has some malformed values ('le', 'norm', 'stoc', 'y', blanks, 'None'), which I did not count as low or medium.

sql:
WITH a AS (
 SELECT ac.account_id, ac.date AS opened, c.gender,
  CAST(strftime('%Y','1996-12-31')-strftime('%Y',c.birth_date)-(strftime('%m-%d','1996-12-31')<strftime('%m-%d',c.birth_date)) AS INTEGER) AS age
 FROM account ac JOIN district d ON d.district_id=ac.district_id AND d.A2='Tabor'
 JOIN disp dp ON dp.account_id=ac.account_id AND dp.type='OWNER'
 JOIN client c ON c.client_id=dp.client_id
 WHERE ac.date<='1996-12-31'),
p AS (
 SELECT a.*,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM card ca JOIN disp x ON x.disp_id=ca.disp_id WHERE x.account_id=a.account_id AND ca.issued<='1996-12-31') AS cards,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=a.account_id AND l.date<='1996-12-31') AS loans,
  (SELECT SUM(l.status='B') FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=a.account_id AND l.date<='1996-12-31') AS nb,
  (SELECT SUM(l.status IN ('C','D')) FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=a.account_id AND l.date<='1996-12-31') AS ncd,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trans t WHERE t.account_id=a.account_id AND t.date BETWEEN '1997-01-01' AND '1997-12-31') AS ntx,
  (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount),0) FROM trans t WHERE t.account_id=a.account_id AND t.date BETWEEN '1997-01-01' AND '1997-12-31' AND t.type='PRIJEM') AS money_in,
  (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount),0) FROM trans t WHERE t.account_id=a.account_id AND t.date BETWEEN '1997-01-01' AND '1997-12-31' AND t.type IN ('VYDAJ','VYBER')) AS money_out,
  (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(balance),0) FROM trans t WHERE t.account_id=a.account_id AND t.date BETWEEN '1997-01-01' AND '1997-12-31') AS peak
 FROM a)
SELECT account_id, opened AS open_date, gender, age, cards AS cards_issued, loans AS loans_approved,
 CASE WHEN loans=0 THEN 'no loan' WHEN nb>0 THEN 'defaulted' WHEN ncd>0 THEN 'repaying' ELSE 'paid off' END AS loan_standing,
 ntx AS transactions_1997, money_in AS money_in_1997, money_out AS money_out_1997, peak AS peak_balance_1997,
 RANK() OVER (ORDER BY peak DESC) AS peak_balance_rank
FROM p ORDER BY peak_balance_rank, account_id;
answer:
The query returns one row per Tabor account, with the 12 requested columns, ordered by peak-balance rank and then account id. I ran it and the output looked right (top row: account 7606, rank 1, peak 132,635). I did not count the rows or check the later ranks.

Readings I chose where the question was ambiguous:
- **Tabor branch:** accounts whose district (`account.district_id`) has `A2='Tabor'`. "Held as of 31 Dec 1996" means the account's open date is on or before 1996-12-31.
- **Owner:** the client on the account's `OWNER` disposition. Age is in whole completed years at 1996-12-31.
- **Cards and loans:** cards counted across all dispositions of the account, issued on or before 1996-12-31. Loans counted if approved on or before that date.
- **Loan standing:** 'no loan' if there are no loans. Otherwise 'defaulted' if any loan has status B, then 'repaying' if any has C or D, else 'paid off'.
- **Money flows (1997):** money in is the sum of `PRIJEM` amounts. Money out is the sum of `VYDAJ` and `VYBER` amounts, so cash withdrawals are included. Both are 0 if there are none.
- **Peak balance:** the maximum `trans.balance` during 1997, or 0 if there were no transactions. It is ranked with `RANK()` over all Tabor accounts, so ties share a rank and the next rank is skipped.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS good_non_dc_count FROM superhero s JOIN alignment a ON a.id=s.alignment_id LEFT JOIN publisher p ON p.id=s.publisher_id WHERE a.alignment='Good' AND (p.publisher_name IS NULL OR p.publisher_name<>'DC Comics')
answer: 358 superheroes have Good alignment and are not published by DC Comics. I counted heroes with no publisher recorded as "not DC", since they are not published by DC. If you only want heroes with a named non-DC publisher, the count is 355.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT uuid, COUNT(*) n FROM rulings GROUP BY uuid) SELECT DISTINCT cards.name, cards.artist, cards.isPromo FROM c JOIN cards USING(uuid) WHERE n=(SELECT MAX(n) FROM c)
answer: I treated each printing as one card row (one uuid) and counted its rulings. Two printings tie for the most rulings, and they give two combinations: Teferi's Protection, Chase Stone, isPromo=0 and Teferi's Protection, Chase Stone, isPromo=1. I did not de-duplicate rulings by text or date within a printing.

sql: SELECT SUM(SEX='F') - SUM(SEX='M') AS diff FROM Patient p WHERE Diagnosis='RA' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.UN<30)
answer: 23. Among RA patients with a normal urea nitrogen result, there are 30 women and 7 men. I read "RA patients" as Diagnosis exactly 'RA'. I read "normal urea nitrogen" as UN < 30, which is the normal range in the docs. A patient counts once if any of their lab records has UN < 30.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE (d.code IS NULL OR d.code='' OR d.code='\N') AND q.q1 IS NOT NULL AND q.q1<>'' AND (CAST(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60000 + CAST(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1,2) AS INTEGER)*1000 + CAST(substr(q.q1,-3) AS INTEGER)) > 120000 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM drivers d2 WHERE d2.forename=d.forename AND d2.driverId<>d.driverId)>=1
answer: 23. This counts qualifying rows with a Q1 time over 2:00.000 set by drivers whose code is NULL, empty or '\N' and whose forename is shared by at least one other driver in the drivers table. Rows with no Q1 time are excluded. The Driver and Qualifying Result terms used are draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT p.Id, u.DisplayName FROM posts AS p LEFT JOIN users AS u ON p.OwnerUserId = u.Id WHERE p.CreaionDate >= '2010-01-01' AND p.CreaionDate < '2011-01-01' AND p.FavoriteCount = (SELECT MAX(FavoriteCount) FROM posts WHERE CreaionDate >= '2010-01-01' AND CreaionDate < '2011-01-01')
answer: Post 1595, owned by Fabian Fagerholm, had the most favorites among posts created in 2010. It is the only post at the top count. The owner name comes from users.DisplayName via OwnerUserId, because posts.OwnerDisplayName is mostly null. 2010 is the range 2010-01-01 up to but not including 2011-01-01 on the misspelled CreaionDate column. The Post and User terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: WITH d AS (SELECT DISTINCT di.A2 AS name, CAST(di.A4 AS INTEGER) AS pop FROM account a JOIN district di ON di.district_id=a.district_id WHERE a.date >= '1993-01-01' AND a.date < '1993-02-01') SELECT name, pop FROM d WHERE pop=(SELECT MAX(pop) FROM d) ORDER BY name
answer: Hl.m. Praha (Prague) has the largest population among districts with an account opened in the first month, at 1,204,953 inhabitants. I took "first month" to mean January 1993, the month of the earliest account (1993-01-01). I used the account's branch district, as in the earlier verified queries. There is no tie.

sql:
SELECT m.molecule_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS bond_count
FROM molecule m
JOIN atom a ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id
JOIN connected c ON c.atom_id = a.atom_id
WHERE m.label = '+'
  AND a.element IN (SELECT element FROM atom GROUP BY element HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) = 1)
GROUP BY m.molecule_id
ORDER BY m.molecule_id
answer: Two carcinogenic molecules qualify: TR430 with 6 bonds and TR499 with 1 bond. Rare means an element that appears in exactly one molecule across the whole database. The bond count is distinct bonds touching at least one atom of a rare element, so a bond between two such atoms counts once, and a molecule with several rare elements gets one pooled count. The Atom and Molecule terms the query relies on are still draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM Patient p WHERE p.Admission LIKE '+%' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND CAST(l.ALP AS REAL) >= 300)
answer:
467 admitted patients never had an ALP result at or above the normal ceiling.

I made three choices where the question was ambiguous:
- **Normal ceiling:** The docs give the ALP normal range as N < 300, so I counted a result of 300 or higher as above normal. Using > 300 instead gives the same 467.
- **Admitted:** I counted a patient as admitted when the Admission entry starts with '+'. Requiring exactly '+' gives 464.
- **Patients with no lab rows:** I included admitted patients who have no Laboratory rows, since they never had a high ALP. Counting only admitted patients who have at least one lab row gives 97.

The Terms "Patient" and "Laboratory Test" are still drafts and not certified. The ontology has no Term for alkaliphosphatase, so I used the Laboratory.ALP column directly.

sql: SELECT c.colors, COUNT(DISTINCT l.format) AS legal_format_count FROM cards c INNER JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.id BETWEEN 1 AND 20 AND l.status = 'Legal' GROUP BY c.colors
answer: Among cards with ID 1-20, white (W) cards are legal in 14 play formats and black (B) cards in 10. Color is cards.colors (only single-color B and W appear in this range). A format counts for a color if at least one card of that color has status 'Legal' there; distinct formats are counted. The Card and Card Legality terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT d.A3 AS region, COUNT(DISTINCT d.district_id) AS district_count, SUM(CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER)) AS total_population, SUM(x.n) AS account_count FROM (SELECT a.district_id, COUNT(DISTINCT a.account_id) AS n FROM account a JOIN loan l ON l.account_id = a.account_id WHERE l.duration > 24 AND a.date < '1997-01-01' GROUP BY a.district_id) x JOIN district d ON d.district_id = x.district_id GROUP BY d.A3 ORDER BY total_population DESC, region ASC LIMIT 1
answer: South Moravia has the largest combined population among districts with a qualifying account: 14 districts, 2,054,989 inhabitants, 68 accounts. A qualifying account has a loan longer than 24 months and was opened before 1997-01-01 (account creation date, 1997 excluded). Districts are the account's branch district, and population is district.A4 cast to an integer. Ties would go to the alphabetically first region, but there was none. I did not run validate_sql or lookup_values. The Account, District and Loan terms are still drafts.

sql: SELECT s.code, s.releaseDate FROM sets AS s WHERE s.releaseDate >= '2020-01-01' AND s.releaseDate < '2021-01-01' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations AS t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.language = 'Spanish' AND TRIM(COALESCE(t.translation, '')) <> '') ORDER BY s.releaseDate, s.code
answer:
The query returns 34 rows (set code, release date), which is every set in the database released in 2020 (34 sets in total). None of them has a Spanish set name.

I counted a set as having no Spanish name if it has no 'Spanish' row in set_translations with a non-empty translation. The table contains 24 Spanish rows with a null or blank translation, and I treated those as missing too. The result runs from J20 and PF20 (2020-01-01) to CC1 (2020-12-04). It includes promo, supplemental and online-only sets such as PZNR, AKR and ANB.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT l.ID FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.SC170 IS NOT NULL AND l.Date=(SELECT MAX(Date) FROM Laboratory x WHERE x.ID=l.ID AND x.SC170 IS NOT NULL) AND l.SC170 IN ('negative','0') AND (SELECT MAX(Date) FROM Laboratory y WHERE y.ID=l.ID) > '1997-01-01' ORDER BY l.ID
answer: 16명의 환자 ID를 반환했습니다(944797, 1110526, 4632421 등). 해석 기준은 세 가지입니다. (1) 가장 최근 검사 표본은 환자의 Laboratory 전체에서 가장 늦은 Date이며 1997-01-01보다 엄격히 늦어야 합니다. (2) 가장 최근 anti-Scl-70 결과는 SC170 값이 비어 있지 않은 검사 중 가장 늦은 날짜의 값입니다. (3) 정상은 기존 검증 쿼리 6번처럼 'negative' 또는 '0'입니다. SC170 값이 있는 검사가 전체 28건뿐이라, 값이 없는 날짜를 최근 결과로 보면 대부분 환자가 제외되기 때문에 값이 있는 검사만 대상으로 삼았습니다.

sql: SELECT e.event_name, e.location, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS members_attended FROM event e LEFT JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.type = 'Budget' AND e.status = 'Closed' GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name, e.location
answer:
Fall Budget Review, held at Conference Room BA 452, had 5 members attend.

I read "budget review event" as an event with type 'Budget', and "has held" as status 'Closed'. The club also has a Spring Budget Review (2020-01-12) with status 'Open' and no attendance records. I left it out because it is not closed. If you want it included, remove the status filter and it will show up with 0 attendees.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.driverRef, d.nationality, d.dob, q.q1, CAST(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60000 + CAST(ROUND(CAST(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1) AS REAL)*1000) AS INTEGER) AS ms FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId WHERE r.year=1995 AND r.name='Japanese Grand Prix' AND q.q1 IS NOT NULL AND q.q1<>'') SELECT driverRef, nationality, dob, q1 FROM t WHERE ms=(SELECT MAX(ms) FROM t)
answer: Mark Blundell set the slowest Q1 time at the 1995 Japanese Grand Prix, with no tie: driverRef blundell, British, born 1966-04-08, Q1 time 16:42.640. That time is far slower than any real qualifying lap, so it looks like a data-entry quirk in the source, and I kept the stored value. I excluded rows with a NULL or empty Q1 and compared times in milliseconds. The Driver, Qualifying Result and Race terms behind the query are draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 1) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s JOIN colour AS c ON s.skin_colour_id = c.id WHERE c.colour = 'Green' AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: The average weight of green-skinned heroes is 1354.6 kg. I counted only heroes whose weight_kg is above 0, because the data records an unknown weight as 0 or NULL. I read "green skin" as the exact colour 'Green' and left out 'Green/Blue'. The number is high, so a few very heavy heroes probably pull the average up. I didn't check which ones, so a median may suit a "typical" weight better. The Superhero and Colour terms the query relies on are still drafts, not certified.

answer:
The ten largest 24-month loans on weekly-statement accounts (frequency 'POPLATEK TYDNE'), as district, amount, approval date, end-of-day balance:
1. Strakonice, 192552, 1994-11-12, 14203
2. Prachatice, 189696, 1996-01-01, 88662
3. Prachatice, 140064, 1998-05-12, 68038
4. Beroun, 139488, 1998-12-06, 47956
5. Tachov, 104712, 1995-12-12, 25753

Choices I made:

sql: SELECT CAST(ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg)) AS INTEGER) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero s JOIN hero_attribute h ON h.hero_id = s.id AND h.attribute_id = (SELECT id FROM attribute WHERE attribute_name = 'Strength') WHERE h.attribute_value = (SELECT h2.attribute_value FROM hero_attribute h2 JOIN superhero x ON x.id = h2.hero_id WHERE x.superhero_name = 'Hulk' AND h2.attribute_id = (SELECT id FROM attribute WHERE attribute_name = 'Strength')) AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: 2106589 kg. Hulk's Strength is 100, and 59 heroes share it. I treated weight_kg of 0 (and NULL) as unknown, because 0 kg is not a real weight, and left those heroes out of the average. The result is pulled up by Godzilla (90,000,000 kg) and King Kong (9,000,000 kg), who are in the data. I kept them because you asked for every superhero.

sql: SELECT SUM(totalSetSize) AS total_cards FROM sets s WHERE strftime('%Y', releaseDate) = '2017' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation <> '')
answer: 793 cards in total. Three of the 33 sets released in 2017 have a translated name. I counted each set's full size from `sets.totalSetSize`, which includes promotional and supplemental printings. I treated a set as localized if it has at least one non-empty translation in `set_translations`. None of those translations are in English, so no extra language filter was needed.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS printings FROM cards WHERE power IS NOT NULL AND power NOT LIKE '%*%' AND CAST(power AS REAL) > 3 AND CAST(power AS REAL) <= 10
answer: 6,410 card printings have a power greater than 3 and at most 10. Each row in `cards` counts as one printing. I left out variable powers (`*`, `1+*`, `2+*`, `*²`) because they have no fixed number. The 4 printings with power 3.5 are included, since 3.5 is strictly greater than 3.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT mj.major_id) AS num_majors FROM member m JOIN major mj ON mj.major_id = m.link_to_major WHERE mj.department = 'Political Science Department'

sql:
WITH acc AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.account_id FROM disp d WHERE d.client_id = 3541),
home AS (SELECT district_id FROM client WHERE client_id = 3541),
tx AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(CASE WHEN type='PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS inc, SUM(CASE WHEN type IN ('VYDAJ','VYBER') THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS exp FROM trans GROUP BY account_id),
dp AS (SELECT district_id, A3 AS region, A2 AS name, CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) AS pop, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY A3 ORDER BY CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) DESC) AS rk FROM district),
top AS (SELECT region, name, pop FROM dp WHERE rk = 1)
SELECT a.account_id, a.date AS account_opened_date, a.frequency, d.A2 AS district_name, d.A3 AS region,
 CASE WHEN a.district_id = (SELECT district_id FROM home) THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS is_client_home_district,
 d.A11 AS district_average_salary,
 COALESCE(l.status,'none') AS loan_status, COALESCE(l.amount,0) AS loan_amount,
 COALESCE(tx.n,0) AS transaction_count, COALESCE(tx.inc,0) AS total_income, COALESCE(tx.exp,0) AS total_expense,
 COALESCE(tx.inc,0)-COALESCE(tx.exp,0) AS net_balance,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM client c JOIN district d2 ON d2.district_id=c.district_id WHERE d2.A3=d.A3) AS clients_in_region,
 (SELECT name FROM top WHERE top.region=d.A3 ORDER BY name LIMIT 1) AS most_populous_district_in_region,
 (SELECT pop FROM top WHERE top.region=d.A3 ORDER BY name LIMIT 1) AS most_populous_district_inhabitants,
 dp.rk AS district_population_rank_in_region
FROM acc JOIN account a ON a.account_id=acc.account_id
JOIN district d ON d.district_id=a.district_id
JOIN dp ON dp.district_id=a.district_id
LEFT JOIN loan l ON l.account_id=a.account_id
LEFT JOIN tx ON tx.account_id=a.account_id
ORDER BY transaction_count DESC, a.account_id
answer:
클라이언트 3541이 접근할 수 있는 계좌는 2932 한 개이고, 쿼리를 실행해 결과 1행을 확인했습니다. 이 계좌는 클라이언트 3540이 소유하고 3541은 DISPONENT(공동 사용자)입니다.

- 개설일 1993-05-04, 빈도 POPLATEK MESICNE
- 계좌 지점 지역구는 Olomouc(north Moravia), 평균 급여 8,994. 클라이언트 3541의 거주 지역구와 달라 'No'입니다.
- 대출은 없어서 상태 'none', 금액 0입니다.
- 거래 655건, 총수입 2,821,377, 총지출 2,787,425, 순잔액 33,952
- north Moravia를 거주 지역으로 둔 클라이언트는 920명입니다.
- north Moravia에서 인구가 가장 많은 지역구는 Ostrava - mesto(323,870명)이고, Olomouc의 인구 순위는 4위입니다.

적용한 해석은 다음과 같습니다.
- 접근 가능한 계좌는 OWNER와 DISPONENT를 구분하지 않고 disp에 연결된 모든 계좌로 봤습니다.
- 지출은 type이 VYDAJ인 거래에 type이 VYBER인 거래(16,666건)를 더해 계산했습니다. VYBER는 문서에 없는 값이지만 현금 인출로 보고 지출에 넣었습니다.
- 순잔액은 수입에서 지출을 뺀 값입니다.
- 순위는 지역 내 모든 지역구를 인구 기준으로 RANK()로 매겼습니다(동률이면 같은 순위, 다음 순위는 건너뜀).

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS school_count FROM schools s JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE s.MailCity = 'San Francisco' AND s.School IS NOT NULL AND t.rtype = 'S' AND t.AvgScrRead + t.AvgScrMath + t.AvgScrWrite >= 1500 AND s.DOCType IN ('Unified School District','High School District','Elementary School District','County Office of Education (COE)')

sql:
WITH last AS (
  SELECT cs.constructorId, r.year, cs.points,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY cs.constructorId, r.year ORDER BY r.round DESC, r.date DESC) rn
  FROM constructorStandings cs JOIN races r ON r.raceId = cs.raceId
), tot AS (
  SELECT c.constructorId, c.name, c.url, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(l.points) FROM last l WHERE l.constructorId=c.constructorId AND l.rn=1),0) AS pts
  FROM constructors c WHERE c.nationality='Italian'
), ranked AS (
  SELECT name, pts, url, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY pts DESC) rk FROM tot
)
SELECT name, pts AS career_points, url FROM ranked WHERE rk<=3 ORDER BY rk, name
answer: The top three Italian constructors by career points are Ferrari (6991.5, http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari), Benetton (861.5, http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benetton_Formula) and Toro Rosso (381, http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Toro_Rosso). There are no ties in the top three ranks. Career points are the sum of each season's final standing points, taken from constructorStandings at the last race of each year, because those values are cumulative within a season. Italian means constructors.nationality = 'Italian', and constructors with no points would stay in the ranking with 0. The introduction website is constructors.url, which is the Wikipedia page; the ontology has no Term for it, so I mapped it from the column description. The Terms used (Constructor, Constructor Standing, Race) are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.City FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode WHERE s.EILCode='HS' AND f.`NSLP Provision Status`='Provision 2' AND f.`Low Grade` NOT IN ('P','K') AND CAST(f.`Low Grade` AS INTEGER)>9 ORDER BY s.School
answer:
Two schools match: City Honors College Preparatory Academy (Inglewood) and Tule Continuation High (Alpaugh).

I took "lowest grade served" from the `Low Grade` column in the free-meal data (`frpm`), and kept schools where it is above 9. That follows an earlier verified query that also used `Low Grade`. The status match is exact, so 'Breakfast Provision 2' and 'Lunch Provision 2' are excluded.

The school directory's `GSserved` column sometimes disagrees with `Low Grade`. If you used `GSserved` instead, the result could differ.

sql: SELECT a.buildUpPlayDribblingClass FROM Team t JOIN Team_Attributes a ON a.team_api_id = t.team_api_id WHERE t.team_short_name = 'POR' AND a.date >= '2015-09-10' AND a.date < '2015-09-11' AND t.team_api_id IN (SELECT m.home_team_api_id FROM Match m JOIN Country c ON c.id = m.country_id WHERE c.name = 'England')

sql: select count(distinct artist) from cards where borderColor='black' and availability like '%arena%' and availability not like '%mtgo%' and power glob '[0-9]*' and power not like '%*%' and cast(power as real)>=5
answer: 56 artists. I counted cards with a black border, `arena` in availability and no `mtgo`, across all printings. Power had to start with a digit, so `*`, `1+*`, `∞` and `?` are excluded, and cast to at least 5.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(A11), 2) AS avg_salary FROM district WHERE district_id IN (SELECT a.district_id FROM client c JOIN disp d ON d.client_id = c.client_id JOIN account a ON a.account_id = d.account_id WHERE c.gender = 'F' AND c.birth_date < '1930-01-01')
answer: The average salary is 9045.64. This is the plain average of district.A11 over the 75 distinct districts of branches that hold accounts linked to female clients born before 1930-01-01. Each district counts once. I counted any linked account (owner or disponent). If only owners' accounts counted, the result would be 9061.89 over 72 districts.

sql: SELECT e.event_name, ROUND(COALESCE((SELECT SUM(x.cost) FROM expense x JOIN budget b ON b.budget_id = x.link_to_budget WHERE b.link_to_event = e.event_id AND x.expense_description LIKE '%water%'), 0) * 1.0 / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event = e.event_id), 2) AS water_cost_per_attendee FROM event e WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event = e.event_id)
answer:
The query returns 17 rows, one per event that had at least one attendee. Events that share a name, such as the two 'Football game' events, appear as separate rows. Each amount is the full cost of every expense whose description includes water, divided by the event's attendee count and rounded to 2 decimals. Events with no water purchases show 0 (the numeric value displays as 0.0, i.e. 0.00). Examples: October Meeting 3.01, September Speaker 2.21, Yearly Kickoff 0.94.

Readings I chose:
- Water purchases are expenses whose description contains 'water'. Every match is a "Water, ..." item list, and a purchase that bundled water with other items counts at its full cost.
- All expenses are included. In this data every expense is marked approved, so no filter on approval is needed.
- Expenses are linked to events through their budget line. Events of any status and any date are included.

sql: select count(*) from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) where d.code is null and (length(q.q1)>8 or q.q1>'2:00.000') and (select count(*) from drivers x where x.forename=d.forename and x.driverId<>d.driverId)>=1

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT c.name, COUNT(DISTINCT r.date||'|'||r.text) AS n FROM cards c JOIN rulings r ON r.uuid=c.uuid WHERE c.originalType='Creature - Elf' GROUP BY c.name) SELECT name, n FROM t WHERE n=(SELECT MAX(n) FROM t)

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS patient_count FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE l.TG >= 200 AND p.Birthday IS NOT NULL AND (CAST(SUBSTR('2026-10-09',1,4) AS INTEGER) - CAST(SUBSTR(p.Birthday,1,4) AS INTEGER) - CASE WHEN SUBSTR('2026-10-09',6,5) < SUBSTR(p.Birthday,6,5) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 50
answer: 106 distinct patients. I read "triglyceride" as Laboratory.TG and "at least 200" as TG >= 200 on any lab record. "Older than 50" means completed age on 2026-10-09 is greater than 50, so someone who turns 51 after that date does not count. Patients with no birthday are excluded. Of the 114 patients with a TG of 200 or more, 106 meet the age condition.

answer: 186.43 cm. I counted each player once (distinct players who were ever in the home number-3 slot, height strictly above 180), not once per appearance.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS majors_without_enrolled_members FROM major m WHERE m.college IN (SELECT m2.college FROM member mb JOIN major m2 ON m2.major_id = mb.link_to_major WHERE mb.first_name = 'Tyler' AND mb.last_name = 'Hewitt') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM member x WHERE x.link_to_major = m.major_id AND x.position = 'Member')

sql: SELECT c.Currency, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM (SELECT CustomerID FROM yearmonth WHERE Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201311' AND Consumption > 0 GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT Date) = 11) y JOIN customers c ON c.CustomerID = y.CustomerID GROUP BY c.Currency

sql: select count(distinct coalesce('u'||p.OwnerUserId,'n'||p.OwnerDisplayName)) as user_count from votes v join posts p on p.Id=v.PostId where v.VoteTypeId=8 and v.BountyAmount>=30 and v.CreationDate>='2010-01-01' and v.CreationDate<'2011-01-01'

sql: SELECT CASE MIN(CASE SUBSTR(GSserved,1,INSTR(GSserved||'-','-')-1) WHEN 'P' THEN -1 WHEN 'K' THEN 0 ELSE CAST(SUBSTR(GSserved,1,INSTR(GSserved||'-','-')-1) AS INTEGER) END) WHEN -1 THEN 'P' WHEN 0 THEN 'K' ELSE MIN(CAST(SUBSTR(GSserved,1,INSTR(GSserved||'-','-')-1) AS INTEGER)) END AS lowest_grade FROM schools WHERE NCESDist='0632640' AND StatusType='Active' AND School IS NOT NULL AND GSserved IS NOT NULL
answer: The lowest grade level is K (kindergarten). I read "begins serving students" as the lowest grade in GSserved, the grade span actually enrolled, not GSoffered. One school has GSoffered P-6, but it serves K-6. I counted only active schools and skipped the district-level row, which has no school name. Grades are ranked P < K < 1, so K comes before 1. Including closed schools would still give K.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.name) FROM cards c WHERE c.types LIKE '%Creature%' AND c.leadershipSkills LIKE '%''brawl'': True%' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM cards p WHERE p.name = c.name AND p.isPromo = 1)

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG("aCL IgM"),1) FROM Examination WHERE "Examination Date" BETWEEN '1993-10-01' AND '1993-10-31' AND (',' || REPLACE("Diagnosis",' ','') || ',') LIKE '%,SLE,%'
