sql: SELECT s.full_name FROM superhero s JOIN hero_attribute ha ON ha.hero_id=s.id JOIN attribute a ON a.id=ha.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name='Strength' AND ha.attribute_value=(SELECT MAX(h.attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute h JOIN attribute b ON b.id=h.attribute_id WHERE b.attribute_name='Strength') AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name<>'-' AND TRIM(s.full_name)<>''
answer: The query returns 35 full names. The highest Strength value is 100, and 63 heroes have it. I read "known" as excluding NULL, blank and '-' placeholder full names, which leaves those 35. Examples are Richard Milhouse Jones, Abraxas, Doomsday, Thanos and Thor Odinson.

sql: select d.forename,d.surname,d.url,d.dob,count(q.q3) as q3_count from drivers d left join qualifying q on q.driverId=d.driverId and trim(coalesce(q.q3,''))<>'' where d.nationality='German' and cast(substr(d.dob,1,4) as int) between 1971 and 1985 group by d.driverId order by q3_count desc,d.dob
answer: The query returns 7 German drivers born 1971–1985. Q3 counts: Nico Rosberg 149, Nick Heidfeld 44, Adrian Sutil 19, Ralf Schumacher 15, Timo Glock 13, Markus Winkelhock 0, André Lotterer 0. Q3 data exists only from 2003 onward, so earlier races contribute nothing. Winkelhock and Lotterer tie at 0, and the older one (Winkelhock) comes first. The column list is forename, surname, url, dob, plus the count.

sql:
WITH b AS (
SELECT c.client_id, c.gender, c.birth_date, ca.type AS card_type,
 CAST(strftime('%Y',ca.issued) AS INT) - CAST(strftime('%Y',c.birth_date) AS INT) AS age_at_issue,
 (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=d.account_id) AS loan_count,
 (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(l.amount),0) FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=d.account_id) AS total_borrowed,
 di.A2 AS district_name, di.A11 AS district_avg_salary
FROM card ca JOIN disp d ON d.disp_id=ca.disp_id
JOIN client c ON c.client_id=d.client_id
JOIN district di ON di.district_id=c.district_id
WHERE ca.issued >= '1994-01-01' AND ca.issued < '1995-01-01')
SELECT client_id, gender, birth_date, card_type, age_at_issue, loan_count, total_borrowed,
 CASE WHEN loan_count>0 AND age_at_issue<30 THEN 'Young borrower'
      WHEN loan_count>0 THEN 'Mature borrower' ELSE 'Non-borrower' END AS borrower_class,
 district_name, district_avg_salary,
 RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY age_at_issue DESC) AS age_rank_in_gender
FROM b ORDER BY client_id;
answer:
21 clients were issued a card in 1994 (11 F, 10 M). Only one has a loan: client 3687, a Young borrower with 1 loan totalling 82,896. The other 20 are Non-borrowers.

Readings I chose:
- The client is whoever the card's disposition belongs to, whether OWNER or DISPONENT.
- Loans are counted on that disposition's account.
- District is the client's home district (client.district_id), with the average salary taken from district.A11.
- Age rank within gender puts the oldest first (rank 1 = oldest). It is a competition rank (RANK), computed among these 1994 card holders only. If you meant youngest first, change the order to ASC.

sql: SELECT SUM(SEX='M') AS male_patients, SUM(SEX='F') AS female_patients FROM Patient p WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.GPT >= 60)
answer: 남성 178명, 여성 956명입니다. ALT는 Laboratory.GPT 컬럼이고, 문서에 적힌 정상 범위가 60 미만이라 GPT가 60 이상인 결과가 한 번이라도 있으면 비정상으로 봤습니다. 검사 기록이 없는 환자와 GPT 값이 비어 있는 환자는 비정상 결과가 없으므로 포함했습니다. Patient 테이블에는 성별이 비어 있는 환자 13명이 있는데, 요청하신 대로 남성과 여성만 집계해서 이 환자들은 제외했습니다.

Commander 2020 (set id 44, code C20) has the largest total card count among the 2020 Commander sets, at 322 cards. The runner-up is Zendikar Rising Commander with 142. There is no tie.

sql: SELECT d.driverRef FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId JOIN races r ON r.raceId=q.raceId WHERE r.year=2017 AND r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND (q.q2 IS NULL OR q.q2='') ORDER BY (q.q1 IS NULL OR q.q1=''), q.q1 DESC, d.driverId ASC
answer: 5 drivers were eliminated after Q1 at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, listed slowest to fastest Q1 time: grosjean (1:43.355), wehrlein (1:41.875), ericsson (1:41.732), jolyon_palmer (1:40.646), kevin_magnussen (1:40.489). The Driver, Qualifying Result and Race terms are still in draft status in the ontology.

sql: SELECT d.A2 AS branch, COUNT(*) AS txn_count FROM trans t JOIN account a ON a.account_id=t.account_id JOIN district d ON d.district_id=a.district_id WHERE d.A3='north Moravia' AND t.date<='1998-10-14' AND (t.k_symbol IS NULL OR TRIM(t.k_symbol)='') GROUP BY d.district_id, d.A2 ORDER BY txn_count DESC, d.A2 LIMIT 3
answer: The top three north Moravia branches by transactions with no characterization (k_symbol) dated on or before 1998-10-14 are Karvina (16,820), Ostrava - mesto (16,748) and Olomouc (9,928). I read "no characterization recorded" as k_symbol that is NULL or blank, which matches how earlier verified queries treated it. A branch is the district of the account (A2), and every transaction on every account in the district is counted. There were no ties in the top three.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.atom_id2) AS bonded_atoms FROM connected c JOIN atom s ON s.atom_id = c.atom_id JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = s.molecule_id WHERE s.element = 's' AND m.label = '+'
answer: 81 distinct atoms are directly bonded to a sulfur atom in carcinogenic (label '+') molecules. Reading chosen: count distinct neighbouring atoms, so an atom bonded to two sulfur atoms counts once; sulfur-sulfur neighbours are included. The Atom and Molecule terms used are still drafts, not certified. I skipped validate_sql and ran the query directly.

sql: WITH RECURSIVE items(event_id, item, rest) AS (SELECT b.link_to_event, '', x.expense_description || ',' FROM expense x JOIN budget b ON x.link_to_budget=b.budget_id WHERE b.link_to_event IN (SELECT link_to_event FROM budget WHERE amount>40) UNION ALL SELECT event_id, trim(substr(rest,1,instr(rest,',')-1)), substr(rest,instr(rest,',')+1) FROM items WHERE rest<>'') SELECT e.location, COUNT(DISTINCT lower(i.item)) AS item_count FROM items i JOIN event e ON e.event_id=i.event_id WHERE i.item<>'' GROUP BY e.location
answer:
Campus Common: 1 distinct item. MU 215: 13 distinct items.

Readings I chose:
- Qualifying events are those with at least one budget line where amount > 40. I counted expenses under all budget lines of those events, not only the line over 40.
- Some expense_description values hold several items, such as "Water, chips, cookies". I split them on commas, so each item counts once, ignoring case and spacing. "Bakery - Donuts, muffins" splits into "Bakery - Donuts" and "muffins".
- Locations are pooled across events.

The Budget, Event and Expense Terms used here are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT p.ID FROM Patient p WHERE p.Admission='-' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND (l.RBC<=3.5 OR l.RBC>=6.0)) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>0) ORDER BY p.ID
answer: 5명이 해당합니다: 1180510, 4471732, 4840422, 4915498, 5122312. 기준은 Admission='-', 검사 중 한 번이라도 RBC<=3.5 또는 RBC>=6.0, 그리고 검사 중 한 번이라도 RNP 역가가 0보다 큰 경우입니다. 두 소견은 서로 다른 검사일에 나와도 됩니다. RNP는 텍스트 컬럼이라 CAST로 숫자 비교했으며, 'negative'는 0으로 계산되어 제외됩니다.

sql: SELECT SUM(b.amount) AS total_budgeted FROM budget b JOIN event e ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE e.event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND e.event_date < '2019-10-01' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM expense x JOIN budget b2 ON b2.budget_id = x.link_to_budget WHERE b2.link_to_event = e.event_id AND LOWER(x.expense_description) LIKE '%pizza%')
answer: $965 total budgeted. This sums every budget line (all categories) for events dated 2019-09-01 through 2019-09-30 that had at least one expense whose description mentions pizza. An EXISTS check keeps events with several pizza expenses from being counted twice. The Budget, Event and Expense terms in the ontology are still drafts.

sql: with p as (select ID from Patient where UPPER(REPLACE(Diagnosis,' ',''))='PSORIATICARTHRITIS') select (select count(*) from Laboratory where ID in (select ID from p)) as total_lab_tests, (select count(*) from p where ID not in (select ID from Laboratory)) as patients_without_lab
answer: 건강 기록상 건선성 관절염(Psoriatic arthritis) 진단 환자는 2명이고, 이들의 검사 기록은 모든 날짜를 합쳐 56건입니다. 검사 기록이 전혀 없는 환자는 1명입니다. 진단명은 대소문자와 공백을 무시하고 정확히 일치하는 경우만 포함했습니다(Patient.Diagnosis 기준).

sql: SELECT d.forename, COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverId) AS runners_up FROM results x JOIN races r ON r.raceId=x.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=x.driverId WHERE r.name='Italian Grand Prix' AND x.positionOrder=2 GROUP BY d.forename HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverId)>=2 ORDER BY runners_up DESC, d.forename
answer: Two forenames recur among Italian Grand Prix runners-up: Mike (3 different drivers) and Juan (2 different drivers). I counted distinct drivers, not second-place finishes. I defined runner-up as results.positionOrder = 2 in races named 'Italian Grand Prix' across all years. Counting finishes instead would not change which names appear, but it would raise Mike to 4 and Juan to 3, because some drivers finished second more than once. The same repeat finishers (Alan, Ayrton, Emerson, Jean, Jenson and others) are each a single driver, so they are left out.

sql: SELECT s.FundingType AS funding_category, COUNT(*) AS charter_schools, SUM(f."Enrollment (K-12)") AS total_enrollment_k12, ROUND(AVG(f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" * 100), 2) AS avg_pct_frpm, ROUND(AVG(t.AvgScrRead + t.AvgScrMath + t.AvgScrWrite), 2) AS avg_sat_total FROM schools s LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode AND t.rtype = 'S' WHERE s.Charter = 1 AND s.StatusType = 'Active' AND s.FundingType IN ('Directly funded', 'Locally funded') GROUP BY s.FundingType ORDER BY s.FundingType
answer:
Directly funded: 902 active charters, 372,954 total 2014-15 K-12 enrollment, 63.88% average free/reduced-price meal eligibility, 1350.84 average combined SAT (302 schools with scores).
Locally funded: 340 active charters, 150,022 total enrollment, 44.84% average meal eligibility, 1480.15 average combined SAT (104 schools with scores).

Readings I chose:
- "Charter" means schools.Charter = 1 with StatusType = 'Active'.
- The funding category is schools.FundingType. I left out the 'Not in CS funding model' category because you asked only for directly and locally funded charters.
- Enrollment and meal eligibility come from the frpm table for 2014-2015, and the percentage is the K-12 FRPM rate multiplied by 100.
- Only school-level SAT rows (rtype 'S') are used.
- All active charters are counted. Of those, 123 directly funded and 21 locally funded schools have no 2014-15 frpm row, so they add to the school count but not to the enrollment total or the meal-eligibility average.

sql: select case p.SEX when 'F' then 'female' else 'male' end as sex, count(*) as patients from Patient p where p.SEX in ('F','M') and exists (select 1 from Laboratory l where l.ID=p.ID and l.HGB<10) group by p.SEX order by p.SEX
answer: Female: 87 patients, male: 11 patients. I read "severe anemia" as hemoglobin (HGB) below 10 on any lab test. That is the wiki's anemia convention and the lower bound of the documented normal range (10 < N < 17). The data has no separate severe-anemia cutoff. Each patient is counted once, and patients with a blank sex value are excluded because they fit neither label.

sql:
SELECT e.event_name, printf('%.2f', ROUND(COALESCE(w.c,0)*1.0/a.n,2)) AS water_per_attendee
FROM event e
JOIN (SELECT link_to_event, COUNT(DISTINCT link_to_member) n FROM attendance GROUP BY 1) a ON a.link_to_event=e.event_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT b.link_to_event ev, SUM(x.cost) c FROM expense x JOIN budget b ON b.budget_id=x.link_to_budget WHERE LOWER(x.expense_description) LIKE '%water%' GROUP BY 1) w ON w.ev=e.event_id
ORDER BY e.event_name, e.event_id;
answer:
17 events had attendees, and the query returns one row each, with the same-named "Football game" events listed separately. Water cost per attendee is highest for October Meeting at 3.01 and lowest for Yearly Kickoff at 0.94 among events with water purchases. The other nine events show 0.00, including Community Theater, Food Bank, both Football games and Registration.

I made three choices where the question was open:
- **Water purchases:** an expense counts if its description contains "water", matched case-insensitively. This also catches combined items like "Water, chips, cookies", and each such expense counts at its full cost.
- **Which expenses:** every expense was included. All 32 are marked approved, so no filter was needed.
- **Attendee count:** distinct members in the attendance table for that event.

sql: select s.type, count(distinct t.setCode) as japanese_name_sets from sets s left join set_translations t on t.setCode=s.code and t.language='Japanese' and t.translation is not null group by s.type order by s.type

I counted a set only when its Japanese row has a non-NULL translation. 28 of the 121 Japanese rows are NULL, and the wiki says NULL rows are not translations. Examples: expansion 41, core 7, duel_deck 16, commander 7, masters 5. Eight types show 0: funny, masterpiece, memorabilia, promo, spellbook, starter, token, treasure_chest and vanguard (nine in total).

sql:
WITH t AS (SELECT c.Segment, c.CustomerID, SUM(y.Consumption) AS tot FROM customers c JOIN yearmonth y ON y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID WHERE c.Currency='CZK' AND c.Segment IN ('SME','LAM','KAM') AND y.Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312' GROUP BY c.Segment, c.CustomerID),
r AS (SELECT Segment, tot, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY Segment ORDER BY tot, CustomerID) rn FROM t),
m AS (SELECT Segment, tot FROM r WHERE rn=1)
SELECT ROUND((SELECT tot FROM m WHERE Segment='SME')-(SELECT tot FROM m WHERE Segment='LAM'),2) AS sme_minus_lam,
ROUND((SELECT tot FROM m WHERE Segment='LAM')-(SELECT tot FROM m WHERE Segment='KAM'),2) AS lam_minus_kam,
ROUND((SELECT tot FROM m WHERE Segment='KAM')-(SELECT tot FROM m WHERE Segment='SME'),2) AS kam_minus_sme
answer: SME − LAM = -14009.34, LAM − KAM = 6046.62, KAM − SME = 7962.72. I only counted CZK customers with at least one 2013 row in yearmonth. Customers with no 2013 records were left out, not treated as zero. Ties were broken by the smaller customer ID.

sql: select ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN Birthday>='1960-01-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) AS percentage from Patient where lower(Diagnosis)='psoriatic arthritis'
answer: 50.0%. The registry has 2 patients with psoriatic arthritis. The diagnosis is spelled with two capitalizations, so I matched it case-insensitively. One was born in 1969 and the other in 1955, so 1 of 2 was born in 1960 or later.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) FROM cards WHERE instr(',' || promoTypes || ',', ',release,') > 0
answer: 54 different cards (by card name) have a printing with the 'release' promo type. I matched 'release' as a whole entry in the comma-separated promoTypes list, so 'prerelease' is excluded. Counting by name gives 54. Counting individual printings (uuid) would give 58.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM results r JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId=r.raceId JOIN status s ON s.statusId=r.statusId WHERE ra.year=1962 AND ra.name='British Grand Prix' AND s.status='Withdrew'
answer: 5 drivers had the result status 'Withdrew' in the 1962 British Grand Prix. I counted only that status and did not count other retirements, such as engine or brake failures.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p.SEX = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS female_percentage FROM Patient AS p WHERE p.Birthday IS NOT NULL AND (CAST(SUBSTR('2026-10-09', 1, 4) AS INTEGER) - CAST(SUBSTR(CAST(p.Birthday AS CHAR(10)), 1, 4) AS INTEGER) - CASE WHEN SUBSTR('2026-10-09', 6, 5) < SUBSTR(CAST(p.Birthday AS CHAR(10)), 6, 5) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 55 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.PT >= 14)
answer: 72.73% of the patients are female. The population is patients whose completed age on 2026-10-09 is over 55 and who have at least one lab record with PT >= 14. The docs give the PT normal range as N < 14, so I treated 14 or higher as abnormal. Patients are counted once each, and those with no birthday are excluded. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms I relied on are still draft, not certified.

sql: WITH molecules AS (SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type = '-') SELECT ROUND(AVG(cnt), 4) AS avg_oxygen_atoms FROM (SELECT m.molecule_id, SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'o' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cnt FROM molecules AS m LEFT JOIN atom AS a ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id GROUP BY m.molecule_id) AS t
answer: 2.1613 oxygen atoms per molecule on average, across molecules with at least one single bond (bond_type '-'). Each molecule counts once, and molecules with no oxygen count as 0. The Atom and Bond terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT s.superhero_name, s.full_name FROM superhero s JOIN hero_attribute h ON h.hero_id = s.id JOIN attribute a ON a.id = h.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Speed' AND h.attribute_value = (SELECT MAX(h2.attribute_value) FROM hero_attribute h2 JOIN attribute a2 ON a2.id = h2.attribute_id WHERE a2.attribute_name = 'Speed') AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(s.full_name) NOT IN ('', '-')
answer: 29명이 조건에 맞습니다. 최고 Speed 값은 100이고, 이 값에 동률인 캐릭터는 39명입니다. 이 가운데 full_name이 '-'로 채워진 10명(Angela, Ardina, Beyonder, Black Flash, Hyperion, Living Tribunal, Man of Miracles, One-Above-All, Spectre, Stardust, The Presence 중 해당자)은 본명을 알 수 없는 것으로 보고 뺐습니다. full_name이 NULL이거나 빈 값인 경우도 같은 기준으로 뺐습니다. 결과 열은 superhero_name, full_name 순서입니다.

sql: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Patient WHERE LOWER(Diagnosis) LIKE '%psoriatic arthritis%')) AS total_tests, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient p WHERE LOWER(p.Diagnosis) LIKE '%psoriatic arthritis%' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID)) AS patients_without_tests
answer: 건선 관절염 진단 환자는 2명입니다. 이 환자들의 검사 기록은 전체 기간 합계 56건이고, 검사 기록이 없는 환자는 1명입니다. 진단명이 'Psoriatic Arthritis'와 'Psoriatic arthritis'로 대소문자만 다르게 적혀 있어서 같은 진단으로 묶었습니다.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT u.Id, u.DisplayName, COUNT(b.Id) n FROM users u JOIN badges b ON b.UserId=u.Id WHERE u.Location LIKE '%Germany%' GROUP BY u.Id) SELECT DisplayName, n AS badge_total FROM c WHERE n=(SELECT MAX(n) FROM c WHERE n<(SELECT MAX(n) FROM c)) ORDER BY DisplayName
answer: Bernd Weiss, with 49 badges, is the only user at the second-highest badge total among users located in Germany. I counted a user as located in Germany if their Location contains "Germany", the same rule the verified queries use. I grouped by user ID, so two users who share a display name are not merged.

sql: WITH f AS (SELECT x.milliseconds, x.positionOrder FROM results x JOIN races r ON r.raceId = x.raceId WHERE r.year = 1988 AND r.name = 'Australian Grand Prix' AND x.milliseconds IS NOT NULL AND x.laps = (SELECT MAX(y.laps) FROM results y WHERE y.raceId = x.raceId)) SELECT ROUND(100.0 * ((SELECT milliseconds FROM f ORDER BY milliseconds DESC LIMIT 1) - (SELECT milliseconds FROM f WHERE positionOrder = 1)) / (SELECT milliseconds FROM f ORDER BY milliseconds DESC LIMIT 1), 2) AS percentage
answer: 1.16%. I read "last full-distance finisher" as the last car that completed all 82 laps and has a recorded elapsed time. That is 4th place, at 6,874,764 ms (1:54:34.764). The winner's time was 6,794,676 ms (1:53:14.676), so the winner was (6,874,764 − 6,794,676) / 6,874,764 = 1.16% faster.

sql: SELECT p.ID, CAST((strftime('%Y','2026-10-09')-strftime('%Y',p.Birthday)) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09')<strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)) AS INTEGER) AS age FROM Patient p WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.HCT>=52)>=2 ORDER BY p.ID
answer: 3 patients have at least two lab results with HCT >= 52: ID 2307640 (age 73), ID 3182521 (age 73) and ID 4007151 (age 58). I counted each lab row as one result and took "52 or higher" as HCT >= 52. Completed age is the year difference minus 1 if the birthday hasn't yet occurred by 2026-10-09.

sql: SELECT AVG(1999 - CAST(strftime('%Y', p.Birthday) AS INTEGER)) AS average_age_1999 FROM Patient p WHERE p.Birthday IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l."U-PRO" IN ('3','4','300','>=300','>=1000'))
answer: The average age in 1999 was about 42.4 years (42.409). Marked or worse proteinuria was read as U-PRO values '3', '4', '300', '>=300' and '>=1000'. The 4 rows reading '%%' (saturated dipstick) are excluded because the question's scale doesn't list them. Each patient is counted once, and patients with no birthday are left out. The Patient and Laboratory Terms are still draft, and I skipped the validate_sql step before running the query.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN height_cm > 0 THEN height_cm END), 2) AS avg_height_cm, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN weight_kg > 0 THEN weight_kg END), 2) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero WHERE skin_colour_id = (SELECT id FROM colour WHERE colour = 'Green') AND alignment_id = (SELECT id FROM alignment WHERE alignment = 'Bad')
answer: 초록색 피부의 악당(skin colour 'Green', alignment 'Bad') 6명 가운데 키가 기록된 5명의 평균 키는 194.2cm, 몸무게가 기록된 4명의 평균 몸무게는 161.75kg입니다. 키나 몸무게가 0인 값은 기록이 없는 것으로 보고 평균에서 뺐습니다. 'Green/Blue' 같은 혼합색은 초록색 피부로 세지 않았습니다.

sql: SELECT d.driverRef, COALESCE(SUM(r.points), 0) AS total_points FROM drivers d LEFT JOIN results r ON r.driverId = d.driverId AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM lapTimes l WHERE l.driverId = r.driverId AND l.raceId = r.raceId) WHERE d.forename = 'Robert' GROUP BY d.driverId, d.driverRef
answer: Five drivers are named Robert: kubica 255 points, and doornbos, la_caze, manzon and obrien 0 points each. Points are summed over races where lapTimes has at least one row for that driver in that race, across all seasons. Reference name is drivers.driverRef. Roberts with no qualifying races are kept with 0. The Driver and Race Result terms are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', Date) = '2010' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) - 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', Date) = '2011' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS diff_pp FROM badges WHERE Name = 'Student'
answer: 2010 share minus 2011 share of all Student badges = -9.54 percentage points (2010 is about 9.54 points lower than 2011). Reading chosen: share = year's Student badges / all Student badges across all years (14,847). Badge term is draft (uncertified). I did not run validate_sql.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT uuid, COUNT(*) n FROM rulings GROUP BY uuid) SELECT DISTINCT cards.name, cards.artist, cards.isPromo FROM c JOIN cards ON cards.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.n = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM c)
answer: Two combinations: (Teferi's Protection, Chase Stone, isPromo=0) and (Teferi's Protection, Chase Stone, isPromo=1). I treated each printing as one cards.uuid, counted rulings per uuid, and kept the printings tied for the highest count. The promo flag is cards.isPromo. The Card term used is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT power_id) AS superpower_count FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id=(SELECT id FROM superpower WHERE power_name='Super Strength'))
answer: 154. I used the definition you gave: a power counts if at least one hero with Super Strength holds it, so Super Strength is included. I did not read "only" as "powers no other hero has".

sql: SELECT DISTINCT t.team_long_name FROM Team_Attributes a JOIN Team t ON t.team_api_id=a.team_api_id WHERE a.date>='2012-01-01' AND a.date<'2013-01-01' AND a.buildUpPlayPassing > (SELECT AVG(buildUpPlayPassing) FROM Team_Attributes WHERE date>='2012-01-01' AND date<'2013-01-01')
answer: 128개 팀이 나옵니다. 팀의 2012년 buildUpPlayPassing 값이 2012년 전체 기록의 평균(약 49.33)보다 높은 경우로 해석했습니다. 평균은 2012년 기록만으로 계산했고, 2012년에 기록이 여러 건인 팀도 한 번만 나오도록 중복을 제거했습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS neutral_heroes_with_known_full_name FROM superhero s JOIN alignment a ON a.id = s.alignment_id WHERE a.alignment = 'Neutral' AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(s.full_name) <> '' AND s.full_name <> '-'
answer: 16 neutral-alignment heroes have a known full name. I counted a full name as unknown when it is NULL, blank, or '-'. In the neutral group, 10 rows have '-' and 2 have NULL or blank.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(n), 2) AS avg_languages FROM (SELECT s.id, COUNT(DISTINCT st.language) AS n FROM sets s LEFT JOIN set_translations st ON st.setCode = s.code AND st.translation IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(st.translation) <> '' WHERE strftime('%Y', s.releaseDate) = '2016' GROUP BY s.id)
answer: 2016 年に発売されたセットの名称は、平均 4.74 言語に翻訳されています。2016 年に発売されたセットはすべて対象で、翻訳が 1 言語もないセットは 0 として平均に入れました。翻訳が空欄でない言語だけを数えています。Card Set と Set Translation は草案(draft)の用語です。

sql: SELECT b.bond_type, COUNT(DISTINCT b.bond_id) AS bond_count FROM bond b JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id=b.molecule_id JOIN connected c ON c.bond_id=b.bond_id JOIN atom a1 ON a1.atom_id=c.atom_id JOIN atom a2 ON a2.atom_id=c.atom_id2 WHERE m.label='+' AND a1.element='c' AND a2.element='c' GROUP BY b.bond_type ORDER BY b.bond_type
answer: In carcinogenic molecules (label '+'), there are 843 carbon-carbon single bonds ('-') and 478 double bonds ('='). No triple-bond ('#') carbon-carbon bonds exist among them, so that type doesn't appear in the result. Each bond is counted once, since the connected table lists both directions.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT a.element FROM atom AS a WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM connected AS c WHERE c.atom_id = a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a.atom_id)
answer: Atoms in no bond have five distinct elements: na, cl, h, zn and k. An atom counted as bonded if it appears at either end of a row in `connected` (atom_id or atom_id2). The Atom term is still draft, not certified.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT e.type, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS members FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event WHERE date(e.event_date) BETWEEN '2019-09-01' AND '2020-05-31' GROUP BY e.type) SELECT type, members FROM t WHERE members = (SELECT MAX(members) FROM t)
answer: Meeting and Registration tie, with 30 members each. I counted distinct members per event type, so someone who came to several events of one type counts once. All events fall within Sept 2019 to May 2020, so the date filter excludes nothing.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT h.UserId FROM postHistory h JOIN posts p ON p.Id = h.PostId WHERE p.ViewCount >= 1000 AND h.UserId IS NOT NULL GROUP BY h.UserId, h.PostId HAVING COUNT(*) = 1
answer: 270명의 사용자가 조회수 1,000 이상인 게시글 중 적어도 한 곳에서 이력 항목을 정확히 1건 남겼습니다. 게시글별로 사용자의 postHistory 행 수를 세어, 1건인 (사용자, 게시글) 조합이 하나라도 있는 사용자를 골랐습니다. 조회수 조건은 ViewCount >= 1000으로 해석했고, UserId가 NULL인 행은 제외했습니다.

sql: SELECT name, releaseDate FROM sets s WHERE type = (SELECT type FROM sets WHERE name = 'From the Vault: Lore') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY releaseDate, name;
answer: Three sets share the 'from_the_vault' expansion type with "From the Vault: Lore" and have no non-NULL foreign-language name. They are From the Vault: Dragons (2008-08-29), From the Vault: Transform (2017-11-24) and Commander Collection: Green (2020-12-04). "From the Vault: Lore" has translations, so it is not in the list. I counted a NULL `translation` row as no name, since 231 of the 1,210 `set_translations` rows are NULL.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_api_id) AS player_count FROM Player_Attributes WHERE jumping >= 80 AND date >= '2007-02-22 00:00:00' AND date < '2007-08-31 00:00:00'
answer: 654 players. I counted distinct players, not assessment rows (there are 1,049 matching rows). I included both end dates by using date >= 22 Feb 2007 and date < 31 Aug 2007, because the date column is stored as text with a 00:00:00 time.

sql: WITH latest AS (SELECT player_api_id, preferred_foot, attacking_work_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) AS rn FROM Player_Attributes) SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN attacking_work_rate = 'low' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS low_pct FROM latest WHERE rn = 1 AND preferred_foot = 'left' AND attacking_work_rate IN ('low','medium','high')
answer: 3.9% of left-footed players currently have a low attacking work rate. This uses each player's latest Player_Attributes record (by date, then id). Only players whose latest record has an attacking work rate of low, medium or high are counted. The Player Attributes Term is still a draft.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cards WHERE borderColor = 'black' AND availability LIKE '%mtgo%' AND power IS NOT NULL AND power NOT LIKE '%*%' AND CAST(power AS REAL) >= 10
answer: 83. I counted each card row (printing) separately. A card counts as available on MTGO if `availability` contains 'mtgo'. Variable power (such as '*') and missing power are excluded. The Card Term is still a draft in the ontology.

sql:
WITH RECURSIVE ex AS (SELECT expense_id, link_to_member AS mid, expense_description AS d, cost FROM expense WHERE expense_date >= '2019-10-01' AND expense_date < '2019-12-01'),
split(mid, item, rest) AS (SELECT mid, '', d || ',' FROM ex UNION ALL SELECT mid, TRIM(SUBSTR(rest, 1, INSTR(rest, ',') - 1)), SUBSTR(rest, INSTR(rest, ',') + 1) FROM split WHERE rest <> ''),
kinds AS (SELECT mid, COUNT(DISTINCT LOWER(item)) AS k FROM split WHERE item <> '' GROUP BY mid),
spend AS (SELECT mid, SUM(cost) AS s FROM ex GROUP BY mid)
SELECT m.first_name || ' ' || m.last_name AS full_name, kinds.k AS kinds_bought, ROUND(spend.s, 2) AS total_spending
FROM kinds JOIN spend USING (mid) JOIN member m ON m.member_id = kinds.mid
WHERE kinds.k = (SELECT MAX(k) FROM kinds) ORDER BY full_name
answer: Sacha Harrison bought the most different kinds of items in October and November 2019: 7 kinds, with total spending of $407.90. There is no tie. I counted 2019-10-01 through 2019-11-30, split comma-separated descriptions into individual items, and counted distinct items ignoring case. Spending is the sum of each expense's cost, counted once.

sql: SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM Patient AS p WHERE p.SEX IN ('F','M') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.ALB < 3.5) GROUP BY p.SEX ORDER BY p.SEX
answer:
Female (F): 64 patients. Male (M): 14 patients.

Reading I chose: a patient counts once if any of their lab results has albumin (ALB) below 3.5, so each patient is counted once even with several low results. The 3.5 cutoff is strict, so exactly 3.5 does not count. Patients with no recorded sex (NULL or empty) are left out because the question asks only for F and M. I did not run a separate check on how many unrecorded-sex patients have low albumin. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms used are still draft, not certified.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT sp.power_name AS power_name, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS hero_count FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON p.id = s.publisher_id JOIN hero_power hp ON hp.hero_id = s.id JOIN superpower sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name <> '-' GROUP BY sp.id, sp.power_name) SELECT power_name, hero_count FROM c WHERE hero_count = (SELECT MAX(hero_count) FROM c) ORDER BY power_name
answer:
가장 흔한 초능력은 Super Strength이고, 해당 능력을 가진 영웅은 151명입니다. 공동 1위는 없습니다.

적용한 기준은 두 가지입니다. 첫째, 'full name을 안다'는 full_name이 NULL이 아니고 '-'도 아닌 경우로 봤습니다. 둘째, 출판사는 publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'로 한정했습니다.

이 쿼리가 쓴 용어(Superhero, Superpower, Publisher)는 아직 인증 전(draft) 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT AVG(HCT) FROM Laboratory WHERE Date LIKE '1991%' AND HCT IS NOT NULL AND CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE("U-PRO",'>',''),'=','') AS REAL) >= 300
answer: The average hematocrit is 41.6, across the 1991 lab tests with proteinuria of at least 300 mg/dL. I counted U-PRO values of '300', '>=300' and '>=1000' (a lower-bound reading counts), and I left out tests with no hematocrit. Trace results and values below 300 were excluded. Run directly, the equivalent filter on those three values (without the REPLACE/CAST) gave 41.6. I did not run the exact query returned above.

sql:
WITH r AS (SELECT pa.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) rn
 FROM Player_Attributes pa WHERE date < '2013-07-13 00:00:00'),
c AS (SELECT * FROM r WHERE rn=1 AND defensive_work_rate IN ('low','medium','high') AND overall_rating IS NOT NULL)
SELECT ROUND(100.0*((SELECT overall_rating FROM c JOIN Player p USING(player_api_id) WHERE p.player_name='Landon Donovan') - AVG(overall_rating))/NULLIF(AVG(overall_rating),0),2) AS pct FROM c;
answer: 18.67. Landon Donovan's overall rating on 12 July 2013 was 18.67% higher than the average. I took each player's latest snapshot dated on or before 12 July 2013, so the average includes players whose rating was last updated earlier. I kept only snapshots whose defensive_work_rate is low, medium or high and whose overall_rating is not null. I picked the latest snapshot first and applied the work-rate filter afterward. The percentage is 100*(Donovan − average)/average.

sql: SELECT d.type, COUNT(DISTINCT d.account_id) AS account_count FROM disp d JOIN account a ON a.account_id = d.account_id JOIN district di ON di.district_id = a.district_id WHERE di.A11 > 8000 AND di.A11 <= 9000 AND d.type <> 'OWNER' GROUP BY d.type
answer: Only one non-OWNER disposition type appears in these districts: DISPONENT, with 461 distinct accounts. I used the account's branch district (account.district_id) and the district's average salary (A11 > 8000 and <= 9000).

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.SEX='F' THEN p.ID END) AS female_patients, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.SEX='M' THEN p.ID END) AS male_patients FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE l.Date>='1994-01-01' AND l.Date<='1994-12-31' AND l.GOT<60
answer:
Female: 80, Male: 16.

Reading chosen: "normal GOT" means GOT < 60, per the docs (normal range N < 60). A patient is counted once if at least one of their 1994 tests had a normal GOT. Tests with a null GOT are not counted. One patient in this group has a blank SEX value and is left out of both counts. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still draft (not certified).

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT c.Segment seg, c.CustomerID id, SUM(y.Consumption) tot FROM customers c JOIN yearmonth y ON y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID WHERE c.Currency='CZK' AND c.Segment IN ('SME','LAM','KAM') AND y.Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312' GROUP BY c.Segment, c.CustomerID), r AS (SELECT seg, tot, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY seg ORDER BY tot, id) rn FROM t), m AS (SELECT seg, tot FROM r WHERE rn=1) SELECT ROUND((SELECT tot FROM m WHERE seg='SME')-(SELECT tot FROM m WHERE seg='LAM'),2) AS sme_minus_lam, ROUND((SELECT tot FROM m WHERE seg='LAM')-(SELECT tot FROM m WHERE seg='KAM'),2) AS lam_minus_kam, ROUND((SELECT tot FROM m WHERE seg='KAM')-(SELECT tot FROM m WHERE seg='SME'),2) AS kam_minus_sme
answer: SME-LAM = -14009.34, LAM-KAM = 6046.62, KAM-SME = 7962.72. Reading used: only CZK customers with at least one 2013 yearmonth row are candidates (data ends 201311, so 11 months); zero-consumption rows are included; ties go to the smaller CustomerID. This relies on draft (uncertified) Terms: Customer and Monthly Customer Consumption.

sql: SELECT MAX(cnt) AS max_powers FROM (SELECT s.id, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id) AS cnt FROM superhero AS s WHERE s.weight_kg = (SELECT MIN(weight_kg) FROM superhero WHERE weight_kg > 0))
answer: 18. I treated weight_kg > 0 as "recorded", because 0 and NULL mean unknown. I took the minimum of those weights, kept every hero at that weight, counted each hero's distinct powers (0 if none), and returned the maximum. The Superhero term used is still a draft.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.AdmEmail1 FROM satscores sat JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = sat.cds WHERE sat.rtype = 'S' AND s.DOC IN ('02','03') AND sat.NumGE1500 = (SELECT MAX(a.NumGE1500) FROM satscores a JOIN schools b ON b.CDSCode = a.cds WHERE a.rtype = 'S' AND b.DOC IN ('02','03'))
answer:
High Tech High North County, administrator email ijones@hightechhigh.org (56 students scored at least 1500). There was no tie. The next highest was High Tech High Chula Vista, with 46.

Readings I chose:
- "Directly runs or charters" means districts of ownership type 02 (State Board of Education) and 03 (Statewide Benefit Charter). If you meant only type 02, the top school would be School of Arts and Enterprise (10 students, gnesbitt@thesae.k12.ca.us).
- "Administrator's email" means the first administrator email listed for the school (AdmEmail1).
- Only school-level SAT rows are counted, not district rows.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT u.Id) AS india_users FROM users u JOIN badges b ON b.UserId = u.Id WHERE b.Name = 'Yearling' AND b.Date < '2014-01-01' AND (LOWER(TRIM(u.Location)) = 'india' OR LOWER(TRIM(u.Location)) LIKE '%, india')
answer: 6 users located in India earned a Yearling badge before 1 January 2014. I counted each user once, even if they hold more than one Yearling badge. I treated a location as India if it is "India" or ends with ", India" (for example "Delhi, India"), and I excluded places like Indiana and Indianapolis. I also checked every location containing "india" that had a qualifying badge, and the result is the same 6 users.

sql: SELECT s.code, s.releaseDate FROM sets s WHERE s.releaseDate LIKE '2020-%' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.language = 'Spanish' AND t.translation IS NOT NULL AND t.translation <> '')
answer: 34 sets released in 2020 have no Spanish name, and the query returns each one's code and release date. That is all 34 sets from 2020, so none of them has a Spanish name. I counted a set as having no Spanish name if it has no 'Spanish' row in set_translations, or if that row's translation is NULL or empty. The table has Spanish rows with NULL translations, which I treated as untranslated.

sql: select (max(strftime('%s',t.Date||' '||t.Time))-min(strftime('%s',t.Date||' '||t.Time)))/60 AS minutes from transactions_1k t join gasstations g using(GasStationID) where g.Country='CZE' and t.Price>1000
answer: 3670 whole minutes elapsed, from 2012-08-23 21:20 to 2012-08-26 10:30. I counted every transaction at a gas station in country 'CZE' with Price > 1000, with no product filter, because the question says "fuel transaction at gas stations" and I read that as any purchase there. I used Price as stored, not Amount x Price. The query takes the difference in epoch seconds and integer-divides by 60, so it rounds down exactly. A first attempt using julianday gave 3669 because of floating-point error, so I discarded it.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(UpVotes),2) AS avg_upvotes, ROUND(AVG(Age),2) AS avg_age FROM users WHERE Id IN (SELECT OwnerUserId FROM posts WHERE CreaionDate LIKE '2012%' GROUP BY OwnerUserId HAVING COUNT(*)>10)
answer: 2012년에 게시물을 10개 넘게 작성한 사용자는 268명이고, 이들의 평균 UpVotes는 505.63, 평균 나이는 36.14입니다. 게시물 생성일 컬럼은 철자가 틀린 `CreaionDate`이며, 2012년 여부는 이 값이 '2012'로 시작하는지로 판단했습니다. 게시물 종류(질문, 답변 등)는 구분하지 않고 모두 셌습니다. 나이가 비어 있는 사용자는 평균 나이 계산에서 제외됩니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.Admission = '+' THEN p.ID END) AS admitted_patients, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.Admission = '-' THEN p.ID END) AS outpatient_patients FROM Patient p WHERE TRIM(p.Diagnosis) = 'SLE' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l."U-PRO" IS NOT NULL AND (l."U-PRO" = '%%' OR CASE WHEN l."U-PRO" LIKE '%(%' THEN CAST(substr(l."U-PRO", instr(l."U-PRO", '(')+1, instr(l."U-PRO", ')')-instr(l."U-PRO", '(')-1) AS REAL) WHEN l."U-PRO" LIKE '>=%' THEN CAST(substr(l."U-PRO", 3) AS REAL) ELSE CAST(l."U-PRO" AS REAL) END >= 30))
answer: 13 patients were admitted to the hospital and 1 was followed at the outpatient clinic. Reading used: only diagnosis = Patient.Diagnosis exactly 'SLE' (so 'SLE susp' and 'SLE, SJS' are excluded). Abnormally high proteinuria = any lab record with U-PRO of 30 or more (the documented normal range is 0 < N < 30). Values like '+2(100)' use the number in parentheses, '>=300' uses the number after the symbol, and '%%' counts as high. Each patient is counted once, based on all of their lab records. Admission '+' is admitted and '-' is outpatient. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms used are still draft in the ontology.

sql: WITH r AS (SELECT e.event_name, SUM(b.spent)*1.0/SUM(b.amount) AS ratio FROM event e JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event=e.event_id WHERE e.status='Closed' GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name HAVING SUM(b.amount)>0) SELECT event_name FROM r WHERE ROUND(ratio,9)=(SELECT MAX(ROUND(ratio,9)) FROM r)
answer: Three closed events tie for the highest spent-to-budget ratio: Officers meeting - November, Officers meeting - October and Officers meeting - September. Ratio = SUM(budget.spent)/SUM(budget.amount) per event (ratio of totals), restricted to events with status 'Closed' and a nonzero total budget. The Event and Budget terms are still draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(E."aCL IgM"),2) AS avg_acl_igm FROM Examination E JOIN Patient P ON P.ID=E.ID WHERE (',' || REPLACE(REPLACE(UPPER(P.Diagnosis),' ',''),char(29),',') || ',') LIKE '%,SJS,%' AND E."aCL IgM" IS NOT NULL AND E."aCL IgM" > 0
answer: The average anti-cardiolipin IgM among SJS patients is 2.89. Patients count if one comma-separated item in Patient.Diagnosis is exactly 'SJS' (e.g. 'SLE, SJS'); 'SJS susp' is excluded. All examinations are included regardless of date, and aCL IgM values of 0 or NULL are left out. A looser text match ('SJS' present but not 'SJS ... susp') gave the same 2.89. The Patient and Special Examination terms are draft (uncertified).

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE duelDeck = 'b' AND hasFoil = 0 AND power IS NOT NULL AND power NOT LIKE '%*%' AND CAST(power AS REAL) < 3
answer: 213 cards in duel deck B have no foil version and a power strictly below 3. Cards with NULL or variable ('*') power are excluded. Each printing counts as one card.

sql: SELECT 1.0 * SUM(DOCType = 'Unified School District') / SUM(DOCType = 'Elementary School District') AS ratio FROM schools WHERE County = 'Orange' AND StatusType = 'Merged'
answer: Orange County has 4 merged Unified School District schools and 7 merged Elementary School District schools, so the ratio is 4/7, or about 0.5714. I read "merged" as StatusType = 'Merged' and the district type as DOCType.

sql: select count(distinct hp.power_id) from hero_power hp join superhero s on s.id=hp.hero_id join gender g on g.id=s.gender_id where g.gender='Male' and s.weight_kg>0 and s.weight_kg<70
answer: 102 different superpowers are held by at least one male hero under 70 kg. I treated a weight of 0 as not recorded, as the docs say, and excluded it along with NULL. Without that exclusion, the 0-weight heroes would have counted as under 70.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND l.DNA IS NOT NULL AND CAST(l.DNA AS REAL) < 8
answer: 3 female patients have at least one anti-DNA (Laboratory.DNA) value below 8. I read "below 8" as strictly less than 8, and I counted distinct patients over all their lab visits. The DNA column is text, so I cast it to a number. Every non-null value is numeric, and NULLs are excluded.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(weight), 1) AS avg_weight FROM Player WHERE player_api_id IN (SELECT player_api_id FROM Player_Attributes WHERE preferred_foot = 'left')
answer: The average weight of left-footed players is 166.6 (the database stores weight in pounds). I counted each player once, and treated a player as left-footed if any of their Player_Attributes rows has preferred_foot = 'left'. The 1,121 players whose recorded foot changes over time are included under this reading. The query matches 3,202 distinct players.

sql: SELECT Id, DisplayName, Views, Reputation FROM users WHERE (instr(','||replace(Location,', ',',')||',',',CA,')>0 OR Location LIKE '%California%' OR Location LIKE '%CA %') AND Views = (SELECT MAX(Views) FROM users WHERE (instr(','||replace(Location,', ',',')||',',',CA,')>0 OR Location LIKE '%California%' OR Location LIKE '%CA %'))
answer: Zach (user id 2817) has the most profile views among California-based users, with 1,244 views and a reputation of 9,604. His location is 'San Francisco, CA'. I did not run the final query. I ran a near-identical version (it also matched ', CA, USA') ordered by views, and Zach was first by a wide margin. The runner-up, jbowman, has 1,101 views, so there is no tie. I treated a user as California-based if the location has 'CA' as its own comma-separated part, or contains 'California', or contains 'CA ' (as in 'Santa Monica CA'). This avoids matching 'Canada' or 'Cambridge'. Locations that name only a California city with no state (for example just 'Oakland') are not counted.

sql: SELECT s.type, COUNT(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL) THEN 1 END) AS sets_with_translation, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL) THEN s.totalSetSize END),0) AS total_cards FROM sets s GROUP BY s.type ORDER BY s.type
answer: The query returns 20 set types, sorted alphabetically, each with the number of sets that have at least one non-null set translation and the sum of totalSetSize for those sets. Nine types show 0 and 0: funny, masterpiece, memorabilia, promo, spellbook, starter, token, treasure_chest and vanguard. The largest rows are expansion (61 sets, 14,023 cards) and core (13 sets, 4,584 cards). I chose to count only non-null translations and to take "total cards" from sets.totalSetSize, as the verified queries do, not from a count of rows in the cards table. The Terms used (Card Set, Set Translation) are still drafts, not certified.

sql: WITH q AS (SELECT p.ID, MAX(CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)) m FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE p.Admission='-' AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND p.ID IN (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory WHERE SSA IS NOT NULL AND SSA NOT IN ('negative','0','-','+-')) GROUP BY p.ID) SELECT ID, m AS anti_rnp FROM q WHERE m=(SELECT MAX(m) FROM q) ORDER BY ID
answer: Patient 4915498 has the highest anti-RNP titer, 256, and no other patient ties. I read the question this way: outpatient means Admission = '-'. An abnormal anti-SSA result is any recorded SSA value outside the normal set ('negative', '0', '-', '+-'). Each patient's anti-RNP is the highest value across all their lab records in all years, and I compared those maxima across patients.

sql:
SELECT CASE p.Admission WHEN '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS care_setting,
 SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.RNP<>'negative' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>=4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS with_elevated_anti_rnp,
 SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.RNP<>'negative' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>=4) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS without_elevated_anti_rnp
FROM Patient p WHERE p.SEX='F' AND p.Admission IN ('+','-') AND p.Birthday <= '1976-10-09'
GROUP BY care_setting ORDER BY care_setting;
answer:
Admitted to the hospital: 10 patients with an anti-RNP result of 4 or higher, 328 without. Followed at the outpatient clinic: 11 with, 532 without.

Assumptions I made:
- "Aged at least 50 as of 2026-10-09" means born on or before 1976-10-09.
- A 'negative' anti-RNP result does not count as elevated.
- Patients with no lab results at all fall in the "no such result" column.
- Admission markers other than exactly '+' or '-' are excluded. This leaves out blank markers and the 3 patients marked '+('.

sql: WITH q AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, MAX(CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)) AS m FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE p.Admission='-' AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory h WHERE h.ID=p.ID AND h.HGB<10) GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX) SELECT ID, SEX, m AS highest_anti_rnp FROM q WHERE m=(SELECT MAX(m) FROM q)
answer: One patient qualifies: ID 4915498, female, highest anti-RNP level 256. I read "outpatient" as Patient.Admission = '-'. I read "anemia" as at least one lab row with HGB < 10. RNP is stored as text, so I compared it as a number, and 'negative' counts as 0. The query returns the maximum for each qualifying patient, then keeps the patients whose maximum equals the overall maximum among them. The query returns the level as a number, so it shows 256.0 rather than 256.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) FROM cards AS c INNER JOIN legalities AS l ON l.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.artist = 'Erica Yang' AND l.format = 'pauper' AND l.status = 'Legal' AND (',' || replace(c.availability,' ','') || ',') LIKE '%,paper,%'
answer: 23 printings. Each card row (uuid) counts as one printing, restricted to artist = 'Erica Yang' exactly, pauper legality status 'Legal' (banned or restricted excluded), and 'paper' present in the availability list.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS s WHERE s.publisher_id = (SELECT publisher_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'Blackwulf') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM superhero AS o INNER JOIN publisher AS op ON op.id = o.publisher_id WHERE op.publisher_name <> '' AND o.publisher_id <> s.publisher_id AND o.eye_colour_id = s.eye_colour_id)
answer: 382. This counts all heroes from Blackwulf's publisher whose eye colour is shared by at least one hero from another publisher. Heroes with a NULL publisher or the empty-name publisher don't count as a different publisher. 'No Colour' is treated as an ordinary eye colour. The Superhero and Publisher Terms are still drafts, and I skipped validate_sql before running the query.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics')/COUNT(*),2) AS percentage FROM superhero s LEFT JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id=p.id WHERE s.height_cm BETWEEN 150 AND 180
answer: 60.87% of the 230 superheroes with height from 150 to 180 cm (inclusive) were published by Marvel Comics. Heroes with no publisher stay in the denominator. Missing heights are stored as 0 or NULL, so the range filter excludes them.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND l.DNA IS NOT NULL AND CAST(l.DNA AS REAL) < 8
answer: 3명입니다. Laboratory.DNA를 숫자로 바꿔 8 미만인 검사가 한 번이라도 있는 여성(SEX='F') 환자를 환자 ID 기준으로 중복 없이 셌습니다. 검사 날짜 제한은 두지 않았습니다. 8 미만인 검사 기록은 전체 5건이었고 숫자가 아닌 값은 없었습니다. 사용한 Patient, Laboratory Test 용어는 아직 인증되지 않은 draft 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE ','||keywords||',' LIKE '%,Flying,%' AND ','||keywords||',' LIKE '%,Cycling,%'
answer: 32 card printings have both Flying and Cycling in their keywords. I counted each printing (row) separately and matched the exact keywords, so variants like Islandcycling, Landcycling or Plainscycling don't count as Cycling. Counting those too would give 45.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.Id, p.Title, COUNT(l.Id) n FROM posts p JOIN postLinks l ON l.PostId=p.Id WHERE p.Title LIKE '%principal component scores%' GROUP BY p.Id, p.Title) SELECT Title, n FROM c WHERE n=(SELECT MAX(n) FROM c)
answer: "How do I analyse principal component scores?" has the most related posts, with 3. It is the only post at that count. I counted every postLinks row where the post is the PostId, with no date filter, to cover the full history. The title match is a case-insensitive substring match.

sql:
WITH app AS (
SELECT id, home_player_1 p FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_2 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_3 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_4 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_5 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_6 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_7 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_8 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_9 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_10 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_11 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016'
UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_1 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_2 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_3 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_4 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_5 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_6 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_7 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_8 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_9 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_10 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_11 FROM Match WHERE season='2015/2016')
SELECT p.player_name, COUNT(DISTINCT app.id) AS matches_played
FROM Player p LEFT JOIN app ON app.p = p.player_api_id
WHERE p.player_name LIKE 'Adam%' AND p.weight > 170
GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.player_name
ORDER BY p.player_name
answer: 24 players qualify (name starts with 'Adam', weight > 170 lb, since Player.weight is in pounds). Matches played = distinct 2015/2016 matches where the player's id appears in any of the 22 home/away lineup slots. Players with no appearances are kept with 0. The prefix match also includes Adama/Adamo names (Adama Coulibaly, Adama Francois, Adama Soumaoro, Adamo Coulibaly). Examples: Adam Masina 30, Adam Danch 29, Adam Marusic 26, Adama Soumaoro 25, Adam Banas 0. The Match and Player terms in the ontology are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT l.name FROM "League" l INNER JOIN "Match" m ON l.id = m.league_id WHERE m.season = '2009/2010' GROUP BY l.id, l.name HAVING AVG(m.home_team_goal) > AVG(m.away_team_goal)
answer: All 11 leagues had a higher average of home goals than away goals in 2009/2010: Belgium Jupiler League, England Premier League, France Ligue 1, Germany 1. Bundesliga, Italy Serie A, Netherlands Eredivisie, Poland Ekstraklasa, Portugal Liga ZON Sagres, Scotland Premier League, Spain LIGA BBVA, Switzerland Super League. I compared the per-match average of home_team_goal with that of away_team_goal across each league's 2009/2010 matches. The League and Match terms are still drafts.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rulings AS r JOIN cards AS c ON c.uuid = r.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Mishra''s Factory' AND date(r.date) = (SELECT MAX(date(r2.date)) FROM rulings AS r2 JOIN cards AS c2 ON c2.uuid = r2.uuid WHERE c2.name = 'Mishra''s Factory')
answer: 46. The latest ruling date for Mishra's Factory across all printings is 2016-06-08. On that date the rulings table has 46 rows, 2 for each of 23 printings. I counted rows, so each printing's copy of a ruling counts separately. If you count each distinct ruling text once, the answer would be 2. The Card and Card Ruling terms I relied on are still drafts, not certified.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT s.School, s.DOCType, f.`Enrollment (K-12)` - f.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)` AS d FROM frpm f JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode WHERE s.FundingType = 'Locally funded' AND f.`Enrollment (K-12)` IS NOT NULL AND f.`Enrollment (Ages 5-17)` IS NOT NULL) SELECT School, DOCType FROM c WHERE d > (SELECT AVG(d) FROM c)
answer:
57개 학교가 조건에 해당합니다. 각 학교의 디렉터리(schools) 이름과 DOC 유형을 반환합니다.

선택한 해석은 다음과 같습니다.
- "locally funded"는 schools.FundingType = 'Locally funded'로 판단했습니다.
- 차이는 frpm의 Enrollment (K-12)에서 Enrollment (Ages 5-17)를 뺀 값입니다.
- 평균은 두 값이 모두 있는 locally funded 학교만으로 계산했고, 평균은 약 16.70입니다.

frpm의 'Charter Funding Type' 열을 기준으로 삼으면 평균이 약 17.55이고 49개 학교가 나옵니다. 질문이 이 열을 뜻했다면 결과가 달라집니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 1) AS average_weight_kg, COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: DC Comics superheroes with a known weight average 101.9 kg, based on 156 superheroes. In this database an unknown weight is stored as NULL or 0, so I left out both. I matched the publisher by the name 'DC Comics'.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.skin_colour_id=(SELECT id FROM colour WHERE colour='Blue') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),2) AS blue_skin_pct FROM superhero s JOIN gender g ON s.gender_id=g.id WHERE g.gender='Female'
answer: 2.46% of female superheroes have blue skin. I counted skin colour exactly 'Blue' (not 'Blue/White'), and used all heroes with gender 'Female' as the denominator.

sql: select distinct s.name, s.releaseDate from cards c join sets s on s.code=c.setCode where c.name='Tarmogoyf' and c.frameVersion glob '[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]' and cast(substr(s.releaseDate,1,4) as int)-cast(c.frameVersion as int)>=10
answer: Only one set qualifies: Modern Masters, released 2013-06-07. Its Tarmogoyf uses the 2003 frame, which is exactly 10 years before the release year (inclusive rule). The other printings don't qualify: Future Sight has frameVersion "future", which isn't a year, so I excluded it. Modern Masters 2015, Modern Masters 2017, Ultimate Masters and Ultimate Box Topper use the 2015 frame, a gap of 0 to 3 years. I used the frameVersion column and ignored frameEffects.

sql: SELECT ID, Date, RNP FROM Laboratory WHERE GOT >= 60 AND CAST(RNP AS REAL) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) FROM Laboratory WHERE GOT >= 60)
answer: Patient 1650222, test date 1989-07-18, anti-RNP reading 256. It is the only test with the highest reading among tests with GOT >= 60. I cast RNP (stored as text) to a number for the comparison. Tests with no RNP value or 'negative' were not counted as high readings.

sql: SELECT e.Symptoms, p.Diagnosis FROM Examination e JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = e.ID WHERE instr(',' || REPLACE(e.Diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',', ',SLE,') > 0 AND e.Symptoms IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(e.Symptoms) <> '' AND p.Birthday IS NOT NULL ORDER BY p.Birthday DESC, p.ID ASC, e."Examination Date" DESC LIMIT 1
answer: The youngest qualifying patient has the symptom 'CNS lupus' and an overall (Patient table) diagnosis of 'SLE'. Readings I chose: SLE counts only as a whole item in the examination's comma-separated diagnosis list, so 'SLE susp' is excluded. Symptoms must be non-empty. Youngest means the latest birth date, with ties going to the smaller patient ID and then the most recent examination date. I did not run validate_sql, and the Patient and Special Examination terms are still drafts.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(case when t.k_symbol='SIPO' then t.amount end)/sum(t.amount),2) from trans t join account a on a.account_id=t.account_id where a.district_id=18 and t.type='VYDAJ' and trim(coalesce(t.k_symbol,''))<>''
answer: 93.31% of the outgoing payments that state a purpose, by amount, went to household bill payments (SIPO). I took "Pisek district branch" to mean accounts whose branch is district 18 (Pisek). I took "outgoing" to mean transactions of type VYDAJ. I counted a payment as stating a purpose only if k_symbol is not NULL, empty or a single space. The query uses all dates.

sql: WITH t AS (SELECT e.type, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS members FROM event e JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_event=e.event_id WHERE substr(e.event_date,1,10) BETWEEN '2019-09-01' AND '2020-05-31' GROUP BY e.type) SELECT type, members FROM t WHERE members=(SELECT MAX(members) FROM t)
answer: Two event types tie for the most members: Meeting and Registration, with 30 members each. I counted each member once per type, even if they attended several events of that type. Every event in the records falls between 2019-09-01 and 2020-05-05, so the September 2019 to May 2020 filter keeps all of them.

sql: WITH l AS (SELECT player_api_id, preferred_foot, attacking_work_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) rn FROM Player_Attributes) SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(attacking_work_rate='low')/COUNT(*),1) AS pct FROM l WHERE rn=1 AND preferred_foot='left' AND attacking_work_rate IN ('low','medium','high')
answer: 3.9% of left-footed players have a low attacking work rate. I took each player's latest record (by date, then id) and kept only left-footed players whose latest record has a valid attacking work rate of low, medium or high. Records with junk or missing values were left out of the denominator. I chose to pick the latest record first and filter after, so "current" means the most recent record even if it has no rating.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM Patient p WHERE p.Admission LIKE '+%' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.ALP >= 300)
answer: 467 admitted patients never had an ALP result at or above the normal ceiling. The docs give the normal range as ALP < 300, so I treated 300 or higher as raised. Using strictly above 300 gives the same 467. I counted every admission mark starting with '+' (including '+(') as admitted. Admitted patients with no lab results are included, because they never had a raised value.

sql: WITH latest AS (SELECT player_api_id, preferred_foot, attacking_work_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) AS rn FROM Player_Attributes WHERE date <= '2015-01-01') SELECT COUNT(*) AS player_count FROM latest WHERE rn = 1 AND preferred_foot = 'left' AND attacking_work_rate IN ('low','medium')
answer: 1,795 players. Reading used: each player's latest rating record dated on or before 2015-01-01; preferred_foot = 'left'; attacking_work_rate in ('low','medium'). Players with no record by that date are excluded. The Player Attributes term used is still a draft (not certified).

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(s.Virtual IN ('F','V','C','P')) / COUNT(*), 1) AS pct_virtual FROM satscores t JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode = t.cds WHERE t.AvgScrMath > 400 AND t.rtype = 'S'
answer: 30.4%. 조건에 맞는 학교 1,126곳 중 342곳이 가상 수업을 제공합니다. 학교 단위 SAT 기록(rtype='S')에서 수학 평균이 400을 넘는 학교만 세었고, 교육구 단위 기록은 제외했습니다. 가상 수업을 일부라도 제공하는 학교는 Virtual 값이 F, V, C, P인 학교로 보았고, N은 제외했습니다. 이 조건에서는 F가 4곳, P가 338곳이었습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS schools_ahead FROM satscores s JOIN schools c ON c.CDSCode = s.cds WHERE c.County = 'Contra Costa' AND s.rtype = 'S' AND s.NumTstTakr > (SELECT NumTstTakr FROM satscores WHERE cds = '07618040730051')
answer: 1 school in Contra Costa County had more SAT test takers than California High (435 test takers). I read the CDS code as '07618040730051', because the stored codes are 14 digits with a leading zero. I counted only school-level SAT rows (rtype = 'S'), so district rows are excluded.

sql: WITH p AS (SELECT s.name, s.releaseDate, CASE WHEN c.frameVersion='future' THEN 2007 ELSE CAST(c.frameVersion AS INTEGER) END AS fy FROM cards c JOIN sets s ON s.code=c.setCode WHERE c.name='Aven Mindcensor'), f AS (SELECT * FROM p WHERE fy=(SELECT MAX(fy) FROM p)) SELECT DISTINCT name AS set_name, releaseDate AS release_date FROM f WHERE releaseDate=(SELECT MAX(releaseDate) FROM f)
answer: Amonkhet Remastered, released 2020-08-13. Aven Mindcensor has 6 printings, counting promo sets. Five use the 2015 frame (Amonkhet Remastered, Amonkhet, Amonkhet Invocations and Amonkhet Promos twice). One, in Future Sight, uses the 'future' frame. I treated 'future' as the 2007 frame, so 2015 is newest. Among the 2015 printings, Amonkhet Remastered has the latest release date, so no tie-break was needed. Note that the Card and Card Set terms the query relies on are still draft in the ontology.

sql: SELECT s.City FROM schools AS s INNER JOIN frpm AS f ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode WHERE CAST(s.CDSCode AS INTEGER) = 1611920113902 AND f.`NSLP Provision Status` = 'Breakfast Provision 2' AND f.`County Name` = 'Alameda' AND s.EILCode = 'HS' AND f.`Low Grade` = '9' AND f.`High Grade` = '12'
answer: The school is in Hayward. It is Impact Academy of Arts & Technology, an Alameda County high school with Breakfast Provision 2 status serving grades 9-12. The stored CDS code has a leading zero (01611920113902), so the query compares it as an integer. I used the physical city (City), which matches the mailing city (Hayward).

sql: SELECT MAX(CAST(L.RNP AS REAL)) AS max_rnp FROM Patient P JOIN Laboratory L ON L.ID = P.ID WHERE P.Admission = '-' AND L.RNP IS NOT NULL AND L.RNP <> 'negative'
answer: The highest anti-RNP (anti-ribonuclear protein) value among outpatient clinic patients is 256. I read "followed at the outpatient clinic" as Patient.Admission = '-', and I did not add a thrombosis filter. RNP is stored as text, so I cast it to a number and excluded 'negative' and nulls. The Patient and Laboratory Terms I relied on are still draft, and I did not run validate_sql before run_sql.

sql: SELECT frameVersion, COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cards GROUP BY frameVersion HAVING CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(frameVersion AS INTEGER)) FROM cards WHERE convertedManaCost = 0)
answer: The newest frame version among cards with converted mana cost 0 is 2015, and 25,500 cards in the database (all cards, not just zero-cost) use it. Reading chosen: "newest" means the highest year; the text value 'future' (8 zero-cost cards) casts to 0 and is not treated as newest, since the Future Sight frame (2007) predates 2015. Ties would each be returned with their own count, but there was none. The Card term is still a draft (not certified).

sql: WITH l AS (SELECT player_api_id, MAX(date) AS d FROM Player_Attributes GROUP BY player_api_id) SELECT ROUND(AVG(p.height), 2) AS avg_height_cm FROM Player_Attributes pa JOIN l ON pa.player_api_id = l.player_api_id AND pa.date = l.d JOIN Player p ON p.player_api_id = pa.player_api_id WHERE pa.defensive_work_rate IN ('low','high')
answer: 180.95 cm. This is the average height of players whose most recent rating record has a defensive work rate of 'low' or 'high'. I treated the other stored values as invalid, not as grades. They are numbers 0–9, '_0', 'ean', 'es', 'o', 'ormal', 'stocky' and blanks, and I left them out. Counting them as "not medium" would give a different number.

sql: SELECT u.DisplayName FROM posts p JOIN users u ON u.Id = p.LastEditorUserId WHERE p.Title = 'Examples for teaching: Correlation does not mean causation'
answer: The last editor of that post is Abhilash (user id 43889). I matched the post by its exact title and joined posts.LastEditorUserId to users.Id. The first check query used a looser title match and returned only this one post.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Examination e ON e.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND p.Admission = '+' AND CAST(strftime('%Y', p.Birthday) AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 1945 AND 1989 AND e."ANA Pattern" = 'P'
answer: 4명입니다. 해석은 다음과 같습니다. 입원 환자는 Admission = '+'로 봤습니다(빈 문자열과 '+(' 행은 제외). 패턴이 정확히 'P'인 검사만 포함하고 'P,S' 같은 조합은 뺐습니다. 환자 수는 중복 없이 셌고, 해당 검사 행도 4건이라 결과는 같습니다.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT l.format, c.name FROM cards c JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid=c.uuid WHERE l.status='Banned' AND l.format=(SELECT format FROM legalities WHERE status='Banned' GROUP BY format ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1) ORDER BY c.name
answer: The format is legacy, with 546 banned printing records. Duel is next with 488 and commander has 332. The query returns 102 rows, each pairing 'legacy' with one distinct banned card name. I read "banned card-printing records" as legalities rows with status 'Banned', counted per format.

sql:
WITH rare AS (SELECT element FROM atom WHERE element IS NOT NULL GROUP BY element HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id)=1)
SELECT a.molecule_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS bond_count
FROM atom a JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id=a.molecule_id AND m.label='+'
JOIN connected c ON c.atom_id=a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2=a.atom_id
WHERE a.element IN (SELECT element FROM rare)
GROUP BY a.molecule_id ORDER BY a.molecule_id
answer: Two carcinogenic molecules qualify: TR430 with 6 bonds and TR499 with 1 bond. A rare element is one found in exactly one molecule across the whole database, carcinogenic or not. I counted each distinct bond that touches at least one atom of a rare element in the molecule. If a molecule had several rare elements, their bonds would be pooled, and a bond between two rare-element atoms is counted once.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT b.bond_id, b.molecule_id FROM bond b JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id JOIN connected c ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id JOIN atom a ON a.atom_id IN (c.atom_id, c.atom_id2) WHERE m.label = '+' AND a.element IN (SELECT element FROM atom GROUP BY element HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) = 1) ORDER BY b.bond_id
answer: 查询返回 7 条键，分属 2 个致癌分子（label = '+'）：TR430 有 6 条（TR430_75_76、TR430_75_77、TR430_75_78、TR430_79_80、TR430_79_81、TR430_79_82），TR499 有 1 条（TR499_1_2）。解读：“键包含某元素”指这条键连接的原子中至少有一个属于该元素；“其他分子都没有记录的元素”指在整个数据集中只出现在一个分子里的元素。用到的 Atom、Bond、Molecule 术语在本体里仍是草稿状态，尚未认证。

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM Patient WHERE LOWER(TRIM(Diagnosis)) = 'psoriatic arthritis'
answer: 2 patients have a diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis. The data spells it two ways ('Psoriatic Arthritis' and 'Psoriatic arthritis', one patient each), so the query ignores case. It counts every row in Patient, with no date or follow-up filter.

sql: select distinct d.nationality from qualifying q join drivers d on d.driverId = q.driverId where q.q3 = (select min(q3) from qualifying where q3 <> '')
answer: Finnish. The fastest Q3 time is 1:04.251, set by Valtteri Bottas, and no one else has that time. Q3 times are all in the same m:ss.fff format, so I compared them as text. I left out NULL and empty Q3 values, which mean the driver was eliminated earlier. I used DISTINCT so that a tie between drivers of the same nationality would show that nationality only once.

sql: SELECT MAX(CAST(RNP AS REAL)) AS highest_anti_rnp FROM Laboratory WHERE CRE < 1.5 AND RNP IS NOT NULL
answer: 256. 크레아티닌(CRE) 1.5 미만과 항-RNP 수치가 같은 검사 기록에 함께 있는 행만 대상으로 했고, 'negative'는 0으로 계산했습니다. 쿼리에 쓴 'Laboratory Test' 용어는 draft(인증 전) 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID JOIN Examination e ON e.ID=p.ID WHERE CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 0 AND e.Thrombosis = 0
answer: 4 patients. I counted a patient if any of their Laboratory rows has an RNP titer above 0 and any of their Examination rows has Thrombosis = 0. The question doesn't say how to combine a patient's several rows, so this is my reading. The Patient, Laboratory Test and Special Examination Terms are still drafts, and I did not run any other reading of the question.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT l.ID) AS patient_count FROM Laboratory l WHERE CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 0 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID = l.ID AND e.Thrombosis = 0) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID = l.ID AND e.Thrombosis <> 0)
answer: 4 patients. I counted a patient if any lab record has RNP above 0 (text 'negative' counts as 0) and they have an examination with Thrombosis = 0 and none with a higher thrombosis degree. Counting only patients with at least one Thrombosis = 0 examination also gives 4.

sql: WITH l AS (SELECT p.player_name, a.overall_rating, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.player_api_id ORDER BY a.date DESC, a.id DESC) AS rn FROM Player p JOIN Player_Attributes a ON a.player_api_id = p.player_api_id WHERE p.player_name IN ('Ariel Borysiuk','Paulin Puel')) SELECT ROUND(100.0 * (MAX(CASE WHEN player_name='Ariel Borysiuk' THEN overall_rating END) - MAX(CASE WHEN player_name='Paulin Puel' THEN overall_rating END)) / MAX(CASE WHEN player_name='Paulin Puel' THEN overall_rating END), 2) AS pct FROM l WHERE rn = 1
answer: 15.25. Ariel Borysiuk's latest overall rating is 15.25% higher than Paulin Puel's, calculated as (Borysiuk − Puel) / Puel × 100. "Latest" is the most recent record by date, with the highest id breaking ties. This uses the draft Terms Player and Player Attributes.

sql: SELECT d.number, d.surname FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId = q.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3 <> '' AND q.q3 < '1:38.000'
answer: 7 drivers set a Q3 time under 1:38.000 at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix: 44 Hamilton, 33 Verstappen, 3 Ricciardo, 18 Stroll, 31 Ocon, 77 Bottas and 7 Räikkönen. The number is drivers.number (the permanent career number), not a per-race number. Q3 times are stored as text in m:ss.mmm format, so comparing them as text gives the same result as comparing them as times. Drivers with an empty Q3 (eliminated earlier) are excluded. The query uses draft (uncertified) terms Driver, Qualifying Result and Race.

sql: WITH rare AS (SELECT element FROM atom GROUP BY element HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id)=1) SELECT b.bond_id, b.molecule_id FROM bond b JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id=b.molecule_id WHERE m.label='+' AND b.molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element IN (SELECT element FROM rare)) ORDER BY b.bond_id
answer: The query returns 112 bonds (bond_id, molecule_id). I read "contain an element recorded for no other molecule" as an element that appears in exactly one molecule across the whole dataset. I took "bonds that belong to" such a molecule to mean every bond in a '+' molecule that has at least one of those elements, not only the bonds touching the rare atom.

sql:
WITH RECURSIVE s(id,item,rest) AS (
SELECT expense_id,'',expense_description||',' FROM expense WHERE link_to_member=(SELECT member_id FROM member WHERE first_name='Sacha' AND last_name='Harrison')
UNION ALL SELECT id,TRIM(SUBSTR(rest,1,INSTR(rest,',')-1)),SUBSTR(rest,INSTR(rest,',')+1) FROM s WHERE rest<>'')
SELECT LOWER(item) AS item_name, COUNT(DISTINCT id) AS times_bought FROM s WHERE item<>'' GROUP BY LOWER(item)
answer:
Sacha Harrison has 12 expense records. I split each description on commas into separate items, ignored case, and counted each purchase once per item. The result:

- posters: 4
- chips: 3
- cookies: 3
- water: 3
- travel mug: 2
- alumni glass: 1
- bakery - donuts: 1
- muffins: 1
- pizza: 1
- post cards: 1

Readings I chose:
- "Club money" means every expense she is linked to. All 12 are marked approved, so no filter was needed.
- Item names are lowercased so that 'Cookies' and 'cookies' count as one item.
- 'Bakery - Donuts, muffins' splits into 'bakery - donuts' and 'muffins', because the comma rule applies to every description. If you want it as one item, 'bakery - donuts, muffins', it would count 1 purchase.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(height_cm), 1) AS avg_height_cm FROM superhero WHERE id <> 1 AND height_cm > 0 AND id IN (SELECT hero_id FROM hero_power WHERE power_id IN (SELECT power_id FROM hero_power WHERE hero_id = 1))
answer: 3-D Man과 초능력을 하나 이상 공유하는 히어로(3-D Man 제외)의 평균 키는 339.5cm입니다. 키가 있는 367명을 기준으로 계산했습니다. 키를 모르는 경우는 NULL이거나 0인 값으로 보고 제외했습니다. 데이터에 NULL이 58건, 0이 155건 있습니다. 큰 키 값이 평균을 끌어올렸을 수 있지만, 데이터는 그대로 사용했습니다.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c WHERE c.name = 'Counterspell' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM foreign_data f WHERE f.uuid = c.uuid AND f.language = 'French') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM foreign_data f WHERE f.uuid = c.uuid AND f.language = 'Italian')
answer: 9. Counterspell has 48 printings in total, and 9 of them have both a French and an Italian entry in foreign_data. I counted each printing (each cards row) once, and I read "localization" as a foreign_data entry for that printing.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.artist = 'Erica Yang' AND l.format = 'pauper' AND l.status = 'Legal' AND c.availability LIKE '%paper%'
answer: 23 printings. I counted each row in `cards` as one printing. I included a card if `artist` is 'Erica Yang', its pauper status in `legalities` is 'Legal' (not 'Banned'), and `availability` contains 'paper'. This includes cards that are also on MTGO or Arena.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.ID FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND l.CPK < 250 AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND l.RNP <> 'negative' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 4 ORDER BY p.ID
answer: 7 outpatient ids: 2320830, 3175008, 4018722, 4398703, 4915498, 5122312, 5400270. Assumptions: outpatient = Admission '-'; CPK < 250 and RNP > 4 must hold on the same lab record; 'negative' RNP excluded (no antibody). The anti-RNP concept had no ontology Term, so I used Laboratory.RNP directly; Patient and Laboratory Terms are drafts.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.element = 'i' THEN a.atom_id END) AS iodine_atoms, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a.element = 's' THEN a.atom_id END) AS sulfur_atoms FROM connected AS c INNER JOIN bond AS b ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id INNER JOIN atom AS a ON a.atom_id = c.atom_id WHERE b.bond_type = '-' AND a.element IN ('i','s')
answer: 3 iodine atoms and 77 sulfur atoms take part in at least one single bond. The `connected` table stores every bond in both directions, so matching on `atom_id` covers every atom in a bond. I counted distinct atom IDs per element, with element 'i' for iodine, 's' for sulfur, and bond_type '-' for single bonds. The Atom and Bond ontology Terms I used are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM atom a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a.element = 'f') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct FROM molecule m WHERE m.label = '+'
answer: 99.34% of carcinogenic molecules (label '+') contain no fluorine atoms (element 'f'). That is 151 of 152 molecules. The Atom and Molecule terms used are still drafts.

sql: select forename, surname from results join drivers using(driverId) where dob>='1980-01-01' and dob<'1991-01-01' and fastestLapSpeed is not null group by driverId order by max(cast(fastestLapSpeed as real)) desc, dob, surname limit 3
answer: Fernando Alonso (253.874), Antônio Pizzonia (253.566), Jenson Button (252.262). I read "born between 1980 and 1990" as dob from 1980-01-01 through 1990-12-31. fastestLapSpeed is stored as text, so I cast it to a number before taking each driver's maximum.

sql: WITH pc AS (SELECT g.gender AS gender, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id) AS n FROM superhero s JOIN gender g ON g.id = s.gender_id WHERE g.gender IN ('Male','Female') AND s.full_name IS NOT NULL AND s.full_name <> '-') SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN gender='Male' THEN n END),2) AS male_avg, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN gender='Female' THEN n END),2) AS female_avg FROM pc
answer: Male: 8.49, Female: 6.83. Heroes with a documented full name are those whose full_name is neither NULL nor '-'. Heroes with no power records count as 0 powers, so each average covers every such hero of that gender. The Gender and Superhero terms used are still drafts. I did not run validate_sql before run_sql.

sql: WITH l AS (SELECT player_api_id, preferred_foot, attacking_work_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) rn FROM Player_Attributes WHERE date <= '2015-01-01') SELECT COUNT(*) AS player_count FROM l WHERE rn=1 AND preferred_foot='left' AND attacking_work_rate IN ('low','medium')
answer: 1,795명입니다. 2015년 1월 1일 이전(당일 포함)의 가장 최근 Player_Attributes 기록을 선수별로 하나만 골라, 그 기록에서 preferred_foot가 'left'이고 attacking_work_rate가 'low' 또는 'medium'인 선수를 셌습니다. 'None', 'norm' 같은 비정상 값과 null은 low/medium이 아니므로 제외했습니다.

sql: SELECT c.County, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM schools s WHERE s.County=c.County AND s.Virtual='F') AS n FROM (SELECT 'Santa Barbara' AS County UNION SELECT County FROM schools WHERE CAST(CDSCode AS INTEGER)=1100170109835) c ORDER BY n DESC, c.County;
answer: Santa Barbara County has 1 exclusive-virtual school (Virtual = 'F'). Alameda County, where school 1100170109835 is located, has 0. I included Alameda with a count of 0 rather than dropping it. Santa Barbara is listed first because it has the larger count.

sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t.k_symbol = 'SIPO' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) / SUM(t.amount), 2) AS sipo_pct
FROM trans t
JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id
JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id
WHERE d.A2 = 'Pisek' AND t.type = 'VYDAJ' AND t.k_symbol IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(t.k_symbol) <> ''
answer: 93.31% of the total amount of outgoing payments with a stated purpose from Pisek-branch accounts went to SIPO household payments.
