 WHERE d.A3=(SELECT A3 FROM district WHERE A2='Litomerice')
  AND ac.date>='1996-01-01' AND ac.date<='1996-12-31'),
g AS (SELECT name, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(AVG(bal),2) av FROM a GROUP BY name)
SELECT name AS district_name, n AS accounts_opened_1996, av AS avg_balance FROM g
UNION ALL SELECT 'REGION AVERAGE', COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(bal),2) FROM a
UNION ALL SELECT 'TOP DISTRICT: '||name, n, av FROM (SELECT * FROM g ORDER BY av DESC, name LIMIT 1)
answer:
Litomerice is in north Bohemia. 147 accounts were opened there in 1996, across 10 districts. The query returns the 10 district rows in name order, then two labeled summary rows, so that all the requested figures come from one query.

District averages of end-of-1996 balance (accounts opened in 1996):
- Ceska Lipa: 18 accounts, 31357.06
- Chomutov: 18, 29084.28
- Decin: 12, 34289.08
- Jablonec n. Nisou: 15, 26449.40
- Liberec: 21, 36765.81
- Litomerice: 9, 27278.67
- Louny: 15, 28686.00
- Most: 12, 31364.25
- Teplice: 15, 35322.07
- Usti nad Labem: 12, 35476.25

The region-wide average across all 147 accounts is 31809.19. The district with the highest average is Liberec at 36765.81, with no tie.

The balance used is the one on each account's last transaction dated on or before 1996-12-31, with the highest trans_id breaking ties on that date. Accounts with no transaction by then would be left out of the averages but still counted. I did not check whether any such accounts exist.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 2) FROM superhero AS s WHERE s.superhero_name <> '3-D Man' AND s.weight_kg > 0 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp JOIN hero_power AS hp0 ON hp0.power_id = hp.power_id JOIN superhero AS d ON d.id = hp0.hero_id WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id AND d.superhero_name = '3-D Man')
answer: 282411.79 kg. This is the average weight of heroes other than 3-D Man who share at least one superpower with him. I excluded heroes whose weight is 0 or NULL. The result includes an extreme outlier weight (the column's maximum is 90,000,000), which I kept because the question didn't ask to exclude outliers. The Superhero term used is still a draft.

sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname FROM qualifying AS q INNER JOIN drivers AS d ON q.driverId = d.driverId INNER JOIN races AS r ON q.raceId = r.raceId INNER JOIN circuits AS c ON r.circuitId = c.circuitId WHERE c.name = 'Marina Bay Street Circuit' AND r.year = 2008 AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3 <> '' ORDER BY q.q3 ASC LIMIT 1
answer: Felipe Massa recorded the fastest Q3 time at Marina Bay Street Circuit in 2008. I took "fastest" to mean the lowest non-empty q3 value. The q3 times are M:SS.mmm text, so they sort correctly as text. The query relies on draft (not certified) Terms: Circuit, Driver, Qualifying Result and Race.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM Patient p WHERE TRIM(p.Diagnosis)='MCTD' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.PLT>100 AND l.PLT<400) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>5)
answer: 1 patient. I read "MCTD alone" as a Patient.Diagnosis that is exactly 'MCTD', which excludes entries like 'MCTD susp' or 'MCTD, SJS'. A normal platelet count is 100 < PLT < 400, taken from docs/Laboratory.csv. Anti-RNP above 5 is CAST(RNP AS REAL) > 5, so 'negative' counts as 0. The two conditions can come from different lab dates.

sql: SELECT s.id, s.name, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT st.language) FROM set_translations st WHERE st.setCode = s.code AND st.translation IS NOT NULL) AS language_count FROM sets s WHERE s.type = 'commander' AND s.releaseDate >= '2020-01-01' AND s.releaseDate <= '2020-12-31' AND s.totalSetSize = (SELECT MAX(totalSetSize) FROM sets WHERE type = 'commander' AND releaseDate >= '2020-01-01' AND releaseDate <= '2020-12-31') ORDER BY s.id ASC
answer: Commander 2020 (set id 44) has the highest total card count among 2020 Commander-type sets, at 322 cards (sets.totalSetSize). The runner-up, Zendikar Rising Commander (id 549), has 142, so there is no tie. Its language count is 0: I counted distinct languages with a non-null translation in set_translations, and the database has no translation rows for this set. The 0 may mean translations were not recorded rather than that none exist. The Card Set and Set Translation terms in the ontology are still drafts.

sql: SELECT DISTINCT c.bond_id FROM connected c JOIN atom a1 ON a1.atom_id=c.atom_id JOIN atom a2 ON a2.atom_id=c.atom_id2 WHERE (a1.element='p' AND a2.element='n') OR (a1.element='n' AND a2.element='p')
answer: 6개 결합이 인(p)과 질소(n)를 잇습니다: TR032_2_3, TR032_3_5, TR058_1_3, TR058_1_4, TR058_1_5, TR298_1_5. 질문이 결합 자체를 묻는다고 보아 bond_id만 반환했고, 연결된 두 원자 중 하나는 p, 다른 하나는 n인 결합을 기준으로 했습니다(방향 무관).

sql: SELECT s.AvgScrMath, s.NumTstTakr FROM schools c JOIN satscores s ON s.cds = c.CDSCode WHERE c.CDSCode = '01611190130609' AND c.FundingType = 'Directly funded'
answer: CDS 1611190130609 (stored as '01611190130609') is a directly funded school. Its average SAT math score is 593, and 20 students took the SAT. The query returns no row if the school is not directly funded, which matches the "no answer" condition. I matched the CDS code as text with the leading zero. The filter is FundingType = 'Directly funded', and I did not add a separate Charter = 1 check. The ontology Terms used (SAT Score Record, School) are still draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.height_cm>0 THEN s.height_cm END),1) AS avg_height_cm, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg>0 THEN s.weight_kg END),1) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON s.publisher_id=p.id WHERE p.publisher_name='George Lucas'
answer: George Lucas's heroes average 187.2 cm in height and 83.0 kg in weight. I read "heroes he created" as the heroes whose publisher is 'George Lucas'. The database stores unknown height or weight as 0 or NULL, so I excluded both and averaged each measure separately over the heroes with a known value.

sql: SELECT a.date FROM Player p JOIN Player_Attributes a ON a.player_api_id = p.player_api_id WHERE p.player_name = 'Kevin Constant' ORDER BY a.crossing DESC, a.date ASC LIMIT 1
answer: Kevin Constant's highest crossing score is 82, first recorded on 2013-02-15 00:00:00. It was recorded again on 2013-03-08 and 2013-03-28. I read "first" as the earliest date at that maximum score. I didn't open the wiki or docs; I only queried the database directly.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers FROM (SELECT c.CustomerID FROM customers c JOIN yearmonth y ON y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID WHERE c.Segment='KAM' AND c.Currency='CZK' AND y.Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312' GROUP BY c.CustomerID HAVING SUM(y.Consumption)>1000000)
answer: 335 KAM-segment customers paying in CZK had total 2013 consumption above 1,000,000. I summed each customer's monthly consumption for 201301 to 201312 and counted only totals strictly above 1,000,000.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS female_admitted_patients FROM Patient WHERE SEX='F' AND Admission LIKE '+%' AND "First Date">='1998-01-01' AND "First Date"<='1998-12-31'
answer: 16 female patients had a first visit in 1998 and were admitted. I counted Admission values '+' (13 patients) and '+(' (3 patients) as admitted, since '+(' looks like a variant of '+'. I left out patients with a blank Admission value. Only SEX = 'F' counts, so blank sex is excluded.

sql: SELECT p.player_name FROM Player p WHERE p.height IN ((SELECT MAX(height) FROM Player),(SELECT MIN(height) FROM Player)) ORDER BY (SELECT AVG(finishing) FROM Player_Attributes a WHERE a.player_api_id=p.player_api_id) DESC LIMIT 1
answer: Juan Quero. He is the shortest player (157 cm) and averages 60.9 finishing across his assessments. The tallest player, Kristof van Hout (208 cm), averages 15.5. Each extreme height belongs to exactly one player.

sql: SELECT t.AvgScrMath, t.NumTstTakr FROM schools s JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE CAST(s.CDSCode AS INTEGER) = 1611190130609 AND s.FundingType = 'Directly funded'
answer: Alameda Community Learning Center (CDS 01611190130609, stored with a leading zero) is a directly funded charter school. Its average SAT math score is 593, and 20 students took the SAT. I matched the code by integer value because the stored code has a leading zero. The query returns no row if the school is not directly funded.

sql: SELECT s.School, f.`Low Grade` AS lowest_grade, f.`Enrollment (K-12)` AS enrollment_k12, COALESCE(t.NumTstTakr, 0) AS sat_test_takers FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode LEFT JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE s.SOCType = 'State Special Schools' ORDER BY CASE f.`Low Grade` WHEN 'P' THEN -1 WHEN 'K' THEN 0 ELSE CAST(f.`Low Grade` AS INTEGER) END DESC, f.`Enrollment (K-12)` DESC, s.School ASC LIMIT 1
answer: California School for the Blind starts at the latest grade among the 3 state special schools (SOCType 'State Special Schools'). Its lowest grade is 1, its K-12 enrollment is 60, and it has 0 SAT test takers because it has no SAT record. Grades are ordered P, K, then 1 to 12. Ties go to the larger enrollment, then to the name that comes first alphabetically. The ontology terms used (School, Free or Reduced Price Meal Record, SAT Score Record) are still drafts.

sql: WITH l AS (SELECT preferred_foot, attacking_work_rate w, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) rn FROM Player_Attributes) SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(w='low')/COUNT(*),1) AS low_attacking_pct FROM l WHERE rn=1 AND preferred_foot='left' AND w IN ('low','medium','high')
answer: 3.9% of left-footed players have a low attacking work rate. That is out of 2,426 left-footed players whose latest record has a valid rating. I took each player's latest record by date, using the highest id to break ties. Both the preferred foot and the work rate come from that record. Players whose latest record has no rating, or a junk value such as 'le', 'norm', 'stoc' or 'y', are left out of the share.

sql:
WITH top5 AS (SELECT district_id, A2 FROM district ORDER BY CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) DESC LIMIT 5),
avgs AS (SELECT t.A2 AS name, 1.0*COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN l.status IN ('C','D') THEN l.amount END),0)/COUNT(a.account_id) AS av FROM top5 t JOIN account a ON a.district_id=t.district_id LEFT JOIN loan l ON l.account_id=a.account_id GROUP BY t.district_id, t.A2)
SELECT name, CAST(ROUND(av) AS INTEGER) AS avg_active_loan_per_account FROM avgs WHERE av=(SELECT MAX(av) FROM avgs)
answer: Brno - mesto has the heaviest active-lending burden among the five most populous districts, at 27,752 koruna of active loan per account. I read the question as asking only for the top district among the five, with ties included, so the result has one row. Active loans are those with status C or D. The average is over all accounts in the branch district, including accounts with no loan. The Account, District and Loan ontology terms are drafts, not certified.

sql:
WITH top AS (SELECT l.loan_id, a.district_id FROM loan l JOIN account a ON a.account_id=l.account_id WHERE l.duration=24 AND a.frequency='POPLATEK TYDNE' ORDER BY l.amount DESC, l.loan_id ASC LIMIT 10),
d AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.district_id, CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER) pop, d.A11 sal FROM district d JOIN top t ON t.district_id=d.district_id)
SELECT (SELECT district_id FROM d ORDER BY pop DESC, district_id ASC LIMIT 1) AS district_id,
(SELECT pop FROM d ORDER BY pop DESC, district_id ASC LIMIT 1) AS inhabitants,
(SELECT ROUND(AVG(sal),2) FROM d) AS avg_salary
answer: 가장 인구가 많은 지구는 district_id 70이고, 인구는 285,387명입니다. 상위 10건 대출이 속한 지구들의 평균 급여는 8,985.75입니다. 24개월, 주 단위 발급('POPLATEK TYDNE') 대출을 승인액 내림차순, 동액이면 loan_id 오름차순으로 정렬해 10건을 뽑았습니다. 지구는 계좌의 district_id(지점 소재지)로 보았고, 평균 급여는 중복을 뺀 지구별 A11의 단순 평균입니다(대출 건수 가중 없음). 인구(A4)는 텍스트라 정수로 변환해 비교했습니다. 쿼리는 실행해 결과를 확인했지만 validate_sql은 거치지 않았고, 사용한 Term(Loan, Account, District)은 draft 상태입니다.

sql: SELECT m.first_name, m.last_name FROM member m JOIN attendance a ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_event) > 7
answer: 29명의 학생이 8개 이상의 행사에 참석했습니다. 예를 들면 Grant Gilmour, Luisa Guidi, Connor Hilton, Tyler Hewitt 등입니다. 이름은 first_name, last_name 두 열로 냈고, 'more than 7'은 8개 이상으로 해석했습니다. 참석 기록(attendance)에서 서로 다른 행사를 센 값 기준입니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(SEX='F')/COUNT(*),1) AS female_pct FROM Patient p WHERE SEX IN ('F','M') AND CAST(SUBSTR(Birthday,1,4) AS INT) BETWEEN 1936 AND 1956 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.CPK>=250)
answer: 85.3% of the group are women (353 women out of 414 men and women). I counted patients born in 1936–1956 by birth year. Patients with no CPK results count as never above normal, and any CPK of 250 or higher excludes a patient. Patients with a blank sex value (13 in the whole registry) are left out of the denominator, since the question asks for the share of men and women only.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.City FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode WHERE s.EILCode = 'HS' AND f.`NSLP Provision Status` = 'Provision 2' AND f.`Low Grade` IN ('10','11','12') ORDER BY s.School
answer: Two schools match: City Honors College Preparatory Academy (Inglewood) and Tule Continuation High (Alpaugh). I took "lowest grade served" from frpm.`Low Grade` and read "above ninth grade" as 10, 11 or 12; 'Adult' is not counted. The status was matched exactly as 'Provision 2'. I skipped validate_sql, though run_sql returned no warnings. The Terms used are still drafts.

sql: SELECT d.type, COUNT(DISTINCT d.account_id) AS account_count FROM disp d JOIN account a ON a.account_id = d.account_id JOIN district di ON di.district_id = a.district_id WHERE d.type <> 'OWNER' AND di.A11 > 8000 AND di.A11 <= 9000 GROUP BY d.type
answer: DISPONENT is the only non-OWNER type, with 461 distinct accounts. I took "district" to mean the district of the account's branch (account.district_id), and average salary to be A11. If you meant the district where the client lives instead, the count would be 475.

sql: select distinct d.nationality from qualifying q join drivers d using(driverId) where q.raceId=981 and q.q2 like '%:%.%' and q.q2=(select min(q2) from qualifying where raceId=981 and q2 like '%:%.%')
answer: British. I used raceId 981 (2017 Italian Grand Prix) and compared Q2 times as text after dropping empty and NULL values. The query returns one row, so there was no tie.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient p WHERE p.Admission = '-' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.RA IN ('-', '+-')) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Examination e WHERE e.ID = p.ID AND (e.KCT = '+' OR e.RVVT = '+' OR e.LAC = '+'))
answer: 128 patients. I read "Rheumatoid Factor" as the Laboratory.RA column, because the docs label RA that way. The Laboratory.RF column is RAHA, a different test. I counted a patient as normal if at least one lab record has RA of '-' or '+-'. I counted a patient as having a positive coagulation measure if any examination has KCT, RVVT or LAC equal to '+'. Patients with no examinations are therefore included. If you required every recorded RA result to be normal, the count would be 98.

sql: select sum(cr.points) as score, c.name, c.nationality from constructorResults cr join races r using(raceId) join constructors c using(constructorId) where r.name='Monaco Grand Prix' and r.year between 1980 and 2010 group by c.constructorId order by score desc limit 1
answer: McLaren (British) scored the most points at the Monaco Grand Prix from 1980 to 2010, with 218.5. I read "between 1980 and 2010" as inclusive and summed constructorResults points per constructor. Ferrari was second with 194.5.

sql:
WITH att AS (SELECT link_to_event, COUNT(DISTINCT link_to_member) n FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event),
w AS (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) n FROM attendance a JOIN event e ON e.event_id=a.link_to_event WHERE e.event_name='Women''s Soccer'),
avgf AS (SELECT ROUND(AVG(COALESCE(att.n,0)),1) v FROM event e LEFT JOIN att ON att.link_to_event=e.event_id WHERE substr(e.event_date,1,10) BETWEEN '2019-09-01' AND '2019-11-30')
SELECT w.n AS womens_soccer_attendees, avgf.v AS fall_2019_avg_attendance, CASE WHEN w.n>avgf.v THEN 'more' WHEN w.n<avgf.v THEN 'fewer' ELSE 'equal' END AS verdict FROM w, avgf
answer: Women's Soccer (2019-10-05) had 17 attendees. The fall 2019 average (1 Sep to 30 Nov 2019) is 16.1 per event, so the verdict is 'more'. The average includes events with no attendance records, counted as 0. I compared event dates by their date part, so events on 30 Nov are included despite the time suffix. There is only one event named Women's Soccer.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c JOIN sets s ON c.setCode=s.code WHERE substr(c.originalReleaseDate,1,4)='2014' AND s.mtgoCode IS NOT NULL AND s.mtgoCode<>''
answer: 293 card printings were originally released in 2014 and belong to a set with an MTGO code. I used the year of cards.originalReleaseDate, so cards with no original release date are excluded. A set counts only if mtgoCode is non-null and non-empty. Each card row is counted once, so the same card name in two sets counts twice. The Card and Card Set terms it relies on are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(Birthday>='1960-01-01')/COUNT(*),1) AS percentage FROM Patient WHERE UPPER(REPLACE(Diagnosis,' ',''))='PSORIATICARTHRITIS'
answer: 50.0%. Two patients have a Patient.Diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis. The spelling differs in case ('Psoriatic Arthritis' and 'Psoriatic arthritis'), so I matched case-insensitively. One was born in 1969 and the other in 1955. "1960 or later" is counted as Birthday on or after 1960-01-01.

sql: WITH b AS (SELECT s.School AS School, s.DOCType AS DOCType, f."Enrollment (K-12)" - f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" AS d FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode WHERE s.FundingType = 'Locally funded' AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" IS NOT NULL AND f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" IS NOT NULL) SELECT School, DOCType FROM b WHERE d > (SELECT AVG(d) FROM b)
answer:
The query returns 57 schools, each with its name (schools.School) and DOC type (schools.DOCType). Their K-12 minus ages 5-17 enrollment difference is above the average for locally funded schools.

I made three choices where the question was open:
- "Locally funded" is read from schools.FundingType. The frpm table has its own "Charter Funding Type" column that disagrees for about 47 schools. Using it instead gave 49 schools in a quick count.
- The average covers only locally funded schools with both enrollment figures present.
- "Exceeds" means strictly greater than the average.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 2) AS avg_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id INNER JOIN attribute AS a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Intelligence' AND s.weight_kg > 0 AND ha.attribute_value IN (SELECT ha2.attribute_value FROM superhero AS s2 INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS ha2 ON ha2.hero_id = s2.id INNER JOIN attribute AS a2 ON a2.id = ha2.attribute_id WHERE s2.superhero_name = 'Abomination' AND a2.attribute_name = 'Intelligence')
answer: The average weight is 103.6 kg for heroes with the same Intelligence score as Abomination. The cohort includes Abomination, and heroes with no recorded weight (0 or NULL) are excluded. The Terms used are drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS good_non_dc_heroes FROM superhero s JOIN alignment a ON a.id=s.alignment_id LEFT JOIN publisher p ON p.id=s.publisher_id WHERE a.alignment='Good' AND (p.publisher_name IS NULL OR p.publisher_name <> 'DC Comics')
answer: 358 superheroes have alignment Good and are not published by DC Comics. I counted heroes with no publisher (3) or a blank publisher name (14) as "not DC", since they are not attributed to DC Comics. If you want only heroes with a named non-DC publisher, the count would be lower, at 341 (358 − 3 − 14, from the sub-counts in my check query). The Alignment and Publisher terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN d.dob < '1985-01-01' AND r.laps > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS percentage FROM results r JOIN races ra ON ra.raceId = r.raceId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = r.driverId WHERE ra.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2005
answer: About 64.88%. Of 2,039 race results from 2000 through 2005, about 64.88% were by drivers born before 1985-01-01 who completed more than 50 laps. I took the denominator to be all results in those years, not just those by drivers born before 1985. No rows had a missing lap count or birth date.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM atom a WHERE a.molecule_id=m.molecule_id AND a.element='f'))/COUNT(*),2) FROM molecule m WHERE m.label='+';
answer: 99.34% of carcinogenic molecules (label '+') have no fluorine atoms. Of the 152 carcinogenic molecules, 151 have none. I counted molecules, not atoms, and treated a molecule as fluorine-free if it has no atom with element 'f'.

sql: SELECT SUM(convertedManaCost) FROM cards WHERE artist = 'Rob Alexander' AND substr(originalReleaseDate, 1, 4) = '2013'
answer: 4.0. Only one Rob Alexander card printing has an original release date in 2013 (2013/1/11), and its converted mana cost is 4. The dates are stored as YYYY/M/D text, so I matched the year with substr. Rows with no original release date are excluded.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(c), 2) AS avg_pit_stops_per_race FROM (SELECT r.raceId, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pitStops p WHERE p.raceId = r.raceId) AS c FROM races r WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name NOT IN (SELECT name FROM races WHERE year = 2000))
answer: The average is 39.71 pit stops per race. I made two judgment calls. First, "not hosted in 2000" means the Grand Prix name (for example 'Chinese Grand Prix') did not appear on the 2000 calendar. That leaves 7 of the 2017 races. Matching on circuit instead would leave 9 races, and I did not compute that average. Second, I averaged over all 7 races, so the 2 races with no pit stop data count as 0. The pitStops table has no rows for them. Averaging only the 5 races that have data would give a higher figure, which I did not compute.

sql: SELECT s.superhero_name FROM superhero AS s JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id JOIN hero_power AS hp ON hp.hero_id = s.id JOIN superpower AS sp ON sp.id = hp.power_id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND sp.power_name = 'Super Strength'
answer: 201 superheroes published by Marvel Comics have the 'Super Strength' power, e.g. 3-D Man, A-Bomb, Abomination, Hulk, Thor and Wolverine. The query returns only superhero_name, since the question asks for the heroes themselves. The result is not truncated. 'Atlas' appears twice because two different heroes share that name, which I kept as separate rows. The ontology has no Term for 'Super Strength', so I matched it directly on superpower.power_name, a value confirmed in the data. This is the power in hero_power, not the 'Strength' attribute score. The Terms used (Superhero, Publisher, Superpower) are drafts, not certified.

sql: select (select avg(a.ball_control) from Player_Attributes a join Player p on p.player_api_id=a.player_api_id where p.player_name='Abdou Diallo') - (select avg(a.ball_control) from Player_Attributes a join Player p on p.player_api_id=a.player_api_id where p.player_name='Aaron Appindangoye') as diff
answer: Abdou Diallo's mean ball control is 49.4 (10 records) and Aaron Appindangoye's is 48.6 (5 records), so the difference is 0.8. The query returns 0.799999999999997 because of floating-point rounding. I averaged over all of each player's attribute records and did not take only the latest one.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(L.ALB),4) AS avg_ALB FROM Laboratory L JOIN Patient P ON P.ID=L.ID WHERE P.SEX='F' AND P.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' AND L.PLT>400
answer: The average ALB is 4.0 (4.0000), taken over 104 lab records with a non-null ALB. I read "lists an SLE diagnosis" as any Patient.Diagnosis containing 'SLE', which includes combinations such as "SLE, SJS" and "SLE susp" entries. I read "PLT > 400" as strictly greater than 400. If you want only patients whose diagnosis is exactly 'SLE', the average is 3.9123 over 65 records.

sql: WITH q AS (SELECT DISTINCT c.client_id, c.district_id FROM client c JOIN disp d ON d.client_id=c.client_id AND d.type='OWNER' WHERE c.gender='F' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM loan l WHERE l.account_id=d.account_id) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM card ca JOIN disp d2 ON d2.disp_id=ca.disp_id WHERE d2.account_id=d.account_id)), ds AS (SELECT DISTINCT district_id FROM q), x AS (SELECT di.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY A3 ORDER BY CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) DESC, A2) rn FROM district di JOIN ds USING(district_id)) SELECT A3 AS region, ROUND(AVG(A11),2) AS avg_district_salary, ROUND(AVG(A13),2) AS avg_unemployment_rate_1996, MAX(CASE WHEN rn=1 THEN A2 END) AS most_populous_district FROM x GROUP BY A3 ORDER BY A3
answer:
The query returns 8 rows, one per region: Prague, central Bohemia, east Bohemia, north Bohemia, north Moravia, south Bohemia, south Moravia and west Bohemia. Each row has the average district salary (A11), the average 1996 unemployment rate (A13) and the most populous district. For example, Prague is 12541.00, 0.43, Hl.m. Praha, and central Bohemia is 9318.30, 3.18, Kladno.

Readings I chose:
- **Client's district:** I used the district recorded on the client, not the account's branch district.
- **Card and loan:** A client qualifies if they are the OWNER of an account that has a loan and has a card linked to any disposition of that account. This matches how an earlier verified query (note 9) treats cards.
- **Averages:** Each district counts once, however many qualifying clients live there. The averages are over the distinct districts where these clients live, not over clients.
- **Most populous district:** Chosen by inhabitants (A4) among those districts only. Ties go to the name that comes first alphabetically.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) AS patient_count FROM Patient P JOIN Laboratory L ON L.ID=P.ID WHERE P.SEX='F' AND L.WBC>3.5 AND L.WBC<9 AND (L.FG<150 OR L.FG>450) AND CAST(L.RNP AS REAL)>15
answer: 1 female patient meets all three conditions. I counted patients, not lab records, and I checked all lab dates. Normal WBC is strictly between 3.5 and 9.0. Abnormal fibrinogen is below 150 or above 450. RNP is above 15, and 'negative' counts as not above 15. Using inclusive fibrinogen boundaries (<=150 or >=450) gives the same count.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(CAST(p.OwnerUserId AS TEXT), 'n:' || p.OwnerDisplayName)) AS user_count FROM votes AS v INNER JOIN posts AS p ON p.Id = v.PostId WHERE v.BountyAmount >= 30 AND v.CreationDate >= '2010-01-01' AND v.CreationDate < '2011-01-01'
answer: 32 users offered a bounty of 30 or more between 2010-01-01 and 2011-01-01. This comes from 48 bounty votes, dated 2010-07-24 to 2010-12-29. The bounty date is votes.CreationDate and the amount is votes.BountyAmount. The offering user is the post's owner: posts.OwnerUserId where it is set, otherwise posts.OwnerDisplayName. Two of the 48 bounty votes were on posts with no owner account, so those were counted by owner name. A name-identified owner could be the same person as an account-identified owner, which would make the count slightly high. The Post and Vote terms are still draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM Patient p WHERE p.Birthday IS NOT NULL AND (2026 - CAST(substr(p.Birthday,1,4) AS INTEGER) - (substr('2026-10-09',6) < substr(p.Birthday,6))) > 50 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.TG >= 200)
answer: 106 patients. I read "older than 50" as completed years of age on 2026-10-09 being strictly greater than 50. A patient counts if at least one laboratory record has TG >= 200. Patients with no birthday are excluded.

sql: SELECT a.element FROM atom a JOIN molecule m ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '-' GROUP BY a.element HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MIN(c) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS c FROM atom a2 JOIN molecule m2 ON m2.molecule_id = a2.molecule_id WHERE m2.label = '-' GROUP BY a2.element))
answer: Three elements are tied for the fewest atoms in non-carcinogenic molecules: ca (calcium), k (potassium) and pb (lead). I read "non-carcinogenic" as molecule.label = '-' and counted every atom row per element. The query returns only the element column. The Atom and Molecule Terms it relies on are draft, not certified.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT m.member_id, (m.position IN ('President','Vice President','Secretary','Treasurer')) AS officer, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_event) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_member = m.member_id) AS n FROM member m) SELECT ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN officer = 1 THEN n END), 2) AS avg_officer, ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN officer = 0 THEN n END), 2) AS avg_other FROM c
answer: Officers (President, Vice President, Secretary, Treasurer) attended an average of 14.50 events each. Other students attended an average of 9.24. Other students are all remaining members, including those listed as 'Member' and 'Inactive'. Members with no attendance count as 0 in their group's average, and all events in the records are included with no date cutoff. The Member term the query relies on is still a draft in the ontology, and I did not run validate_sql before running the query.

sql: WITH q AS (SELECT a.district_id, COUNT(DISTINCT a.account_id) n FROM loan l JOIN account a ON a.account_id=l.account_id WHERE l.duration>24 AND l.date<'1997-01-01' GROUP BY a.district_id) SELECT d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS district_count, SUM(CAST(d.A4 AS INTEGER)) AS total_population, SUM(q.n) AS account_count FROM q JOIN district d ON d.district_id=q.district_id GROUP BY d.A3 ORDER BY total_population DESC, region LIMIT 1
answer: South Moravia: 13 qualifying districts, combined population 1,947,078, and 40 qualifying accounts. Interpretation: "opened" refers to the loan date (before 1997-01-01), long-term means duration > 24 months, and districts are the account's branch district. Accounts are counted once each (distinct).

sql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.hasContentWarning = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS percentage FROM cards c JOIN legalities l ON l.uuid = c.uuid WHERE l.format = 'commander' AND l.status = 'Legal'
answer: 100.0%. 55,235 card printings are legal in commander, and none of them has hasContentWarning = 1. I counted each printing (uuid) as one card, and "legal status" means status = 'Legal'.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(m),1) AS avg_mana_value FROM (SELECT c.name, MIN(c.convertedManaCost) AS m FROM cards c WHERE c.types LIKE '%Creature%' AND c.edhrecRank BETWEEN 1 AND 1000 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM legalities l WHERE l.uuid=c.uuid AND l.status='Banned') GROUP BY c.name)
answer:
The average mana value is 3.4. It covers 7 distinct creature cards that have EDHRec rank 1 to 1000 and a 'Banned' row in at least one format.

I made three choices:
- "Banned in at least one format" means any `legalities` row with status 'Banned'. It is not limited to Commander.
- "Creature" means `types` contains 'Creature'.
- Each card counts once, grouped by name. The rank and mana value were identical across a card's printings.

sql: SELECT P.ID AS patient_id, P.SEX AS sex, L.Date AS last_test_date, L.`U-PRO` AS proteinuria_level FROM Patient P JOIN Laboratory L ON L.ID = P.ID WHERE L.`U-PRO` IS NOT NULL AND L.`U-PRO` <> '' AND L.Date = (SELECT MAX(L2.Date) FROM Laboratory L2 WHERE L2.ID = P.ID AND L2.`U-PRO` IS NOT NULL AND L2.`U-PRO` <> '') ORDER BY P.ID
answer: The query returns 295 rows, one per patient with a proteinuria test, which matches the 295 distinct patients with a recorded U-PRO result. Columns are patient ID, sex, the date of the latest proteinuria test, and the U-PRO value from that test. I counted a test as done when U-PRO is neither NULL nor an empty string, so a blank is treated as not tested. A '-' (negative) result counts as a test. "Most recent" is the latest proteinuria test, not the patient's latest lab visit of any kind, so a later visit with no U-PRO value is skipped. The level is returned as stored, for example '-', 'TR', '1', '300' or '>=1000'. No patient has two proteinuria tests on the same date, so there are no ties.

sql: SELECT c.Currency, COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM (SELECT CustomerID FROM yearmonth WHERE Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201311' AND Consumption>0 GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT Date)=11) y JOIN customers c USING(CustomerID) GROUP BY c.Currency;
answer: CZK: 61 customers, EUR: 4 customers. I read "bought fuel in a month" as Consumption > 0 in yearmonth (the convention in the verified queries), so a customer counts only if all 11 months, 201301 to 201311, have positive consumption. Zero or negative rows and missing months do not count.

sql: SELECT P.SEX AS sex, COUNT(DISTINCT P.ID) AS patients FROM Patient P WHERE P.SEX IN ('F','M') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory L WHERE L.ID = P.ID AND CAST(L.RNP AS REAL) > 32) GROUP BY P.SEX ORDER BY P.SEX
answer: 12 women and 0 men. The query returns one row per sex (F: 12). No male patient has any RNP value above 32, so M has no row. A patient counts if any of their lab records has RNP strictly above 32. RNP is stored as text, so I cast it to a number; 'negative' and similar values become 0 and are excluded. The Laboratory Test and Patient terms are still drafts and have not been certified. The ontology had no term for the anti-ribonuclear protein antibody, so I used the Laboratory.RNP column, which the docs describe as that antibody.

sql: select s.School, s.Phone from schools s join satscores t on t.cds=s.CDSCode where s.DOC='03' and t.rtype='S' and t.NumGE1500=(select max(t2.NumGE1500) from schools s2 join satscores t2 on t2.cds=s2.CDSCode where s2.DOC='03' and t2.rtype='S')
answer: High Tech High North County, phone (619) 243-5014. It had 56 SAT test takers scoring 1500 or above, the most of any school run by a statewide benefit charter network (DOC code '03'). No other school tied. I counted only school-level SAT rows (rtype='S'). The district-level row (102) has no school name, so I excluded it.

sql: select a.date from Player_Attributes a join Player p on a.player_api_id=p.player_api_id where p.player_name='Kevin Constant' and a.crossing=(select max(a2.crossing) from Player_Attributes a2 join Player p2 on a2.player_api_id=p2.player_api_id where p2.player_name='Kevin Constant') order by a.date limit 1
answer: Kevin Constant first recorded his highest crossing score (82) on 2013-02-15. The score was also 82 on 2013-03-08 and 2013-03-28, and I took the earliest date as "first".

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS school_count FROM satscores t JOIN schools s ON s.CDSCode=t.cds WHERE t.rtype='S' AND s.MailCity='San Francisco' AND s.DOCType IN ('Unified School District','High School District','Elementary School District','County Office of Education (COE)') AND t.AvgScrRead+t.AvgScrMath+t.AvgScrWrite>=1500
answer: 3 schools qualify. In the first query, 4 San Francisco mailing-city schools had a total SAT score of at least 1500. Three of them are in one of the four district types you listed, so one is excluded. I ran that first query with the district-type check as a flag rather than a filter. The final query below is validated but I did not run it separately. I read "average total SAT score" as AvgScrRead + AvgScrMath + AvgScrWrite from the school-level SAT records (rtype 'S'), and "district type" as schools.DOCType. frpm.`District Type` gives the same count of 3. I assumed the four listed district types are what make a school public. The ontology Terms used are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers c WHERE c.Currency='EUR' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM yearmonth y WHERE y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID AND y.Date BETWEEN '201201' AND '201212' AND y.Consumption>0) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM yearmonth y WHERE y.CustomerID=c.CustomerID AND y.Date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312' AND y.Consumption>0)
answer: 1,516 customers who pay in EUR had gas consumption in both 2012 and 2013. I counted a customer as having gas consumption in a year if at least one month of that year has yearmonth.Consumption > 0, following the glossary's definition of "purchased gas". The 'Customer' and 'Monthly Customer Consumption' Terms I used are still drafts and have not been certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.SEX='F' THEN p.ID END) - COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.SEX='M' THEN p.ID END) AS diff FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE p.Diagnosis='RA' AND l.UN<30
answer: 23. There are 23 more women than men among RA patients with normal urea nitrogen. I took RA to mean Diagnosis exactly 'RA', which excludes combined diagnoses like 'RA, SJS' and uncertain ones like 'RA susp'. I took normal urea nitrogen to mean UN < 30 (from the Laboratory docs), counting a patient if any lab record meets it. Patients are counted once each.

sql: select round(avg(A11),2) from district where A3='central Bohemia' and district_id in (select c.district_id from client c join disp d on d.client_id=c.client_id and d.type='OWNER' where not exists (select 1 from disp d2 join card k on k.disp_id=d2.disp_id where d2.account_id=d.account_id))
answer: 9357.25 (yearly CZK). I read "in central Bohemia" as the client's own district having region 'central Bohemia'. Clients are the owners (disp.type='OWNER') of accounts where no disposition of the account has a card. I averaged A11 over the distinct districts, not once per client.

sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Male' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS male_count, COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Female' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS female_count FROM superhero AS s JOIN colour AS c ON c.id = s.hair_colour_id JOIN gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id WHERE c.colour = 'Blue' AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id) >= 10
answer: 3 male and 0 female blue-haired superheroes have ten or more listed powers (male_count = 3, female_count = 0). I read 'blue-haired' as hair colour exactly 'Blue', so mixed values such as 'Blue/White' and 'Black/Blue' are excluded. I counted a hero's powers as the number of hero_power rows. The Colour, Gender and Superhero terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified. The validator's fan-out warning doesn't apply, because each hero joins to exactly one gender and the power count is a per-hero subquery.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards c JOIN sets s ON s.code = c.setCode WHERE substr(c.originalReleaseDate,1,4) = '2014' AND s.mtgoCode IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(s.mtgoCode) <> ''
answer: 293 printings. I used cards.originalReleaseDate (stored as YYYY/M/D, so I took the first 4 characters) for the year. I counted a set as MTGO-available when sets.mtgoCode is non-NULL and non-empty (no sets have an empty code). Each card row counts once, so the same name in several sets is counted per set.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS slow_q1_count FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = q.driverId WHERE (d.code IS NULL OR d.code = '') AND d.forename IN (SELECT forename FROM drivers GROUP BY forename HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) AND q.q1 IS NOT NULL AND q.q1 <> '' AND CAST(substr(q.q1,1,instr(q.q1,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60000 + CAST(substr(q.q1,instr(q.q1,':')+1,2) AS INTEGER)*1000 + CAST(substr(q.q1,-3) AS INTEGER) > 120000;
answer: 23 qualifying 1 (Q1) lap times were slower than 2:00.000. They were set by drivers with no code whose first name is shared with at least one other driver. I read "no code" as a NULL or empty code, and I counted each Q1 time as one row. I did not count distinct drivers. I converted the times to milliseconds before comparing, so a time of exactly 2:00.000 is not counted.

sql: select count(distinct p.id) from superhero s join publisher p on p.id=s.publisher_id where s.height_cm>200 and p.publisher_name is not null and trim(p.publisher_name)<>''
answer: 7 publishers have at least one hero strictly taller than 200 cm: Dark Horse Comics, DC Comics, George Lucas, Image Comics, J. R. R. Tolkien, Marvel Comics and Microsoft. I left out the publisher record with a blank name (id 1), which has 2 tall heroes, because it isn't a real publisher. I kept George Lucas, J. R. R. Tolkien and Microsoft because they are named publisher entries in the database. If you only want comic publishers, the count is 4 (Dark Horse, DC, Image, Marvel).

sql: SELECT s.City, COUNT(DISTINCT s.CDSCode) AS magnet_provision2_schools FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON s.CDSCode = f.CDSCode WHERE s.Magnet = 1 AND f.`NSLP Provision Status` IN ('Provision 2','Breakfast Provision 2','Lunch Provision 2') GROUP BY s.City ORDER BY magnet_provision2_schools DESC, s.City
answer:
The query returns 32 cities, each with its count of magnet schools running a Provision 2 meal program. Los Angeles has the most at 48, then San Diego at 12 and Stockton at 8. Most of the other cities have 1 to 6.

I made three choices where the question was ambiguous:
- **Provision 2 statuses:** I counted 'Provision 2', 'Breakfast Provision 2' and 'Lunch Provision 2' as Provision 2. 'Multiple Provision Types' is excluded, as you asked.
- **City:** I used schools.City, the location city, not MailCity.
- **Magnet flag:** I used Magnet = 1.

City names are grouped exactly as stored, so spelling variants stay separate. 'Montclair' and 'Montclair,' appear as two rows, and 'Pacomia' appears as its own city. The School and Free or Reduced Price Meal Record terms the query relies on are still draft, not certified.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN c.colour = 'Blue' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 2) AS percentage FROM superhero AS s JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id LEFT JOIN colour AS c ON s.skin_colour_id = c.id WHERE g.gender = 'Female'
answer: 2.46% of female superheroes have blue skin. I counted every hero with gender 'Female' as the denominator, including those with an unknown skin colour. 'Blue' matches only the exact colour 'Blue', not combinations such as 'Blue/White'. The ontology has no Term for 'female superheroes' or 'blue skin', so I used the gender table and the superhero.skin_colour_id link to the colour table directly. The Colour and Gender Terms are still draft. validate_sql was skipped; run_sql returned a fan-out warning that doesn't apply, since each hero has one skin colour.

sql:
WITH cur AS (SELECT player_api_id, overall_rating, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC, id DESC) rn FROM Player_Attributes WHERE date < '2011-01-01' AND overall_rating IS NOT NULL),
sel AS (SELECT player_api_id FROM cur WHERE rn=1 AND overall_rating > 80),
apps AS (SELECT id mid, home_player_1 pid FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_2 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_3 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_4 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_5 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_6 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_7 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_8 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_9 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_10 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_11 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_1 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_2 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_3 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_4 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_5 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_6 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_7 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_8 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_9 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_10 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_11 FROM Match WHERE season='2010/2011'),
cnt AS (SELECT s.player_api_id, COUNT(DISTINCT a.mid) n FROM sel s LEFT JOIN apps a ON a.pid=s.player_api_id GROUP BY s.player_api_id)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(n),2) AS avg_matches FROM cnt
answer:
The average is 22.47 matches per player in the 2010/2011 season.

I made three choices where the question was open:
- **Rating as of 31 Dec 2010:** I used each player's latest rating record dated on or before 31 Dec 2010. If a player had several records on the same date, I took the one with the highest id. I kept players whose rating on that record was strictly above 80.
- **Matches played:** A player counts for a match if they appear in either team's 11-man lineup in a match labelled season '2010/2011'.
- **Players with no matches:** They stay in the average with a count of 0. Dropping them would raise the figure.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) AS female_patient_count FROM Patient AS p INNER JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'F' AND l.PT < 14 AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) >= 16
answer: 3 female patients have a laboratory record with PT below 14 seconds and anti-RNP of 16 or higher. Both values come from the same record. A patient is counted once even if several records qualify. RNP is stored as text, so I cast it to a number; 'negative' and blank values become 0 and don't qualify.

sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, CAST(strftime('%Y','2026-10-09') AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y',p.Birthday) AS INTEGER) - (strftime('%m-%d','2026-10-09') < strftime('%m-%d',p.Birthday)) AS age FROM Patient p WHERE p.Birthday IS NOT NULL AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.GLU >= 180 AND l."T-CHO" < 250) ORDER BY p.ID
answer: 13 patients match (e.g. 57266, M, 103; 5065022, F, 54). I read the question as requiring both conditions (GLU >= 180 and T-CHO < 250) in the same laboratory record. Age is completed years on 2026-10-09, which means the year difference minus 1 if the birthday hasn't yet occurred by 10-09. Patients with no birthday are excluded. The Patient and Laboratory Test terms are still draft, not certified.

sql:
WITH latest AS (SELECT a.player_api_id, a.overall_rating, a.defensive_work_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY a.player_api_id ORDER BY a.date DESC, a.id DESC) rn FROM Player_Attributes a WHERE a.date < '2013-07-13' AND a.overall_rating IS NOT NULL),
cur AS (SELECT * FROM latest WHERE rn=1 AND defensive_work_rate IN ('low','medium','high'))
SELECT ROUND(100.0*((SELECT c.overall_rating FROM cur c JOIN Player p ON p.player_api_id=c.player_api_id WHERE p.player_name='Landon Donovan') - AVG(overall_rating))/AVG(overall_rating),2) AS pct_higher FROM cur
answer:
Landon Donovan's overall rating on 12 July 2013 was 18.67% higher than the average across all players on that date.

I took each player's latest rating record dated on or before 12 July 2013. That way players not updated that day still count with the rating they carried. I kept only players whose defensive work rate in that record is 'low', 'medium' or 'high', which drops odd values such as numbers or blanks. Donovan has a record dated exactly 12 July 2013.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c JOIN posts p ON p.Id = c.PostId WHERE c.Score = 0 AND c.PostId IN (SELECT PostId FROM comments GROUP BY PostId HAVING COUNT(*) = 1)
answer: 10999. I counted comments whose post exists in `posts` and is the only comment record for that post, then kept those with Score = 0. The 36 comments pointing to posts that are not in `posts` are excluded. One of them would otherwise have counted, which gives 11000.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(height_cm), 1) AS avg_height_cm FROM superhero WHERE height_cm > 0 AND race_id = (SELECT race_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'A-Bomb')
answer: 181.2 cm. I read "A-Bomb's group" as A-Bomb's race (Human), since the docs describe race as "race or group". A-Bomb is included. Heroes with a height of NULL or 0 are excluded, because the docs say those mean the height is missing. If "group" meant publisher (Marvel Comics), the result would differ.

sql: SELECT d.forename||' '||d.surname AS driver_name, ps.duration AS pit_stop_time, r.name AS race_name, c.name AS circuit_name, c.location AS circuit_location FROM pitStops ps JOIN races r ON r.raceId=ps.raceId JOIN circuits c ON c.circuitId=r.circuitId JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=ps.driverId WHERE r.date BETWEEN '2016-09-01' AND '2016-09-30' AND ps.milliseconds=(SELECT MIN(p.milliseconds) FROM pitStops p JOIN races x ON x.raceId=p.raceId WHERE x.date BETWEEN '2016-09-01' AND '2016-09-30') ORDER BY driver_name
answer: 2016년 9월 레이스에서 가장 빠른 피트 스톱은 23.633초이고, 두 명이 같은 기록을 냈습니다. 둘 다 이탈리아 그랑프리(Autodromo Nazionale di Monza, 위치 Monza)에서 나왔고, 드라이버는 Daniel Ricciardo와 Lewis Hamilton입니다. 레이스 날짜가 2016-09-01~09-30인 경기를 대상으로 했고, 최단 기록은 milliseconds 값으로 비교했습니다.

sql: SELECT g AS lowest_grade FROM (SELECT SUBSTR(GSserved,1,INSTR(GSserved||'-','-')-1) AS g FROM schools WHERE NCESDist='0632640' AND GSserved IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY CASE g WHEN 'P' THEN -1 WHEN 'K' THEN 0 ELSE CAST(g AS INTEGER) END LIMIT 1
answer: K (kindergarten). I used the directory's grade span `schools.GSserved` and took the first grade of each span. Grades were ranked P < K < 1..12 rather than as text. I included all schools with NCESDist '0632640', open or closed. Nine schools start at K, one starts at 1, and one has no grade span recorded. The answer is the same if closed schools are excluded.

sql: SELECT c.Segment AS segment, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers c JOIN (SELECT CustomerID FROM yearmonth WHERE Date LIKE '2012%' GROUP BY CustomerID HAVING SUM(Consumption) < 30000 AND MAX(Consumption) > 0) y ON c.CustomerID=y.CustomerID GROUP BY c.Segment ORDER BY c.Segment
answer: 2012년 총 소비량이 30,000 미만인 고객 수는 KAM 1,123명, LAM 2,031명, SME 21,862명입니다. 해석은 두 가지로 정했습니다. 먼저 '2012년에 카드를 사용한 고객'은 2012년 중 소비량이 0보다 큰 달이 한 번 이상 있는 고객으로 봤습니다. 그리고 총 소비량은 2012년 월별 소비량(yearmonth)을 모두 더한 값이며, 정확히 30,000인 고객은 제외했습니다. 참고로 yearmonth에는 2012년 1월부터 9월까지만 데이터가 있어서, 이 합계는 9개월 기준입니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg),2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON p.id=s.publisher_id WHERE p.publisher_name='George Lucas' AND s.weight_kg>0 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power hp WHERE hp.hero_id=s.id)
answer: 77.4 kg (77.40 to two decimals). I counted only George Lucas heroes with at least one row in hero_power. I treated weight_kg of 0 or NULL as unrecorded and left those heroes out, as the earlier verified queries do.

sql: SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS full_name FROM lapTimes l JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId = l.driverId WHERE l.milliseconds IS NOT NULL GROUP BY d.driverId ORDER BY MIN(l.milliseconds), d.driverId LIMIT 20
answer: I read the question as the 20 distinct drivers, ranked by each driver's single fastest lap in the lapTimes table (milliseconds). The query returns one column, full name (forename and surname), shortest lap first. The list runs from Lewis Hamilton (67.411 s), Daniel Ricciardo, Kimi Räikkönen, Sebastian Vettel and Valtteri Bottas down to Pascal Wehrlein at 20th (69.241 s). No two drivers in the top 20 share a best lap, so the order has no ties.

sql: SELECT s.FundingType AS charter_funding_type, COUNT(DISTINCT s.CDSCode) AS active_schools, SUM(f."Enrollment (K-12)") AS total_k12_enrollment, SUM(f."FRPM Count (K-12)") AS total_frpm_k12 FROM schools s JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode = s.CDSCode WHERE s.Charter = 1 AND s.DOCType = 'County Office of Education (COE)' AND s.StatusType = 'Active' AND s.FundingType IN ('Directly funded','Locally funded') GROUP BY s.FundingType ORDER BY CASE s.FundingType WHEN 'Directly funded' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END
answer:
Directly funded: 75 active schools, 38,306 K-12 enrollment, 22,008 FRPM-eligible K-12 students. Locally funded: 36 active schools, 12,285 K-12 enrollment, 7,535 FRPM-eligible K-12 students.

Readings I chose: "run by county offices of education" means schools.DOCType = 'County Office of Education (COE)' and Charter = 1. Funding type comes from schools.FundingType. I applied the Active filter to all three measures, so enrollment and FRPM totals cover only the active schools. Enrollment and FRPM come from the frpm table, which holds 2014-2015 data. The Terms I relied on (School, Free or Reduced Price Meal Record) are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT p.player_api_id, AVG(a.heading_accuracy) AS mean_heading_accuracy FROM Player p JOIN Player_Attributes a ON a.player_api_id=p.player_api_id WHERE p.height>180 AND a.heading_accuracy IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.player_api_id ORDER BY mean_heading_accuracy DESC, p.player_api_id LIMIT 10
answer: 쿼리는 키가 180cm를 넘는 선수의 heading_accuracy 평균을 구해 상위 10명을 반환합니다. 1위는 선수 30699(평균 91.8)입니다. heading_accuracy가 비어 있는 기록은 평균에서 제외했고, 평균이 같으면 player_api_id가 작은 선수를 먼저 두었습니다. 질문이 "선수 목록"이라 선수 API ID와 평균값 두 열을 출력했습니다. 이름이 필요하면 player_name 열을 추가하면 됩니다.

sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(p.Admission='+'),0) AS admitted_inpatients, COALESCE(SUM(p.Admission='-'),0) AS outpatient_followed FROM Patient p WHERE TRIM(p.Diagnosis)='SLE' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.`U-PRO` IS NOT NULL AND CASE WHEN l.`U-PRO` IN ('+','+(','%%') THEN 30 WHEN l.`U-PRO` LIKE '%(%' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(l.`U-PRO`,INSTR(l.`U-PRO`,'(')+1) AS REAL) WHEN l.`U-PRO` LIKE '>=%' THEN CAST(SUBSTR(l.`U-PRO`,3) AS REAL) ELSE CAST(l.`U-PRO` AS REAL) END >= 30)
answer:
13 patients were admitted as inpatients and 1 was followed at the outpatient clinic.

Readings I chose:
- "Only diagnosis is SLE" means Patient.Diagnosis is exactly 'SLE'. 'SLE susp' and combinations such as 'SLE, SJS' are excluded.
- "Abnormally high proteinuria" means a U-PRO result of 30 mg/dL or more at any lab visit, since the docs give the normal range as 0 < N < 30. Plain numbers are read as mg/dL. '+1(30)' and '+2(100)' use the value in parentheses, and '>=300' counts as 300. I counted '+', '+(' and '%%' as positive. Dipstick-style values of 1 to 4 are treated as mg/dL, so they are normal.
- "Full history" means each patient is counted once if any of their lab records qualifies.
- Admission '+' means admitted and '-' means outpatient. One qualifying SLE patient has a blank Admission value and falls in neither count.

sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(sc.NumTstTakr,0))*1.0/COUNT(*),2) AS avg_sat_test_takers_per_school FROM schools s LEFT JOIN satscores sc ON sc.cds=s.CDSCode WHERE s.County='Los Angeles' AND s.OpenDate>='2007-01-01' AND s.OpenDate<'2008-01-01' AND s.DOC IN ('00','52','54','56')
answer: The average is 14.57 SAT test takers per school. I counted 47 Los Angeles County schools that opened in 2007 and are run by a school district. Those are 43 unified, 3 high school and 1 elementary district school. A county office of education would also count, but none opened in 2007. I left out the one school run by the State Board of Education. Schools with no SAT record count as zero test takers.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT u.DisplayName n, COUNT(*) k FROM postHistory h JOIN users u ON u.Id=h.UserId WHERE h.PostId=(SELECT Id FROM posts WHERE Title='Why square the difference instead of taking the absolute value in standard deviation?') AND h.Comment IS NOT NULL AND h.Comment<>'' GROUP BY u.Id) SELECT n AS DisplayName, k AS EditCommentCount FROM c WHERE k=(SELECT MAX(k) FROM c)
answer: mbq left the most edit comments on that post (post 118): 3. I counted revisions with a non-empty Comment, each revision as its own event, so the repeated "deleted 5 characters in body; edited title" note counts twice. The other commenting editor, user 919, left 1. Three revisions by user 83 have empty comments and were excluded. There is no tie.

sql: select p.SEX, count(distinct p.ID) as patient_count from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where l.ALB<3.5 and p.SEX in ('F','M') group by p.SEX order by p.SEX
answer: ALB가 3.5 미만인 환자는 여성(F) 64명, 남성(M) 14명입니다. 환자 한 명에게 해당 검사 기록이 여러 건이어도 1명으로 셌고, 검사 기록 중 하나라도 ALB가 3.5 미만이면 포함했습니다. 성별이 비어 있는 환자 2명은 F나 M이 아니어서 결과에서 뺐습니다.

sql: WITH w AS (SELECT t.team_long_name AS name, COUNT(*) AS wins FROM Match m JOIN Team t ON t.team_api_id = m.away_team_api_id WHERE m.league_id = 19694 AND m.season = '2009/2010' AND m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal GROUP BY t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name) SELECT name FROM w WHERE wins = (SELECT MAX(wins) FROM w) ORDER BY name
answer: Celtic and Rangers are tied, each with 11 away wins in the 2009/2010 Scotland Premier League. I counted an away win as a match where the away team scored more goals than the home team. The query returns only the team names.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.weight_kg), 1) AS avg_weight_kg, COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN publisher AS p ON p.id = s.publisher_id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' AND s.weight_kg > 0
answer: DC Comics superheroes with a known weight average 101.9 kg, based on 156 superheroes. I counted a weight as known when weight_kg is greater than 0, because the data stores 0 or NULL for missing weights. I did not remove outliers. The data has a maximum weight of 90,000,000 kg, but I don't know whether that hero is a DC Comics superhero. The Superhero and Publisher terms the query relies on are still drafts and not certified.

sql: SELECT p.ViewCount, u.DisplayName FROM posts p LEFT JOIN users u ON u.Id = p.LastEditorUserId WHERE p.Title = 'Computer game datasets'
answer: The post 'Computer game datasets' has 1708 views. Its last editor is mbq. I took the editor from LastEditorUserId and joined it to users for the display name. The post's own LastEditorDisplayName is empty.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient p WHERE p.Birthday > '1960-01-01' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.RNP IS NOT NULL AND l.RNP <> 'negative' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL) > 10)
answer: 594 patients born after 1960-01-01 never had an RNP result strictly above 10. Of the 603 patients born after that date, 9 had a raised result. Patients with no lab results are included, and 'negative' counts as not raised. I read "born after 1 January 1960" as Birthday > '1960-01-01', so 1 January itself is excluded.

sql:
WITH d AS (SELECT district_id, A2 name, A3 region, A11 sal, CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) pop,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY A3 ORDER BY CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) DESC) rk,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY A3 ORDER BY CAST(A4 AS INTEGER) DESC, district_id) rn FROM district),
t AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) n,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type='PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) inc,
  SUM(CASE WHEN type<>'PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) exp FROM trans GROUP BY account_id),
rc AS (SELECT d.region, COUNT(*) c FROM client c JOIN d ON d.district_id=c.district_id GROUP BY d.region)
SELECT a.account_id, a.date AS opened_date, a.frequency, d.name AS district_name, d.region,
  CASE WHEN d.district_id=(SELECT district_id FROM client WHERE client_id=3541) THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS is_home_district,
  d.sal AS average_salary, COALESCE(l.status,'none') AS loan_status, COALESCE(l.amount,0) AS loan_amount,
  COALESCE(t.n,0) AS transaction_count, COALESCE(t.inc,0) AS total_income, COALESCE(t.exp,0) AS total_expense,
  COALESCE(t.inc,0)-COALESCE(t.exp,0) AS net_balance, rc.c AS clients_in_region,
  top.name AS most_populous_district, top.pop AS most_populous_inhabitants, d.rk AS population_rank
FROM account a
JOIN d ON d.district_id=a.district_id
JOIN d top ON top.region=d.region AND top.rn=1
JOIN rc ON rc.region=d.region
LEFT JOIN loan l ON l.account_id=a.account_id
LEFT JOIN t ON t.account_id=a.account_id
WHERE a.account_id IN (SELECT account_id FROM disp WHERE client_id=3541)
ORDER BY transaction_count DESC, a.account_id;
answer:
Client 3541 can access one account, 2932 (owner or disponent). It was opened 1993-05-04, has monthly statements (POPLATEK MESICNE), and is held in Olomouc, north Moravia. Olomouc is not the client's home district. Its average salary is 8994. The account has no loan (status 'none', amount 0). It has 655 transactions, income 2,821,377, expense 2,787,425 and net balance 33,952. North Moravia has 920 clients whose home district is in the region. Its most populous district is Ostrava - mesto with 323,870 inhabitants, and Olomouc ranks 4th.

Readings I chose:
- "Can access" means any disp row for the client, owner or disponent.
- Income is PRIJEM transactions. Expense is every other type (VYDAJ and the undocumented VYBER).
- Net balance is income minus expense.
- Population is the A4 column cast to integer.
- Rank uses RANK(), so ties share a rank and the next rank skips.
- Region is district.A3.
- The region client count uses client.district_id, the home district.
- Accounts with no transactions would show 0 for the count and totals.

sql:
WITH l AS (
SELECT country_id, home_player_1 p FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, home_player_2 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, home_player_3 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, home_player_4 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, home_player_5 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, home_player_6 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, home_player_7 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, home_player_8 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, home_player_9 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, home_player_10 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, home_player_11 FROM Match
UNION ALL SELECT country_id, away_player_1 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, away_player_2 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, away_player_3 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, away_player_4 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, away_player_5 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, away_player_6 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, away_player_7 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, away_player_8 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, away_player_9 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, away_player_10 FROM Match UNION ALL SELECT country_id, away_player_11 FROM Match),
c AS (SELECT co.name, COUNT(DISTINCT l.p) n FROM l JOIN Player pl ON pl.player_api_id=l.p JOIN Country co ON co.id=l.country_id WHERE pl.weight>=210 GROUP BY co.name)
SELECT name, n FROM c WHERE n=(SELECT MAX(n) FROM c) ORDER BY name;
answer:
England had the most players weighing 210 lb or more, with 12. There was no tie.

I took "weight" to be pounds, which the wiki infers because the docs give no unit. I counted players from both teams (home and away lineups, 11 slots each) in every match played in each country's league. I counted each player once per country, not once per match appearance. If you wanted appearances counted instead, the number would be higher and I didn't run that version.

sql: select round(100.0*sum(e)/count(*),2) as pct from (select p.ID, max(CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>64) e from Patient p join Laboratory l on l.ID=p.ID where p.SEX='F' and l.RNP is not null and l.RNP<>'' group by p.ID);
answer: 5.49%. Among 91 women with at least one anti-RNP result, 5 had a titer above 1:64, and all five were 256. I counted each patient once, as elevated if any of their results was above 64. 'negative' and '0' counted as available and not elevated, and patients with no RNP value were excluded. If you count lab rows instead of patients, the figure would differ.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) FROM connected AS c INNER JOIN atom AS a1 ON a1.atom_id = c.atom_id INNER JOIN atom AS a2 ON a2.atom_id = c.atom_id2 WHERE (a1.element = 'h' OR a2.element = 'h') AND a1.molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element = 'y')
answer: 2 bonds in the yttrium-containing molecule have a hydrogen atom at one end. I counted distinct bonds where either atom is hydrogen, since the connected table stores each bond in both directions. The Atom term used is still a draft in the ontology.

sql: WITH c AS (SELECT SUM(p.publisher_name='DC Comics') AS dc, SUM(p.publisher_name='Marvel Comics') AS mv FROM superhero s JOIN publisher p ON p.id=s.publisher_id) SELECT CASE WHEN dc>mv THEN 'DC Comics' WHEN mv>dc THEN 'Marvel Comics' ELSE 'Tie' END AS publisher, ABS(dc-mv) AS difference FROM c
answer: Marvel Comics has more superheroes, by 163 (387 for Marvel and 224 for DC Comics). I counted rows in `superhero` by publisher name. The query returns the publisher (or 'Tie') and the difference, which is 0 in a tie.

sql: WITH cc AS (SELECT c.client_id, c.gender, c.birth_date, ca.type AS card_type, CAST(strftime('%Y', ca.issued) AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', c.birth_date) AS INTEGER) AS age, d.account_id, c.district_id FROM card ca JOIN disp d ON d.disp_id = ca.disp_id JOIN client c ON c.client_id = d.client_id WHERE ca.issued >= '1994-01-01' AND ca.issued < '1995-01-01'), ln AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(amount) AS total FROM loan GROUP BY account_id) SELECT cc.client_id, cc.gender, cc.birth_date, cc.card_type, cc.age AS age_at_card_issue, COALESCE(ln.n, 0) AS number_of_loans, COALESCE(ln.total, 0) AS total_amount_borrowed, CASE WHEN COALESCE(ln.n, 0) > 0 AND cc.age < 30 THEN 'Young borrower' WHEN COALESCE(ln.n, 0) > 0 THEN 'Mature borrower' ELSE 'Non-borrower' END AS borrower_classification, di.A2 AS district_name, di.A11 AS district_average_salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY cc.gender ORDER BY cc.age DESC) AS age_rank_within_gender FROM cc JOIN district di ON di.district_id = cc.district_id LEFT JOIN ln ON ln.account_id = cc.account_id ORDER BY cc.client_id
answer:
21 clients were issued a card in 1994 (each has one card). Only client 3687 has a loan (1 loan, 82,896, Young borrower, age 22). The other 20 are Non-borrowers with 0 loans and 0 borrowed.

Readings I chose where the question was open:
- Loans are counted on the account of the disposition that holds the card.
- District name and average salary come from the client's home district (client.district_id), not the account's branch district.
- Age rank within gender runs oldest first (rank 1 = oldest) with standard competition ranking (RANK). The question didn't give a direction. For youngest first, change the ORDER BY inside RANK() to ASC.
- Age is the issue year minus the birth year, as defined in the question.
- Non-borrowers show 0 for number of loans and total amount borrowed.

The Client, Credit Card, Disposition, District and Loan terms are draft (not certified). validate_sql warned that the loan-to-disposition join isn't a modeled relationship. I join loan to the account through the account id.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(t), 2) AS avg_total_expense_per_event FROM (SELECT SUM(e.cost) AS t FROM expense e JOIN member m ON m.member_id = e.link_to_member JOIN budget b ON b.budget_id = e.link_to_budget WHERE m.first_name = 'Elijah' AND m.last_name = 'Allen' AND strftime('%m', e.expense_date) IN ('09','10') GROUP BY b.link_to_event)
answer: 98.77. Elijah Allen's September and October expenses (2019) fall under 6 events, with total costs of 592.62 across them, so the mean per event is 98.77. I read "September or October" as those months in any year (only 2019 exists for them), and linked each expense to an event through its budget line.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0*SUM(element='cl')/COUNT(*),4) FROM atom WHERE molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type='-')
answer: 3.4824% of atoms in molecules with at least one single bond are chlorine. Single bond is bond_type '-' and chlorine is element 'cl'.

sql: WITH it AS (SELECT d.forename, d.surname, q.q3, CAST(SUBSTR(q.q3,1,INSTR(q.q3,':')-1) AS INTEGER)*60 + CAST(SUBSTR(q.q3,INSTR(q.q3,':')+1) AS REAL) AS s FROM qualifying q JOIN drivers d ON d.driverId=q.driverId WHERE d.nationality='Italian' AND q.q3 IS NOT NULL AND q.q3<>'') SELECT DISTINCT forename, surname, q3 FROM it WHERE s=(SELECT MIN(s) FROM it)
answer: Jarno Trulli, 1:11.328. He is the only Italian driver with that fastest Q3 time. I read "Italian" as drivers.nationality = 'Italian' and counted only non-empty Q3 times. I compared times numerically in seconds. The Driver and Qualifying Result terms used are draft, not certified.

sql: WITH lm AS (SELECT MAX(m.date) AS d FROM Match m JOIN Team t ON t.team_api_id IN (m.home_team_api_id, m.away_team_api_id) WHERE t.team_long_name = 'KSV Cercle Brugge' AND m.season = '2012/2013') SELECT (SELECT ta.buildUpPlaySpeedClass FROM Team_Attributes ta JOIN Team t ON t.team_api_id = ta.team_api_id WHERE t.team_long_name = 'KSV Cercle Brugge' AND ta.date <= lm.d ORDER BY ta.date DESC, ta.id DESC LIMIT 1) AS buildUpPlaySpeedClass FROM lm
answer: Fast. KSV Cercle Brugge's last 2012/2013 match was on 2013-03-16. The snapshot in effect then was dated 2012-02-22 and has build-up play speed class Fast. The next snapshot, dated 2013-09-20, falls after the match.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT q.driverId) FROM qualifying q JOIN races r ON r.raceId = q.raceId WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND q.q2 <> '' AND q.q2 < '1:40.000'
answer: 15 drivers set a Q2 time faster than 1:40.000 at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix. All 15 Q2 times were between 1:34.660 and 1:38.526. Empty Q2 values were excluded, and times were compared as text, which works because they all use the M:SS.mmm format.

sql: with t as (select code from sets where code in (select setCode from cards where name='Abyssal Horror') order by releaseDate, code limit 1), l as (select code from sets order by releaseDate desc, code limit 1), pick as (select code from t union select code from l) select s.name, round(100.0*sum(case when c.manaCost is not null and c.manaCost<>'' and c.convertedManaCost<=3 then 1 else 0 end)/count(*),2) as pct from sets s join pick p on p.code=s.code join cards c on c.setCode=s.code group by s.code order by s.releaseDate
answer: Urza's Saga (where Abyssal Horror was first printed, 1998-10-12): 58.15%. Time Spiral Remastered (latest release, 2021-03-19): 80.00%. I took the percentage over all card printings in each set. A card counts only if it has a printed mana cost and a converted mana cost of 3 or less.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT hp.power_id) AS superpower_count FROM hero_power AS hp INNER JOIN superhero AS s ON hp.hero_id = s.id INNER JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id WHERE g.gender = 'Male' AND s.weight_kg > 0 AND s.weight_kg < 70
answer: 102개의 서로 다른 초능력을 몸무게 70kg 미만인 남성 히어로가 1명 이상 보유하고 있습니다. 몸무게가 기록되지 않은 경우(NULL 또는 0)는 70kg 미만으로 세지 않았고, 성별은 gender 값이 'Male'인 경우만 남성으로 봤습니다. 사용한 Gender, Superhero 용어는 아직 draft 상태입니다.

sql: WITH m AS (SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type='-') SELECT ROUND(1.0*SUM(CASE WHEN a.element='o' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(DISTINCT m.molecule_id),4) FROM m LEFT JOIN atom a ON a.molecule_id=m.molecule_id
answer: 평균 산소 원자 수는 분자당 2.1613개입니다. 단일 결합은 bond_type '-'로 보았고, 산소 원자가 없는 분자도 분모에 포함했습니다.

sql: SELECT c.Text, u.DisplayName FROM comments c JOIN posts p ON p.Id = c.PostId LEFT JOIN users u ON u.Id = c.UserId WHERE p.Title = 'Analysing wind data with R' ORDER BY c.CreationDate DESC, c.Id DESC LIMIT 10
answer: The query returns the 10 most recent comments on 'Analysing wind data with R', newest first, as comment text and author display name. I took the display name from users through comments.UserId, because comments.UserDisplayName is empty for these comments. I broke ties in creation time by higher comment Id. The result has 10 rows, from 2011-02-14 08:50 back to 2011-02-13 08:35. The authors are eliavs, David Heffernan, Spacedman, mpiktas and mbq.

sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT DISTINCT link_to_event AS id FROM budget WHERE category='Advertisement' AND link_to_event IS NOT NULL) SELECT ROUND(AVG((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance a WHERE a.link_to_event=ev.id)),2) AS avg_attendance FROM ev
answer: 12.53. 광고(Advertisement) 예산 항목이 있는 이벤트는 15건이고, 날짜 제한 없이 모두 포함했습니다. 이벤트별 참석 회원 수(attendance 행 수)를 구해 평균을 냈습니다. 한 이벤트에 광고 예산 항목이 여러 개여도 이벤트는 1번만 계산했습니다. 참석 기록이 없는 이벤트는 0명으로 포함했습니다. 현재 데이터에는 해당하는 이벤트가 없습니다.

sql:

WHERE p.player_name LIKE 'Aaron%' AND p.birthday >= '1991-01-01'
GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.player_name
ORDER BY p.player_name
answer: Six players match (birthday on or after 1991-01-01, name starting 'Aaron'). Starts in 2015/2016: Aaron Appindangoye 0, Aaron Doran 0, Aaron Kuhl 5, Aaron Lennox 1, Aaron Splaine 1, Aaron Taylor-Sinclair 0. A match counts if the player is in any of the 22 starting line-up slots (home or away), counted once per match. Players with no starts are kept with 0 because the question asks for every player; add HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT m.id) > 0 to drop them.

sql: SELECT p.ID FROM Patient p WHERE p.Admission='-' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.CPK<250) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID=p.ID AND l.RNP<>'negative' AND CAST(l.RNP AS REAL)>4) ORDER BY p.ID
answer:
9명이 조회되었습니다: 2320830, 3175008, 4013163, 4018722, 4398703, 4840422, 4915498, 5122312, 5400270.

적용한 기준은 다음과 같습니다. 외래 환자는 Admission이 '-'인 환자입니다. 'negative'인 RNP 결과는 항체가 검출되지 않은 것이므로 4 초과로 보지 않았습니다. 같은 검사일에 두 조건을 모두 만족해야 한다고 보지 않고, 기록 전체에서 CPK가 250 미만인 검사가 한 번 이상 있고 RNP가 4 초과인 검사도 한 번 이상 있으면 포함했습니다. 같은 검사 기록에서 두 조건을 모두 만족하는 환자만 세면 7명입니다.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(s.height_cm), 1) AS avg_height_cm FROM superhero s WHERE s.height_cm > 0 AND s.race_id = (SELECT race_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'A-Bomb')
answer: 181.2 cm. I read "A-Bomb's group" as the race column, which the docs describe as the character's "race or group", so the average covers every hero with A-Bomb's race, A-Bomb included. Heroes with a height of 0 or NULL are left out. The query ran as written and returned 181.2. It relies on the Superhero term, which is still a draft in the ontology and not certified.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM comments c JOIN posts p ON p.Id=c.PostId WHERE c.Score=0 AND c.PostId IN (SELECT PostId FROM comments GROUP BY PostId HAVING COUNT(*)=1)
answer: 10,999 comments. I counted rows in the comments table per post, not the posts.CommentCount field. I kept only posts that have exactly one comment row and that exist in posts. Of those, I counted the comments with Score = 0.

sql: SELECT s.City, SUM(COALESCE(f."NSLP Provision Status",'')='Provision 2') AS provision2_magnet_schools FROM schools s LEFT JOIN frpm f ON f.CDSCode=s.CDSCode WHERE s.Magnet=1 GROUP BY s.City ORDER BY provision2_magnet_schools DESC, s.City;
answer:
The query returns 155 cities, each with at least one magnet school (Magnet=1). Los Angeles has the most Provision 2 magnet schools at 48, then San Diego at 12 and Stockton at 8. Many cities show 0.

I used `schools.City`, the physical location city, rather than the mailing city. A school counts only if its `frpm."NSLP Provision Status"` is exactly 'Provision 2'. That excludes 'Multiple Provision Types', 'Breakfast Provision 2', 'Lunch Provision 2', 'CEP' and the other statuses. Cities with magnet schools but no Provision 2 schools are kept with a count of 0, because the question asks for every city with at least one magnet school.

City spellings are used as stored. The data has 'Montclair,' next to 'Montclair', and 'Pacomia' next to 'Pacoima'. I did not merge them.

sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE (',' || REPLACE(keywords, ', ', ',') || ',') LIKE '%,Flying,%' AND (',' || REPLACE(keywords, ', ', ',') || ',') LIKE '%,Cycling,%'
answer: 32 cards (counting each printing as its own row) have both Flying and Cycling as exact keywords. A plain substring match gives 45, but it also counts variants such as Islandcycling, Landcycling and Plainscycling. I read "Cycling" as the exact keyword and excluded those variants.

sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT f.language) AS foreign_languages FROM cards c JOIN foreign_data f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.name = 'Swamp'
answer: Swamp has been printed in 11 foreign languages: Chinese Simplified, Chinese Traditional, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Phyrexian, Portuguese (Brazil), Russian and Spanish. I matched only the card named exactly 'Swamp', so variants such as Snow-Covered Swamp are excluded. I counted every language in foreign_data, and that includes Phyrexian, which has a single printing. Without Phyrexian the count is 10. The Card and Card Foreign Data terms I used are still drafts and have not been certified.

sql:
WITH RECURSIVE ob AS (SELECT DISTINCT link_to_event ev FROM budget WHERE remaining < 0),
items(expense_id, item, rest) AS (SELECT x.expense_id, '', x.expense_description || ',' FROM expense x JOIN budget b ON x.link_to_budget=b.budget_id WHERE b.link_to_event IN (SELECT ev FROM ob) UNION ALL SELECT expense_id, trim(substr(rest,1,instr(rest,',')-1)), substr(rest,instr(rest,',')+1) FROM items WHERE rest<>'')
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT lower(item)) AS distinct_item_kinds FROM items WHERE item<>''
answer:
7 distinct kinds of items were bought for over-budget events. These are cookies, parking, pizza, posters, travel mug, water and chips.

How I read the question:
- An event is over budget if at least one of its budget lines has remaining < 0 (amount minus spent). This gives 5 events. The stored remaining column agrees with amount − spent on every budget line.
- I counted every expense of those events, not only the expenses in the over-budget category. I read "bought for events that went over budget" as the whole event.
- I split each comma-separated expense description into separate items.
- I treated "Cookies" and "cookies" as one item, so the count is 7. Matching case exactly would give 8.
- I applied no date filter. The event records span 2019-09-01 to 2020-05-05, which I took as the semester.
- The Budget, Event and Expense terms in the ontology are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT p.ID, p.SEX FROM Patient p WHERE (',' || replace(replace(replace(p.Diagnosis, char(29), ','), ', ', ','), '  ', ',') || ',' LIKE '%,SLE,%' OR p.Diagnosis LIKE 'SLE (diffuse%') AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.`T-BIL` >= 1.2) ORDER BY p.SEX, p.ID
answer: The query returns 14 patients (ID and sex). A patient counts if "SLE" is a confirmed entry in Patient.Diagnosis, which is the overall diagnosis rather than the one in Examination. I split the text on commas, double spaces and the control character used in values like "SLE^]SJS", then required an entry that is exactly "SLE". This keeps combinations such as "SLE, APS" and "SLE  SJS susp" and the single "SLE (diffuse LE)" value. It drops "SLE susp" and "SLE susp, SJS susp", where SLE is only suspected. A patient also needs at least one Laboratory row with T-BIL >= 1.2.

sql: SELECT s.School, s.Phone FROM schools s JOIN satscores t ON t.cds = s.CDSCode WHERE s.DOC = '03' AND t.rtype = 'S' AND t.NumGE1500 = (SELECT MAX(t2.NumGE1500) FROM schools s2 JOIN satscores t2 ON t2.cds = s2.CDSCode WHERE s2.DOC = '03' AND t2.rtype = 'S')
answer: High Tech High North County, phone (619) 243-5014. It had 56 SAT test takers scoring 1500 or above, the most among schools of the Statewide Benefit Charter type (DOC 03). The runner-up was High Tech High Chula Vista with 46, so there is no tie. I used school-level SAT rows only (rtype 'S'). The district-level row for the same network shows 102, but it has no school name and is not a single school.

sql:
WITH slots AS (
SELECT country_id, home_player_1 pid FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_2 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_3 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_4 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_5 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_6 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_7 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_8 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_9 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_10 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, home_player_11 FROM Match
UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_1 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_2 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_3 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_4 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_5 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_6 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_7 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_8 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_9 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_10 FROM Match UNION SELECT country_id, away_player_11 FROM Match),
cnt AS (SELECT c.id, c.name, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN p.weight <= 160 THEN p.player_api_id END) n
