For 1998, the pair with the largest total is bank AB, counter-account 44119823: 12 outgoing payments totalling 108,408. No other pair ties with it.

Choices I made:
- "Owner has a gold card" means a gold card issued on a disposition of type OWNER for that account.
- "Large district" means the branch district's inhabitants (A4) are at least 250,000.
- Only debit transactions (VYDAJ) dated 1 January to 31 December 1998 are counted.
- Debits with no recipient bank or counter-account are left out, because they can't form a pair. These are mostly cash or fee debits.

sql: SELECT s.block AS block, SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM set_translations t WHERE t.setCode = s.code AND t.translation IS NOT NULL) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS translated_sets, SUM(s.baseSetSize) AS total_base_set_size FROM sets s WHERE s.block IN ('Masques','Mirage') GROUP BY s.block ORDER BY s.block
answer: Masques has 2 sets with an official translated name and 640 base-set cards in total. Mirage has 1 translated set and 684 base-set cards. A set counts as translated if it has at least one set_translations row with a non-null translation. Base set size is the sum of sets.baseSetSize. The Card Set and Set Translation terms are still drafts, not certified.

sql: SELECT p.ID, p.Diagnosis, l.DNA FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID=p.ID WHERE p.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' AND p.Diagnosis NOT LIKE '%SLE susp%' AND l.DNA IS NOT NULL AND CAST(l.DNA AS REAL)=(SELECT MAX(CAST(l2.DNA AS REAL)) FROM Patient p2 JOIN Laboratory l2 ON l2.ID=p2.ID WHERE p2.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' AND p2.Diagnosis NOT LIKE '%SLE susp%' AND l2.DNA IS NOT NULL)
answer: 환자 2933261 (진단: SLE)의 항 DNA 검사 결과가 185로 가장 높았고, 동점 환자는 없었습니다. 판단 기준 두 가지를 적용했습니다. 진단에 'SLE'가 들어 있어도 'SLE susp'(의심)인 환자는 확진이 아니므로 제외했고, DNA 컬럼이 텍스트라서 숫자로 변환해 비교한 뒤 원래 표기(185)를 그대로 출력했습니다. 의심 환자까지 포함해 봐도 1위는 같은 환자(185)입니다.

sql: SELECT c.name, c.number, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM foreign_data f WHERE f.uuid = c.uuid) AS foreign_printings FROM cards c WHERE c.watermark = 'abzan' AND CAST(c.number AS INTEGER) = (SELECT MAX(CAST(number AS INTEGER)) FROM cards WHERE watermark = 'abzan') ORDER BY c.name
answer:
Abzan Beastmaster, collector number 55888 (set PRM), with 0 foreign-language printings. There is no tie.

Two readings I chose:
- Collector numbers are stored as text, some with suffixes like "200s". I compared them as integers, so 55888 is the highest. A plain text sort would rank "9s" above it.
- I counted foreign_data rows for this specific printing (the PRM card with number 55888), and it has none. The same card name also has a Fate Reforged printing (number 119) with 10 foreign-language rows. If you meant the card across all of its printings, the count would be 10.

sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM member mm WHERE mm.link_to_major = m.major_id) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS pct_majors_without_members FROM major AS m
answer: 76.99% of majors have no club member. The denominator is every major in the `major` table (113 rows), including majors with no members. A major counts as reached if any row in `member` links to it, whatever the member's position, including "Inactive". The `Major` term is still a draft in the ontology, and I skipped `validate_sql` and went straight to `run_sql`.

sql: select m.department as department_name, count(distinct m.major_id) as majors_offered, count(distinct case when mem.member_id is not null then m.major_id end) as majors_held, round(1.0*count(mem.member_id)/count(distinct m.major_id),2) as avg_members_per_major from major m left join member mem on mem.link_to_major=m.major_id where m.department in (select department from major where college='College of Humanities and Social Sciences') group by m.department order by m.department
answer:
The query returns 11 departments in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences. Each row has the department name, the number of majors it offers, the number of those majors held by at least one member, and members per offered major rounded to two decimals. I read "the majors it offers" and "the majors held" as counts. No department has majors in more than one college, so the "any of its majors" rule changes nothing here.

Only 3 departments have members:
- Languages, Philosophy and Communication Studies: 8 majors offered, 3 held, 0.38 members per major.
- Political Science: 3 offered, 2 held, 1.0.
- Liberal Arts Program: 1 offered, 1 held, 1.0.

The other 8 departments have no members: Aerospace Studies, Asian Studies, English, History, Journalism and Communication, Military Science, Religious Studies, and Sociology, Social Work and Anthropology.

The average divides all members in a department's majors by the number of majors it offers, including majors nobody holds. Members with no major (one member has a NULL major link) are left out.

sql: WITH f AS (SELECT u.Location, (SELECT MIN(p.CreaionDate) FROM posts p WHERE p.OwnerUserId = u.Id) AS first_post FROM users u) SELECT COUNT(*) AS user_count FROM f WHERE first_post >= '2010-01-01' AND first_post < '2011-01-01' AND ' ' || REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE(LOWER(Location), ',', ' '), '.', ' '), '(', ' '), ')', ' '), '[', ' ') || ' ' LIKE '% india %'
answer: 12 users whose first post was created in calendar year 2010 are located in India. I took a user's first post to be their earliest post by creation date, among users who own at least one post. I counted a location as India only when 'India' appears as a whole word, ignoring case, so "Indiana" and "Indianapolis" are excluded. Matching on the word also catches variants such as "Delhi,  India" and "India, Pune". A looser substring match gives the same 12 for 2010.

sql: WITH oc AS (SELECT DISTINCT d.client_id, d.account_id FROM disp d JOIN card c ON c.disp_id = d.disp_id WHERE d.type = 'OWNER' AND c.type = 'classic'), cl AS (SELECT a.district_id, COUNT(DISTINCT oc.client_id) AS n_clients FROM oc JOIN account a ON a.account_id = oc.account_id GROUP BY a.district_id), pay AS (SELECT a.district_id, COUNT(DISTINCT t.bank || '|' || t.account) AS n_ext, SUM(t.amount) AS total FROM (SELECT DISTINCT account_id FROM oc) x JOIN account a ON a.account_id = x.account_id JOIN trans t ON t.account_id = x.account_id WHERE t.type = 'VYDAJ' AND t.bank IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(t.bank) <> '' AND t.account IS NOT NULL AND t.account > 0 GROUP BY a.district_id) SELECT di.A2 AS district_name, COALESCE(cl.n_clients, 0) AS client_count, COALESCE(pay.n_ext, 0) AS external_account_count, COALESCE(pay.total, 0) AS total_amount FROM district di LEFT JOIN cl ON cl.district_id = di.district_id LEFT JOIN pay ON pay.district_id = di.district_id ORDER BY total_amount DESC, di.A2
answer:
The query returns one row for each of the 77 districts, with district name, client count, external account count and total amount, in that order. I ran it and checked the first 10 rows. I did not look at the rest, including the districts that should show zeros.

Hl.m. Praha is first with 96 clients, 123 external accounts and 14,125,240 paid out. Olomouc is second with 11 clients, 16 external accounts and 3,235,882.

Readings I chose:
- **Clients:** a client counts if they have the OWNER disposition on an account and that disposition has a classic card. Each client is counted once, in the district of the branch holding that account (account.district_id).
- **Payments:** outgoing payments are transactions with type 'VYDAJ' on those owned accounts. The query leaves out cash withdrawals ('VYBER'), because the question says payments to other banks.
- **External accounts:** these are distinct (bank, account) pairs on those payments. A payment counts only if it has a partner bank code and a partner account number above 0. Rows without a counterparty add nothing to the account count or the total.
- **Totals:** unrounded, over the whole history. They are sorted from highest to lowest, with ties broken by district name.

The terms the query relies on (Account, Credit Card, Disposition, District, Transaction) are draft in the ontology, not certified. The validator also warned that the join between trans and disp is not a known relationship. The query does not join them directly. It joins trans to account.

SELECT season, COUNT(DISTINCT pid) AS player_count FROM (
SELECT season, away_player_1 AS pid FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_2 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_3 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_4 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_5 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_6 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_7 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_8 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_9 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_10 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5
UNION ALL SELECT season, away_player_11 FROM Match WHERE home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5
) GROUP BY season ORDER BY season
answer: One row per season (8 seasons, 2008/2009 to 2015/2016) with the number of distinct players in the away starting eleven (away_player_1..11) in matches the away side lost by 5+ goals (home_team_goal - away_team_goal >= 5). Counts: 2008/2009 242, 2009/2010 320, 2010/2011 465, 2011/2012 525, 2012/2013 420, 2013/2014 354, 2014/2015 525, 2015/2016 462. Assumptions: "lineup" means the 11 starter columns; NULL slots are ignored; each player is counted once per season. The Match term is still a draft in the ontology.
